title: [Phase 1] TrustLevel enum — shared kernel consolidation
description:
## Goal / Problem

Consolidate TrustLevel from internal/research/domain/research.go into the shared kernel so both Discovery and Research contexts can use it. Currently TrustLevel exists only in the Research bounded context as an int enum. The Domain Storytelling redesign requires TrustLevel on every domain element (actors, work objects, sentences, annotations, glossary terms, boundary signals). It must live in the shared kernel.

## Background / Context

- **Spike source:** alty-cli-1i3 (format validation), alty-cli-dh8 (domain research quality)
- **Architecture ref:** docs/ARCHITECTURE.md — Section 3 Source Layout (shared/domain/valueobjects/trust_level.go)
- **DDD ref:** docs/DDD.md — Section 2 Ubiquitous Language: TrustLevel definition
- **Existing code:** internal/research/domain/research.go:15-23 (current TrustLevel)
- **Pattern reference:** internal/shared/domain/valueobjects/domain_values.go (existing shared kernel VOs)

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Shared Kernel |
| Ubiquitous Language | TrustLevel, UserStated, UserConfirmed, AIResearched, AIInferred |
| Layer | Domain |

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| **S**ingle Responsibility | TrustLevel only handles trust provenance semantics |
| **O**pen/Closed | New trust levels (if ever needed) added to enum, no existing code changes |
| **L**iskov Substitution | N/A (value object, not interface) |
| **I**nterface Segregation | No interface needed — pure value object |
| **D**ependency Inversion | Domain layer, zero dependencies |

## TDD Workflow

### RED Phase

Write failing tests first:

\`\`\`go
// internal/shared/domain/valueobjects/trust_level_test.go
TestNewTrustLevel_ValidValues: Each of 4 enum values constructs successfully
TestNewTrustLevel_InvalidValue: Returns error for unknown value
TestTrustLevel_String: Each value returns correct lowercase string
TestTrustLevel_IsHigherTrust: UserStated > UserConfirmed > AIResearched > AIInferred
TestTrustLevel_IsHigherTrust_Equal: Same level returns false
TestTrustLevel_Validate: Valid values pass, invalid fails
TestTrustLevel_TextRoundTrip: MarshalText to string, UnmarshalText back, equals original
TestTrustLevel_UnmarshalText_InvalidString: Returns error for unknown string
TestTrustLevel_UnmarshalText_EmptyString: Returns error for empty input
\`\`\`

Run: go test ./internal/shared/domain/valueobjects/... → should FAIL

### GREEN Phase

1. Create internal/shared/domain/valueobjects/trust_level.go
2. Define TrustLevel type with 4 constants (UserStated, UserConfirmed, AIResearched, AIInferred)
3. Implement: NewTrustLevel, String, Validate, IsHigherTrust, ParseTrustLevel, MarshalText, UnmarshalText
4. Update internal/research/domain/research.go: type alias + constant re-export (see Design > Migration Path)

Run: go test ./internal/shared/domain/valueobjects/... → should PASS
Run: go test ./internal/research/... → should still PASS (zero test modifications)

### REFACTOR Phase

- Verify naming matches docs/DDD.md glossary (TrustLevel, not TrustScore)
- Ensure zero external dependencies in shared/domain/
- Run all quality gates

## Steps

1. Write test file internal/shared/domain/valueobjects/trust_level_test.go with all test cases
2. Create internal/shared/domain/valueobjects/trust_level.go with TrustLevel enum, constructor, methods
3. Update internal/research/domain/research.go: replace TrustLevel definition with type alias + constant re-export from shared kernel
4. Verify existing research tests pass without modification
5. Run quality gates

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] TrustLevel enum with 4 values: UserStated, UserConfirmed, AIResearched, AIInferred
- [ ] String() returns lowercase_snake: "user_stated", "user_confirmed", "ai_researched", "ai_inferred"
- [ ] IsHigherTrust() implements ordering: UserStated > UserConfirmed > AIResearched > AIInferred
- [ ] MarshalText/UnmarshalText round-trips correctly (encoding.TextMarshaler, NOT yaml.Marshaler)
- [ ] Research domain re-exports TrustUserStated etc. via type alias + constants (see Design > Migration Path)
- [ ] Existing research domain tests pass without ANY modification
- [ ] Zero external dependencies in shared/domain/valueobjects/trust_level.go
- [ ] All quality gates pass (go build, go vet, golangci-lint, go test -race)

## Edge Cases

| Case | Input | Expected Output |
|------|-------|-----------------|
| Invalid int value | TrustLevel(99) | Validate() returns error |
| Invalid text string | "unknown_trust" | UnmarshalText returns error |
| Empty text string | "" | UnmarshalText returns error |
| Equal comparison | UserStated.IsHigherTrust(UserStated) | false (not strictly higher) |
| Lowest vs highest | AIInferred.IsHigherTrust(UserStated) | false |
| Highest vs lowest | UserStated.IsHigherTrust(AIInferred) | true |

## Quality Gates

\`\`\`bash
go build ./...
go vet ./...
golangci-lint run ./...
go test ./internal/shared/domain/valueobjects/... -race -cover
go test ./internal/research/... -race
\`\`\`

- [ ] Lint passes
- [ ] All tests pass with >= 90% coverage (Core subdomain)
- [ ] Edge cases have test coverage
- [ ] Research domain tests unchanged and passing

## Pre-Implementation Validation (VERIFIED 2026-03-24)

- [x] shared/domain/valueobjects/ directory exists (17 files found)
- [x] research/domain/research.go TrustLevel is an int enum (verified: lines 15-23, 4 constants 1-4)
- [x] TrustLevel only referenced in research/domain/ + throwaway prototypes (grep confirmed)
- [x] No circular dependency risk (shared kernel → nothing; research → shared is allowed)
- [x] No existing TextMarshaler/TextUnmarshaler in shared kernel (grep confirmed — T1 is first to set pattern)
- [x] YAML library not needed in domain layer — encoding.TextMarshaler is stdlib, yaml.v3 auto-detects it

## QA Before Close

- [ ] Happy path: all 4 trust levels construct, compare, serialize correctly
- [ ] Edge cases: invalid values, empty strings, boundary comparisons
- [ ] Error handling: clear error messages for invalid inputs
- [ ] No regressions: research domain tests pass (zero modifications)
- [ ] Domain layer has no external dependencies

## Risks / Dependencies

- No blocking dependencies — this is the foundation ticket

## YAML Serialization Pattern (SETTLED — T1 sets the pattern for T2-T9)

This ticket establishes the YAML serialization approach for ALL Domain Storytelling VOs. The decision made here is binding for StoryActor, WorkObject, StorySentence, Annotation, BoundarySignal, BoundedContextSketch, UbiquitousLanguageEntry, and ConversationTurn.

**Decision:** Use \`encoding.TextMarshaler\` / \`encoding.TextUnmarshaler\` for enum types in the domain layer. Do NOT import \`gopkg.in/yaml.v3\` in domain layer — that would leak infrastructure into domain.

**Why:** The yaml.v3 library's \`yaml.Marshaler\` interface lives in an infrastructure package. Domain VOs must have zero external dependencies. Go's stdlib \`encoding.TextMarshaler\` is sufficient — yaml.v3 automatically uses TextMarshaler/TextUnmarshaler when present.

**Pattern to implement:**
\`\`\`go
// In domain layer (zero external deps):
func (t TrustLevel) MarshalText() ([]byte, error) {
    return []byte(t.String()), nil
}

func (t *TrustLevel) UnmarshalText(data []byte) error {
    parsed, err := ParseTrustLevel(string(data))
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    *t = parsed
    return nil
}
\`\`\`

**Subsequent tickets (T2-T9) must follow this exact pattern.** Reference this ticket's implementation, not re-debate the approach.

## Grooming Notes (2026-03-24)

Issues found and fixed during grooming:
1. **MarshalYAML → MarshalText**: Methods section listed yaml.Marshaler methods which would require importing yaml.v3 in domain. Fixed to encoding.TextMarshaler.
2. **Removed Equals()**: Not idiomatic Go for int-based types. == operator works directly.
3. **Test names fixed**: YAMLRoundTrip → TextRoundTrip, UnmarshalYAML → UnmarshalText. Full YAML round-trip belongs in T10 (infrastructure).
4. **Migration path settled**: Type alias + constant re-export. Only approach that preserves existing research test compatibility.
design:
### Data Models

| Model | Type | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| TrustLevel | Value Object (enum) | Provenance indicator: UserStated > UserConfirmed > AIResearched > AIInferred |

### Methods

- NewTrustLevel(value) — constructor with validation
- String() string — human-readable name
- Validate() error — ensures value is in valid range
- IsHigherTrust(other TrustLevel) bool — comparison (UserStated > UserConfirmed > AIResearched > AIInferred)
- MarshalText() ([]byte, error) — encoding.TextMarshaler for YAML/JSON serialization (zero external deps)
- UnmarshalText([]byte) error — encoding.TextUnmarshaler for deserialization
- ParseTrustLevel(string) (TrustLevel, error) — parse from lowercase string

### Naming Convention

Shared kernel constants drop the Trust prefix (redundant with type name):
- valueobjects.UserStated, valueobjects.UserConfirmed, valueobjects.AIResearched, valueobjects.AIInferred

Research domain re-exports preserve existing names for backward compat:
- domain.TrustUserStated = valueobjects.UserStated (etc.)

### Migration Path (SETTLED)

Use type alias + constant re-export in research domain. This is the ONLY approach that preserves existing test compatibility without modification:

\`\`\`go
// internal/research/domain/research.go
import "github.com/alto-cli/alto/internal/shared/domain/valueobjects"

type TrustLevel = valueobjects.TrustLevel  // type alias, not new type

const (
    TrustUserStated    = valueobjects.UserStated
    TrustUserConfirmed = valueobjects.UserConfirmed
    TrustAIResearched  = valueobjects.AIResearched
    TrustAIInferred    = valueobjects.AIInferred
)

func AllTrustLevels() []TrustLevel { return valueobjects.AllTrustLevels() }
\`\`\`

Why type alias (not new type): existing tests assert int values and use assert.Less on domain.TrustLevel directly. A new type would break type identity.
close_reason: Implemented: shared kernel TrustLevel VO with TextMarshaler pattern, research domain migrated via type alias, 100% coverage, all gates pass. Commit 6115fc7.

title: Spike: AI domain research quality across known-to-obscure domains
description:
## Type: Spike

## Risk Being De-risked

AI story proposals may be low quality for obscure domains. The domain research phase (web search to bootstrap domain knowledge) is the primary mitigation, but we have not tested whether web search produces usable domain knowledge for niche domains, or whether that knowledge translates into refinable story proposals.

## Research Questions

1. For well-known domains, does web search produce enough knowledge to propose reasonable stories?
2. For obscure domains, does web search produce anything useful?
3. What search queries work best? Test patterns:
   - "[domain] workflow"
   - "[domain] software features"
   - "[domain] business process"
   - "[domain] management system"
   - "[domain] industry practices"
4. How should research results be structured for the moderator to consume? (structured knowledge base format)
5. What is the quality floor? When should alto say "I could not find enough, let us start from your description instead"?
6. How long does domain research take? Is 2-3 minutes acceptable?
7. Can the research output produce a refinable story? (Not just "is the research good" but "can a user correct the proposed story into something accurate?")
8. What about domains where the user has PARTIAL knowledge? (Most common real case — user knows some but not all)

## Key Decision This Spike Must Produce

**Decision 1: Domain research viable for MVP?**
- A) Yes — viable across the spectrum, include in Phase 4
- B) Partially — viable for well-known/moderate domains only, include with quality floor gate
- C) No — defer to future work, focus on user-narrates flow instead

**Decision 2: Research output format**
- What structure does the AI domain expert agent need?
- Fields: actors, workflows, entities, regulatory requirements, existing software, typical interactions
- How does this feed into story proposal?

**Decision 3: Quality floor threshold**
- Concrete criteria for "insufficient research" (e.g., fewer than 3 actors identified, no workflow found)
- Fallback behavior when floor not met

## Approach

Test web research for 5 domains across a spectrum of obscurity. Use WebSearch (the same tool alto would use in production).

| Domain | Obscurity | Expected Result |
|--------|-----------|----------------|
| E-commerce order fulfillment | Very well-known | Baseline — should work perfectly |
| Veterinary clinic management | Moderately known | Good test — some software exists |
| Municipal water treatment operations | Niche industrial | Specialized but documented |
| Artisan cheese aging and inventory | Small niche | Limited software coverage |
| Competitive sheep dog trial scoring | Very obscure | Minimal coverage |

For each domain:
1. Run 3-5 web searches using the query patterns above
2. Extract structured knowledge: actors, workflows, entities, regulations, existing software
3. Measure: time taken, number of useful sources, coverage of domain aspects
4. Propose an initial 3-story set from research alone (primary, failure, secondary)
5. Rate each story: Could a domain-knowledgeable user refine this into something accurate?
   - Usable: user could say "yes, roughly right" and make 2-3 corrections
   - Partially usable: user would need to rewrite 50%+ but the actors/objects are a good start
   - Insufficient: user would be better off starting from scratch

Also test the PARTIAL knowledge case:
6. For vet clinic: pretend user says "I know the appointment flow but not billing" — can research fill in the billing side while preserving user's stated knowledge?

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] 5 domains tested across known-to-obscure spectrum
- [ ] Structured knowledge extracted for each domain (actors, workflows, entities, regulations, software)
- [ ] 3-story set proposed for each domain from research alone
- [ ] Story quality rated: usable / partially usable / insufficient with concrete reasoning
- [ ] Optimal search query patterns identified (which patterns produce best results)
- [ ] Partial knowledge case tested (user knows some, research fills gaps)
- [ ] Timing measured per domain (search time + extraction time)
- [ ] Decision 1: domain research viable for MVP?
- [ ] Decision 2: research output format defined
- [ ] Decision 3: quality floor threshold with concrete criteria
- [ ] Findings documented in docs/research/

## Output

- Research data for 5 domains (searches, extractions, proposed stories) in docs/research/samples/
- Research report: docs/research/YYYYMMDD_ai_domain_research_quality.md
- Decision 1: MVP viability
- Decision 2: research output format specification
- Decision 3: quality floor threshold and fallback behavior
- Recommended search query templates
notes: Decision 1: A) Yes -- viable across the spectrum, include in Phase 4. All 5 domains scored Usable (3/3) across known-to-obscure spectrum. Decision 2: DomainResearchResult struct with actors, entities, workflows, failure modes, regulatory items, existing software, quality score, and trust levels per element. Decision 3: Quality floor = >=3 actors, >=3 entities, >=5 workflow steps, >=5 sources, >=2 queries returning results. Fallback: honest disclosure + switch to user-driven mode.
close_reason: All 3 decisions made. Decision 1: A) Yes, domain research viable across full obscurity spectrum for MVP Phase 4. All 5 domains (e-commerce, vet clinic, water treatment, cheese aging, sheepdog trials) scored Usable 3/3. Average search time 17s. Decision 2: DomainResearchResult schema defined with actors, entities, workflows, failure modes, regulatory, software, trust levels, and quality score. Decision 3: Quality floor = >=3 actors, >=3 entities, >=5 workflow steps, >=5 sources. Fallback: disclose limitation and switch to user-driven narration.

title: Spike: .story.yaml format and export validation
description:
## Type: Spike

## Risk Being De-risked

The .story.yaml format may need iteration as we learn what downstream consumers actually need. Defining the format without validating against export targets and downstream consumers risks rework.

## Shared Sample Domains

Uses the same 3 domains as all storytelling spikes. Writes the canonical sample stories that other spikes can reuse.

## Scope (Focused)

This spike validates the FORMAT only. It does NOT build export adapters or migration code. Deliverables:
1. Finalized .story.yaml schema
2. Finalized glossary.yaml and context-map.yaml schemas
3. Hand-written samples for 3 domains
4. Paper validation against 4 consumers (PlantUML, Egon, DDD.md generation, ticket pipeline)
5. v1 session format analysis (read existing code, document what needs migrating)

Export adapters and migration code are implementation tasks in the epic, NOT spike work.

## Research Questions

1. Does the proposed .story.yaml format (from research report Section 9.1) capture everything needed?
   - Can it represent all DST elements: actors (with types), work objects (with types), sentences, annotations (constraints + invariants), variations, trust levels?
   - Can it represent both coarse-grained and fine-grained stories?
   - Is it readable by humans in a terminal (not just machine-parseable)?
2. Can the format export to PlantUML DomainStory-PlantUML syntax? (paper validation: write the PlantUML by hand from the YAML, check nothing is lost)
3. Can the format export to Egon .egn JSON? (paper validation: write the JSON by hand, check Egon schema compatibility)
4. Does the format capture enough for DDD.md generation? (paper exercise: extract glossary, context map, invariants from the YAML)
5. Does the format capture enough for ticket pipeline? (paper exercise: derive epics and tasks from the YAML)
6. Is YAML the right serialization? Evaluate:
   - YAML: human-readable, standard, but whitespace-sensitive
   - JSON: machine-friendly, but less readable for domain experts reviewing in terminal
   - TOML: good for config, awkward for nested structures like sentences
   - Custom DSL: most readable, but parser cost
7. What does the existing v1 session format (discovery_session.json) look like? What fields need migrating?

## Key Decision This Spike Must Produce

**Decision 1: .story.yaml format finalized**
- Schema locked (fields, types, nesting)
- Trust level representation confirmed
- Annotation types enumerated (constraint, invariant, assumption, variation_pointer)

**Decision 2: Serialization format**
- YAML confirmed, or alternative chosen with rationale

**Decision 3: Companion formats**
- glossary.yaml schema finalized
- context-map.yaml schema finalized

**Decision 4: v1 migration feasibility**
- Can v1 Q/A sessions produce useful v2 stories? Or is migration lossy?
- If lossy: should v1 sessions just be archived, not migrated?

## Approach

1. Read existing FileSystemSessionRepository code (filesystem_session_repository.go) to understand v1 format
2. Write 3 sample .story.yaml files by hand for the shared domains
3. Write 1 sample glossary.yaml by hand
4. Write 1 sample context-map.yaml by hand
5. For each sample, do paper validation:
   - Write equivalent PlantUML by hand -> check nothing lost from YAML
   - Write equivalent Egon .egn JSON by hand -> check Egon schema documented at egon.io
   - Extract glossary entries from stories -> check coverage
   - Derive epic/task structure from stories -> check viability
6. Test readability: print YAML in terminal, assess scanability for 10+ sentence stories
7. Analyze v1 format: what fields exist, what maps to v2, what is lost

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] 3 sample .story.yaml files written (e-commerce, vet clinic, alto)
- [ ] 1 sample glossary.yaml written
- [ ] 1 sample context-map.yaml written
- [ ] Paper validation: PlantUML export feasible (hand-written example, no lossy fields)
- [ ] Paper validation: Egon .egn export feasible (hand-written JSON, schema-compatible)

title: Spike: Boundary detection heuristics validation
description:
## Type: Spike

## Risk Being De-risked

Boundary detection heuristics (one-way flow, language differences, different triggers, org boundaries) may produce false positives or miss real boundaries. We need to validate accuracy against known domains AND prototype the detection algorithm before building the engine.

## Shared Sample Domains

Uses the same 3 domains as all storytelling spikes:
1. **E-commerce** (known contexts: Catalog, Cart, Order, Payment, Shipping)
2. **Veterinary clinic** (known contexts: Scheduling, Clinical, Billing, Inventory)
3. **alto itself** (known contexts: Bootstrap, Discovery, Ticket Pipeline, Knowledge, etc.)

Uses sample stories produced by alty-cli-gox, or writes its own if gox has not completed yet.

## Research Questions

1. Do the 4 boundary signals reliably identify bounded contexts from text-based stories?
   - One-way information flow
   - Language differences (same term, different meaning)
   - Different triggers (time-based vs event-based)
   - Organizational boundaries
2. Does the "same work object, different context" signal work? (Section 5.2 of methodology report: e.g., "Customer" in Sales has name/email; "Customer" in Billing has account/payment method)
3. What is the false positive rate? What triggers false signals?
4. What is the false negative rate? What real boundaries do the heuristics miss?
5. How many stories are needed before detection becomes reliable? (Is 3 enough for RAPID mode?)
6. How should confidence scores be calibrated?
7. What happens when NO signals fire? (Domain is small enough for one context — is that a valid outcome?)

## Key Decision This Spike Must Produce

**Decision 1: Are 3 coarse-grained stories sufficient for RAPID mode boundary detection?**
- If yes: RAPID mode can propose bounded contexts
- If no: RAPID mode proposes a flat domain model, boundary detection requires THOROUGH mode

**Decision 2: Can the heuristics be automated from text-based stories?**
- A) Yes — algorithmic detection is feasible (string matching on work object names, activity flow direction analysis)
- B) Partially — some signals (language differences) need LLM/NLP, others (flow direction) are algorithmic
- C) No — all signals require human or LLM judgment

**Decision 3: Confidence thresholds**
- What score = "propose to user" (high confidence)
- What score = "suggest with caveat" (medium)
- What score = "too uncertain, ask user" (low)

## Approach

For each of the 3 domains:
1. Write 3 coarse-grained stories in alto text format (or reuse from alty-cli-gox)
2. Apply each heuristic BOTH manually AND algorithmically:
   - Manual: read stories, identify signals by human judgment
   - Algorithmic: write a simple Go script that scans for: repeated work object names across stories, directional activity patterns, different verbs for same objects
3. Compare manual vs algorithmic detection results
4. Compare detected contexts to known-correct bounded contexts
5. Calculate precision (% of detected boundaries that are real) and recall (% of real boundaries detected)

Also test edge cases:
- Domain with only 1 bounded context (is that detected correctly as "no split needed"?)
- Domain with ambiguous boundaries (where reasonable people disagree)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] 3 domains tested with all 4 heuristic types + "same work object, different context" signal
- [ ] Both manual AND algorithmic detection tested for each domain
- [ ] Precision and recall calculated per heuristic type and per domain
- [ ] Decision 1 documented: 3 stories sufficient for RAPID mode?
- [ ] Decision 2 documented: algorithmic feasibility per signal type
- [ ] Decision 3 documented: confidence thresholds with calibration data
- [ ] Edge cases tested: single-context domain, ambiguous boundaries
- [ ] False positive patterns identified with concrete examples
- [ ] Findings documented in docs/research/

## Output

- Boundary detection test data (stories + known contexts + detected contexts) in docs/research/samples/
- Simple Go detection script (throwaway, informs engine design)
- Research report: docs/research/YYYYMMDD_boundary_detection_heuristics_validation.md
- Decision 1: story count for RAPID mode
- Decision 2: algorithmic feasibility per signal
- Decision 3: confidence thresholds
notes: Decision 1: YES, 3 coarse-grained stories are sufficient for RAPID mode (manual precision 0.87, recall 0.85). Must present as proposed boundaries, not definitive. Decision 2: 2/5 signals are reliably algorithmic (same-object-diff-context precision 0.85, org-boundary precision 0.67); 3/5 require LLM (language differences, trigger classification, actor overloading). Decision 3: HIGH >= 0.65 or 2+ signal types (100% accuracy), MEDIUM 0.45-0.64 with 1 type (58% accuracy), LOW < 0.45 (do not propose).
close_reason: All 3 decisions resolved with data. (1) 3 stories sufficient for RAPID mode - manual P/R 0.87/0.85, must present as proposed boundaries. (2) Hybrid detection required: same-object-diff-context + org-boundary are algorithmically reliable (P 0.85/0.67); language-diff + trigger-classification + actor-overloading need LLM. (3) Confidence thresholds calibrated: HIGH >= 0.65 or 2+ signal types (100% accuracy), MEDIUM 0.45-0.64 (58%), LOW < 0.45 (suppress). Edge cases validated: TODO app correctly gets no-split, ambiguous recipe domain correctly flagged as uncertain. Research report with full precision/recall tables in docs/research/20260323_boundary_detection_heuristics_validation.md

title: Spike: CLI-based Domain Storytelling moderator prototype
description:
## Type: Spike

## Risk Being De-risked

Domain Storytelling in CLI is unprecedented. No prior art exists for text-only, AI-moderated DST. We need to validate that the moderator conversation works in a terminal before building the full domain model.

## Shared Sample Domains

All storytelling spikes use the same 3 domains for consistency:
1. **E-commerce** (well-known: Catalog, Cart, Order, Payment, Shipping)
2. **Veterinary clinic** (moderately known: Scheduling, Clinical, Billing, Inventory)
3. **alto itself** (we know it: Bootstrap, Discovery, Ticket Pipeline, Knowledge)

## Research Questions

1. Can the DST moderator flow (propose story -> user refines sentence by sentence -> synthesis) work in a terminal without visuals?
2. What does the consultant interaction pattern feel like? Test BOTH approaches:
   a. AI proposes full story, user corrects sentences (consultant-proposes)
   b. AI asks "what happens first?", user narrates, AI structures (user-narrates)
   c. Which feels more natural? Or is a hybrid best?
3. How does the user CORRECT a proposed story? Test: reject a sentence, add a missing actor, reorder activities, split a story when branching detected.
4. How does the synthesis checkpoint feel? Is phase-based synthesis better than every-3-answers playback?
5. What is the minimum viable Prompter interface for the consultant pattern?
6. Does the mode selection UX (RAPID/THOROUGH/EXISTING) make sense as the first interaction?

## Key Decision This Spike Must Produce

**Decision 1: Primary interaction pattern**
- A) Consultant-proposes: AI generates story, user refines (like gstack design-consultation)
- B) User-narrates: AI moderates with questions, user tells the story (traditional DST workshop)
- C) Hybrid: AI proposes first story from README, user narrates subsequent stories

**Decision 2: Story proposal mechanism for MVP**
- A) Template matching from README nouns/verbs (no LLM, no external dependency)
- B) User-driven only (AI asks "tell me the primary workflow", user types it, AI structures into sentences)
- C) LLM required from day 1 (template matching produces unusable output)

Note: Option B means no AI story proposal at all -- the user provides all domain knowledge. This is a valid MVP if template matching fails, because gstack's CEO review handles the "scope challenge" upstream.

## Approach

Build a throwaway prototype (standalone Go main in /tmp or docs/research/prototype/, not wired into alto) that:
1. Reads one of the 3 sample READMEs
2. Tests both interaction patterns (consultant-proposes AND user-narrates)
3. Walks user through refining/narrating a story sentence by sentence
4. Records structured StorySentence objects
5. Tests correction flows: reject sentence, add actor, reorder, split story
6. Plays back a phase synthesis
7. Tests mode selection as first interaction

Test with a real human (you, the user) on at least one domain to get subjective feedback.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Prototype runs in terminal with all 3 sample domains
- [ ] Both interaction patterns tested: consultant-proposes AND user-narrates
- [ ] Story correction flow works: reject, add, reorder, split
- [ ] Synthesis checkpoint tested: phase-based vs every-N-answers
- [ ] Decision 1 documented: which interaction pattern (or hybrid)
- [ ] Decision 2 documented: story proposal mechanism for MVP
- [ ] Minimum Prompter interface documented (method signatures for consultant flow)
- [ ] Findings documented in docs/research/

## Output

- Prototype code (throwaway, not merged)
- Sample stories for the 3 shared domains (reused by other spikes)
- Research report: docs/research/YYYYMMDD_cli_domain_storytelling_prototype.md
- Decision 1: interaction pattern
- Decision 2: story proposal mechanism
- Recommended Prompter interface (method signatures)
notes: Decision 1: C) Hybrid — consultant-proposes first story (requires LLM), user-narrates subsequent. For MVP, user-narrates only. Decision 2: B) User-driven only — template matching from README fails catastrophically (found 1/5 actors, 0 work objects, generated nonsensical sentences). LLM required for consultant-proposes but not for MVP. Decision 3: StorytellingPrompter with 8 methods (SelectMode, ProposeStory, AskNarration, ConfirmSentence, AskChoice, DisplayStory, SynthesisCheckpoint, AskAnnotation) replacing current 4-method Prompter.
close_reason: All 3 decisions validated with prototype evidence. Decision 1: Hybrid (consultant-proposes + user-narrates), with user-narrates as MVP. Decision 2: User-driven only for MVP — template matching fails catastrophically on all 3 domains, LLM needed for consultant-proposes (Phase 2). Decision 3: New 8-method StorytellingPrompter interface defined. Additional findings: branching detection is high-value, two-tier synthesis (per-sentence + phase) is correct model, mode selection works as first interaction. Prototype code in docs/research/prototype/cli-dst/, sample stories in docs/research/samples/, report in docs/research/20260323_cli_domain_storytelling_prototype.md.

title: Spike: gstack UX patterns + Domain Storytelling for alto discovery redesign
description:
## Type: Spike

## Thesis

**gstack owns "what to build" (scope, product vision, ambition). alto owns "how to structure it" (DDD, bounded contexts, tickets).**

The pipeline: User idea -> gstack /plan-ceo-review (scope challenge) -> alto discovery (Domain Storytelling, DDD artifacts) -> alto ticket pipeline (beads epics and tasks).

This spike investigates how to make alto's half of that pipeline actually good -- because right now our 10-question flow is too rigid to deliver on the README promise that "20 minutes of questions saves you 20 hours of rewrites."

## Context

alto's current discovery flow works but fails users in two ways:

1. **Rigid interaction** -- 10 fixed questions in strict phase order, no branching, no adaptation, no recommendations. It is a form wizard, not a consultant. gstack's skill system demonstrates a fundamentally better interaction pattern.

2. **Assumes domain expertise** -- Questions like "What are the core entities in your domain?" and "What domain events are published when state changes occur?" presume the user already has answers. Many users arrive with a vague idea and no domain knowledge. Full Event Storming is too heavy for this. Domain Storytelling is the right weight.

## Scope Boundary: What This Spike Covers

| In scope | Out of scope |
|----------|-------------|
| gstack interaction patterns we can adopt | Building gstack skills for alto |
| Domain Storytelling methodology research | Implementing the new discovery flow |
| AI domain expert agent design | LLM integration or prompt engineering |
| Pipeline design (gstack -> alto -> beads) | gstack modifications |
| Domain model changes needed | Actual code changes to Session/Flow |

## Research Questions

### RQ1: gstack Interaction Patterns (what to learn)

Study these skills in .claude/skills/gstack/:

**plan-ceo-review/SKILL.md** -- The gold standard for interactive decision-making:
- 4 modes (Expansion, Selective Expansion, Hold Scope, Reduction) selected upfront
- Per-issue AskUserQuestion with opinionated recommendations
- Opt-in ceremony: each expansion proposal is its own decision
- Context-dependent defaults (greenfield -> Expansion, bug fix -> Hold Scope)

**design-consultation/SKILL.md** -- The gold standard for consultant-style discovery:
- Phase 0: Auto-infer product context from README, package.json, codebase
- Phase 1: Single combined question covering everything needed, pre-filled from inference
- Phase 2: Optional competitive research (only if user says yes)
- Phase 3: Complete proposal with SAFE/RISK breakdown -- propose, do not ask
- Phase 4: Drill-downs only on request
- Coherence validation when user overrides one section

**Shared preamble pattern** (all skills):
- Re-ground: state project, branch, current task (assumes 20-min gap)
- Simplify: plain English a smart 16-year-old could follow
- Recommend: opinionated, with rationale and completeness score
- Options: lettered, self-contained, one decision per interaction
- Escape hatch: if obvious, just do it -- do not waste a question

**Key contrast with alto's current flow:**
- gstack: "From what I can see, this is X for Y. Sound right?" (proposes, invites correction)
- alto: "Who are the actors that interact with your system?" (asks into void)

### RQ2: Domain Storytelling for AI-Guided Discovery (what to adopt)

**Why Domain Storytelling over Event Storming:**
- Sentence-based: "Actor does Activity using Work Object" -- natural language
- One story at a time, one scenario at a time -- prevents overwhelm
- Maps directly to DDD: actors -> aggregates, activities -> commands, work objects -> entities/VOs
- No technical jargon required from the user
- Sequential numbering makes validation easy

**Research needed:**
- How does the workshop format translate to a CLI conversation?
- Minimum viable Domain Story to bootstrap bounded contexts?
- Progression: Domain Story -> DDD Canvas -> Bounded Contexts -> Subdomain Classification
- Compare artifact quality: Domain Storytelling vs our current Q1-Q10

**References:**
- "Domain Storytelling" by Stefan Hoppe and Henning Schwentner (Addison-Wesley)
- domainstorytelling.org -- notation guide
- Comparison with Event Storming, Example Mapping, and other discovery techniques

### RQ3: AI Domain Expert Agent (what to build)

**The problem gstack solves differently:**
Garry Tan bakes his extensive startup/product experience into skill prompts. The agent draws on that knowledge to make opinionated proposals. This works because the domain (product/startup strategy) is consistent across users.

**Our problem is harder:**
Our users' domains vary widely (veterinary clinics, HR systems, logistics, fintech). We cannot pre-bake domain expertise. But we can bootstrap it.

**The pattern (modeled on gstack's design-consultation Phase 2):**
1. User gives vague idea: "I want to build a veterinary clinic management system"
2. alto offers: "Want me to research this domain first so I can propose better stories?"
3. If yes: AI agent researches via web search -- industry practices, common workflows, regulatory requirements, typical entities, existing software in the space
4. Agent proposes initial domain stories: "When a pet owner calls to book an appointment, the receptionist checks available slots, assigns a vet, and creates a visit record. Does that match how clinics work?"
5. User corrects and refines -- alto adapts, never argues
6. Even imperfect AI research gets the user past the blank-page problem

**Key design question:** Knowledge Trust Hierarchy -- USER_STATED > USER_CONFIRMED > AI_RESEARCHED > AI_INFERRED. How to track and surface this in generated artifacts?

### RQ4: The gstack -> alto -> beads Pipeline

**The handoff points:**

```
gstack /plan-ceo-review          alto discovery              alto ticket pipeline
========================    ======================    ==========================
Scope challenge              Domain Storytelling       Beads epics + tasks
10-star product vision       Bounded contexts          Dependency ordering
Mode selection               Subdomain classification  Template compliance
Accepted/deferred scope      DDD artifacts (PRD,       AC from domain invariants
CEO plan artifact              DDD.md, ARCH.md)
```

**Research needed:**
- Can alto consume gstack CEO plan output (~/.gstack/projects/{slug}/ceo-plans/) as input context?
- What format does alto need from the scope phase? (accepted scope items, deferred items, vision statement)
- Should alto detect gstack presence and offer to use CEO plan output? Or should this be manual?
- What if the user does not use gstack? alto must work standalone -- gstack is optional upstream enrichment.

## Key Files to Study

### gstack (.claude/skills/gstack/)
- plan-ceo-review/SKILL.md -- Interactive scope challenge with 4 modes
- plan-ceo-review/SKILL.md.tmpl -- Template showing what is shared vs skill-specific
- design-consultation/SKILL.md -- Consultant-style discovery (closest analog to what alto needs)
- plan-eng-review/SKILL.md -- Structured review with STOP points
- ARCHITECTURE.md -- System design
- SKILL.md.tmpl -- Shared preamble pattern

### alty-cli (current implementation)
- internal/discovery/domain/question.go -- 10-question catalog (the rigid part)
- internal/discovery/domain/discovery_session.go -- Session aggregate with strict state machine
- internal/discovery/domain/fixed_question_flow.go -- Fixed phase ordering
- internal/discovery/domain/conversational_flow.go -- More flexible but still question-driven
- internal/discovery/infrastructure/cli_discovery_adapter.go -- CLI orchestration
- internal/discovery/infrastructure/huh_prompter.go -- TUI prompts (charmbracelet/huh)

## Acceptance Criteria

### gstack patterns (RQ1)
- [ ] Document the 5 interaction principles from gstack: re-ground, simplify, recommend, options, escape hatch
- [ ] Document progressive disclosure: how phases activate conditionally, how auto-inference pre-fills context
- [ ] Document the consultant posture pattern with concrete before/after examples (gstack way vs alto current way)
- [ ] Identify 3-5 patterns adoptable in alto's discovery flow

### Domain Storytelling (RQ2)
- [ ] Research Domain Storytelling methodology: notation, workshop format, outputs
- [ ] Map Domain Storytelling elements to DDD concepts (actors -> aggregates, activities -> commands, work objects -> entities/VOs)
- [ ] Evaluate Domain Storytelling vs Event Storming for AI-guided discovery (complexity, knowledge requirements, artifact quality)
- [ ] Propose the story-to-DDD progression that replaces Q1-Q10

### AI domain expert agent (RQ3)
- [ ] Design the research-then-propose flow (modeled on design-consultation Phase 2)
- [ ] Define Knowledge Trust Hierarchy and how it surfaces in generated artifacts
- [ ] Identify domain model changes needed: Session, Question, Flow, new value objects

### Pipeline design (RQ4)
- [ ] Document the gstack -> alto -> beads handoff points and data formats
- [ ] Confirm alto works standalone (gstack is optional upstream)
- [ ] Propose how alto detects and consumes gstack CEO plan output

## Output

Research report at docs/research/YYYYMMDD_gstack_ux_and_domain_storytelling.md
notes:
Additional research direction (2026-03-23): Evaluate the gstack + alto pipeline model.

The idea: gstack handles project SCOPE (CEO review, eng review, design review) while alto handles DDD DESIGN (domain storytelling, bounded contexts, subdomain classification) and then TICKETS (beads epics, dependency-ordered tasks).

Pipeline: User idea -> gstack /plan-ceo-review (scope challenge, 10-star product) -> alto discovery (Domain Storytelling, DDD artifacts) -> alto ticket pipeline (beads epics and tasks)

This is important because gstack author (Garry Tan) bakes his extensive product/startup experience into the skill prompts. That experience drives the opinionated recommendations. For alto DDD discovery, we need to similarly bake in domain expertise -- but our users domains vary widely. Hence the AI domain expert agent that researches the specific domain before guiding the conversation.

Key question: Can alto consume gstack CEO plan output as input context for DDD discovery? If so, the user gets scope-challenged product thinking PLUS properly structured DDD artifacts PLUS dependency-ordered tickets.
close_reason:
Research complete. Three reports produced:

1. docs/research/20260323_gstack_ux_and_domain_storytelling.md (consolidated spike report)
2. docs/research/20260323_domain_storytelling_methodology.md (foundational DST research)
3. docs/research/20260323_domain_storytelling_2025_2026_developments.md (2025-2026 developments)

Key findings:
- 5 gstack interaction patterns to adopt (consultant proposal, one-decision-per-interaction, progressive phases, opinionated recommendations, coherence validation)
- Domain Storytelling validated as primary discovery technique (text-native, maps to DDD, lighter than Event Storming)
- 2026 breakthrough: Junker proved DST artifacts as LLM input produce better code (constrained generation technique)
- DST alone misses business rules -- need complementary technique for invariants/events/policies
- AI domain expert agent pattern designed (research-then-propose, modeled on gstack design-consultation Phase 2)
- Knowledge Trust Hierarchy defined (USER_STATED > USER_CONFIRMED > AI_RESEARCHED > AI_INFERRED)
- Documentation artifacts defined: .story.yaml, glossary.yaml, context-map.yaml, discovery-report.md
- 10 follow-up implementation tickets identified
- PRD updated with conversational discovery capability and Domain Storytelling approach

title: Move GitOps port to shared kernel
description:
## Goal / Problem

The `GitOps` port interface exists only in Rescue context (`internal/rescue/application/ports.go`), but Bootstrap (77p.4: auto-commit init output) also needs git operations. Creating a duplicate port in Bootstrap violates DRY. Moving it to shared kernel allows both contexts to use it.

## Background / Context

- Grooming of alty-cli-77p.4 revealed this cross-context concern
- Current location: `internal/rescue/application/ports.go`
- Methods: `CreateBranch`, `HasGit`, `IsClean`, etc.
- Bootstrap needs at minimum: `HasGit`, `StageFiles`, `Commit`
- ISP suggests Bootstrap should depend on a smaller interface than full GitOps

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Shared Kernel |
| Ubiquitous Language | GitOps, GitCommitter |
| Layer | Application (port) + Infrastructure (adapter stays in place) |

## Design

### Option A: Move full GitOps to shared

Move the entire `GitOps` interface to `internal/shared/application/ports.go`. Both Rescue and Bootstrap import from shared.

### Option B: ISP — Split into focused interfaces

```go
// internal/shared/application/ports.go

// GitDetector checks git repo state
type GitDetector interface {
    HasGit(dir string) bool
    IsClean(dir string) (bool, error)
}

// GitCommitter stages and commits
type GitCommitter interface {
    StageFiles(dir string, files []string) error
    Commit(dir string, message string) error
}

// GitBrancher manages branches
type GitBrancher interface {
    CreateBranch(dir string, name string) error
    CheckoutBranch(dir string, name string) error
}
```

Rescue composes all three. Bootstrap uses GitDetector + GitCommitter only.

### Recommendation

**Option B** — follows ISP, avoids Bootstrap depending on branch operations it doesn't need.

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| **S**ingle Responsibility | Each interface has one concern |
| **O**pen/Closed | New git operations add new interfaces, don't modify existing |
| **L**iskov Substitution | Existing adapter implements all sub-interfaces |

description:
## Goal / Problem

`DiscoverySession.SkipQuestion(questionID, reason)` accepts a reason parameter but discards it — only stores `skipped[questionID] = true`. Skip reasons are needed for Progressive Discovery (u6l epic) to show why questions were skipped and to enable re-asking.

## Background / Context

- Grooming of alty-cli-u6l.1 and u6l.2 revealed this domain model gap
- Current: `skipped map[string]bool` in DiscoverySession
- Needed: `skipped map[string]string` (key=questionID, value=reason)
- The `SkipQuestion()` method already receives the reason — it just doesn't store it
- `ToSnapshot()` and `FromSnapshot()` need updating for the new type
- Also needed: `UnskipQuestion(questionID)` method to allow re-asking (u6l.2 depends on this)

|-------|--------|-------|
| `skipped` | `map[string]bool` | `map[string]string` |

    // Remove from skipped map, allowing the question to be answered
}
```

title: Allow generate commands with partial model + warnings
description:
## Goal / Problem

Generate commands block entirely if the domain model is incomplete. They should work with partial models, producing what they can and warning about gaps.

## Background / Context

- Issues 4, 5, 13 from .notes/issues.md
- Current behavior: all three handlers return hard errors on empty/partial models:
  - TicketGenerationHandler.BuildPreview: "no bounded contexts" error (ticket_generation_handler_test.go:176)
  - FitnessGenerationHandler.BuildPreview: returns error if len(bcs)==0 (fitness_generation_handler.go:76-79)
  - ConfigGenerationHandler.BuildPreview: no explicit model check, fails downstream
- DomainModel already has a Warnings field (domain_model.go:30) — prepared for partial validation
- DomainModel.Finalize() checks 4 invariants and can emit warnings (e.g. "All bounded contexts are Generic")
- 623.3 will wire --from-docs to these handlers — u6l.3 makes them tolerant of incomplete imports

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Ticket, Fitness, ToolTranslation (application layers) |
| Ubiquitous Language | ModelGap, PartialGeneration, GenerationWarning |
| Layer | Application (generation handlers) |

## Design

### Approach: Handler-Level Gap Tolerance

Instead of modifying DomainModel internals, make each handler tolerant of incomplete input:

1. Remove hard errors for empty contexts — replace with warnings
2. Generate what's possible, skip what's not
3. Return preview with warnings attached

### Minimum Viable Model Per Handler

| Handler | Minimum Needed | Skip If Missing |
|---------|----------------|-----------------|
| Ticket | 1+ bounded contexts | Event tickets (if no events), relationship tickets (if no relationships) |
| Fitness | 1+ bounded contexts with classification | Unclassified contexts |
| Config | 1+ tools detected | Per-context config sections (if no contexts) |

### Warning Accumulation

Each preview type already has a Summary() method. Add a Warnings field:

```
type TicketPreview struct {
    // ... existing fields
    warnings []string
}
func (p *TicketPreview) Warnings() []string
```

Same pattern for FitnessPreview and ConfigPreview.

### Truly Empty Model = Error

If model has ZERO bounded contexts AND zero aggregates AND zero events -> return error: "model is empty, nothing to generate. Run 'alty guide' or 'alty import' first."

### No --strict Flag

The original ticket proposes --strict. YAGNI — remove. The default behavior becomes tolerant. If users want strict validation, they run Finalize() explicitly via alty check.

## TDD Workflow

### RED Phase

```
// Ticket handler
TestTicketBuildPreview_WhenPartialModel_ExpectPreviewWithWarnings
TestTicketBuildPreview_WhenNoContexts_ExpectPreviewWithWarning
TestTicketBuildPreview_WhenEmptyModel_ExpectError

// Fitness handler
TestFitnessBuildPreview_WhenPartialModel_ExpectPreviewWithWarnings
TestFitnessBuildPreview_WhenNoClassifications_ExpectWarning
TestFitnessBuildPreview_WhenEmptyModel_ExpectError

// Config handler
TestConfigBuildPreview_WhenNoContexts_ExpectPartialOutput
TestConfigBuildPreview_WhenEmptyModel_ExpectError
```

### GREEN Phase

1. Add Warnings field to TicketPreview, FitnessPreview, ConfigPreview
2. Replace hard errors with warning accumulation in each BuildPreview
3. Add minimum-viable check (truly empty = error)
4. Update existing tests that expect hard errors

### REFACTOR Phase

- Extract shared isModelEmpty(model) helper to shared/domain/ddd
- Standardize warning message format across handlers

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Enforcement |
|-----------|-------------|
| S | Each handler manages its own gap tolerance |
| O | Warning accumulation added without changing generation logic |
| L | Preview types still satisfy same contracts |
| I | No new interfaces needed |
| D | Handlers depend on DomainModel — no new deps |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Partial model with some contexts -> produces partial preview + warnings
- [ ] Model with contexts but no events -> skips event tickets, warns
- [ ] Model with contexts but no classifications -> skips classification fitness, warns
- [ ] Truly empty model -> returns error with guidance
- [ ] Warning messages clearly state what was skipped and why
- [ ] Existing tests updated for new tolerance behavior

## Edge Cases

| Case | Input | Expected |
|------|-------|----------|
| 1 context, no events | Minimal model | Tickets for context only, warn about events |
| All contexts Generic | No Core/Supporting | Warning: "All contexts Generic — no core domain tickets" |
| No aggregates | Contexts without aggregates | Skip aggregate tickets, warn |
| Empty model | Zero everything | Error: "model is empty" |
| Complete model | All data present | No warnings, full output |

## Pre-Implementation Validation

- [ ] Read ticket/application/ticket_generation_handler.go BuildPreview — trace what fails
- [ ] Read fitness/application/fitness_generation_handler.go BuildPreview — trace what fails
- [ ] Read tooltranslation/application/config_generation_handler.go BuildPreview — trace what fails
- [ ] Read shared/domain/ddd/domain_model.go — confirm Warnings field exists
- [ ] Count tests that expect hard errors on empty model — these change to warning tests

## QA Before Close

- [ ] go build ./... — zero errors
- [ ] go vet ./... — zero errors
- [ ] golangci-lint run ./... — zero issues
- [ ] go test ./... -race — all pass

## Risks / Dependencies

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| Changing error -> warning breaks existing tests | Update tests — this is intentional behavior change |
| Partial output confusing to users | Warnings explain what's missing |
| 623.3 depends on handlers working with imported models | u6l.3 makes handlers tolerant — complementary |

title: Design and implement session persistence format
description:
## Goal / Problem

Discovery sessions are stored only in-memory (DiscoveryHandler.sessions map). When the process exits, all session state is lost. Progressive discovery requires persisting sessions to disk so they can be resumed across invocations.

## Background / Context

- Issue 4 from .notes/issues.md — skipping questions produces no persistent output
- P3 (alty-cli-2e4) CLOSED — skip reasons now persisted in snapshot format
- Existing ToSnapshot()/FromSnapshot() with JSON round-trip already tested at discovery_session_test.go:789-797
- SessionRepository and SessionCheckpoint defined in DDD.md glossary (line 239-240)

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Guided Discovery |
| Ubiquitous Language | SessionRepository, SessionCheckpoint, DiscoverySession |
| Layer | Application (port) + Infrastructure (adapter) |

## Design

### Port Interface

\`\`\`go
// internal/discovery/application/ports.go

// SessionRepository persists and loads DiscoverySession state across process invocations.
type SessionRepository interface {
    Save(ctx context.Context, session *domain.DiscoverySession) error
    Load(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) (*domain.DiscoverySession, error)
    Exists(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) (bool, error)
}
\`\`\`

### Adapter

\`\`\`go
// internal/discovery/infrastructure/filesystem_session_repository.go

type FileSystemSessionRepository struct {
    baseDir string  // e.g. ".alty/"
}
\`\`\`

### Persistence Format

JSON via existing ToSnapshot()/FromSnapshot(). No new serialization format.

\`\`\`
Save: session.ToSnapshot() -> json.Marshal -> write .alty/discovery_session.json
Load: read file -> json.Unmarshal -> domain.FromSnapshot(data)
\`\`\`

### Snapshot Format (current, after P3 fix)

Skip reasons serialized as \`[]map[string]string\` with \`question_id\` + \`reason\` keys.
Full format includes: session_id, status, persona, register, mode, round, tech_stack, answers, skipped, playback_confirmations, context_classifications, readme_content.

### Sequence Flow

\`\`\`
DiscoveryHandler                FileSystemSessionRepository         File System
    |                                    |                               |
    |-- Save(session) ------------------>|                               |
    |                                    |-- session.ToSnapshot()        |
    |                                    |-- json.Marshal(snapshot)      |
    |                                    |-- os.MkdirAll(baseDir)------->|
    |                                    |-- os.WriteFile(path, data)--->|
    |<-- nil ----------------------------|                               |
\`\`\`

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| **S**ingle Responsibility | SessionRepository owns persistence only, not session logic |
| **O**pen/Closed | New storage backends (DB, cloud) add adapters, don't modify port |
| **L**iskov Substitution | Any SessionRepository impl works in handler |
| **I**nterface Segregation | 3 focused methods (Save/Load/Exists), not bundled with FileWriter |
| **D**ependency Inversion | Handler depends on SessionRepository port, not filesystem |

## TDD Workflow

### RED Phase

\`\`\`go
// internal/discovery/infrastructure/filesystem_session_repository_test.go
TestFileSystemSessionRepository_Save_WhenValidSession_WritesJSONFile
TestFileSystemSessionRepository_Save_WhenDirMissing_CreatesDir
TestFileSystemSessionRepository_Load_WhenFileExists_RestoresSession
TestFileSystemSessionRepository_Load_WhenFileNotFound_ReturnsError
TestFileSystemSessionRepository_Load_WhenCorruptedJSON_ReturnsError
TestFileSystemSessionRepository_Exists_WhenFileExists_ReturnsTrue
TestFileSystemSessionRepository_Exists_WhenFileMissing_ReturnsFalse
TestFileSystemSessionRepository_RoundTrip_WhenSavedAndLoaded_PreservesState

// internal/discovery/application/discovery_handler_test.go
TestDiscoveryHandler_WhenAnswerQuestion_SavesSession
TestDiscoveryHandler_WhenSkipQuestion_SavesSession
\`\`\`

### GREEN Phase

1. Create SessionRepository port in \`internal/discovery/application/ports.go\`
2. Create FileSystemSessionRepository at \`internal/discovery/infrastructure/filesystem_session_repository.go\`
3. Implement Save: \`session.ToSnapshot()\` -> \`json.Marshal\` -> \`os.WriteFile\`
4. Implement Load: \`os.ReadFile\` -> \`json.Unmarshal\` -> \`domain.FromSnapshot\`
5. Implement Exists: \`os.Stat\` check
6. Add SessionRepository to DiscoveryHandler constructor
7. Call repo.Save() after AnswerQuestion and SkipQuestion in handler
8. Add compile-time check: \`var _ application.SessionRepository = (*FileSystemSessionRepository)(nil)\`

### REFACTOR Phase

- Extract file path logic to helper method
- Ensure error wrapping follows project convention (\`fmt.Errorf("saving session: %w", err)\`)
- Run full quality gates

## Steps

1. Add \`SessionRepository\` interface to \`internal/discovery/application/ports.go\`
2. Create \`internal/discovery/infrastructure/filesystem_session_repository.go\` following \`FilesystemFileWriter\` pattern
3. Write adapter tests (TDD RED -> GREEN)
4. Add \`sessionRepo SessionRepository\` field to \`DiscoveryHandler\`
5. Update \`NewDiscoveryHandler\` constructor signature
6. Call \`sessionRepo.Save()\` after each AnswerQuestion/SkipQuestion in handler
7. Update composition root (\`internal/composition/app.go\`) to wire new dependency
8. Update handler tests with mock SessionRepository

## Edge Cases

| Case | Input | Expected Output |
|------|-------|-----------------|
| Missing .alty/ directory | Save when dir doesn't exist | Create dir with MkdirAll, then write |
| Corrupted JSON file | Load with invalid JSON | Return wrapped error |
| Empty file | Load empty file | Return wrapped error |
| File permissions error | Write to read-only dir | Return wrapped error |
| Session not found | Load non-existent ID | Return specific NotFound error |
| Concurrent writes | Two saves racing | Last write wins (acceptable for CLI) |
| Empty projectDir | Save with "" baseDir | Return validation error |
| Very large session | Many answers + classifications | JSON handles gracefully |

## Pre-Implementation Validation

- [x] ToSnapshot()/FromSnapshot() JSON round-trip tested (discovery_session_test.go:789-797)
- [x] Skip reasons included in snapshot (discovery_session.go:496-503, new format after P3)

- [ ] Verify no import cycles from discovery/infrastructure -> discovery/application

## QA Before Close

- [ ] Save + Load round-trip preserves all session fields
- [ ] Skip reasons survive round-trip

go test ./... -race

- **Risk:** DiscoveryHandler constructor change will break existing callers (composition root, tests, MCP). Mitigate: make SessionRepository optional (accept nil, skip saving).
- **Dependency:** Completed: P3 (alty-cli-2e4) — skip reasons now persisted in snapshot

    classification: string  # enum: "core" | "supporting" | "generic" (line 120-129)
    rationale: string       # optional, omitempty (artifact_generation_handler.go:384)
    layers: []string        # default: ["domain", "application", "infrastructure"]
    relationships:          # list, optional
      - target: string
        direction: string   # enum: "upstream" | "downstream" (line 158-166)
        pattern: string     # enum: "domain_event" | "shared_kernel" | "acl" | "open_host" (line 169-181)
```

### Generator schema (subset, what alty guide emits)

Source: internal/discovery/application/artifact_generation_handler.go:406-412

The generator emits: name, module_path, classification, rationale, layers
The generator does NOT emit: relationships

This gap matters for alty-cli-623.2 -- the import command should produce the FULL schema (including relationships) since users creating files manually will want relationship data.

## Steps

title: Generate valid TOML config with detected project settings
description:
## Goal / Problem

`alty init` creates `.alty/config.toml` with only `project_name` and `version`. It should include detected language, module path, and AI tools from `ProjectDetectionResult` (77p.1).

## Background / Context

- Issue 2, 9 from .notes/issues.md
- 77p.1 delivered `ProjectDetectionResult` with `Language()`, `ManifestPath()`, `HasAIToolConfig()`, etc.
- Current `ContentProvider.ContentFor(path, projectName)` only passes project name — needs richer input
- `BurntSushi/toml v1.6.0` already in `go.mod` (indirect dep)
- Schema must align with `docs/internal-formats.md` Section 1 + f0g.1 `[llm]` placeholder

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Bootstrap |
| Ubiquitous Language | ProjectConfig, ContentProvider |
| Layer | Domain (ProjectConfig VO) + Infrastructure (TOML content gen) + Application (ContentProvider signature) |

## Design

### Target Config Schema

```toml
# alty project configuration

[project]
name = "my-service"
language = "go"
module_path = "github.com/user/my-service"

[tools]
detected = ["claude", "cursor"]

[discovery]
completed = false

# [llm]
# provider = ""
# model = ""
# api_key_env = ""
# Uncomment and configure when LLM features are enabled (see f0g epic)
```

### Data Models

| Model | Type | Location | Purpose |
|-------|------|----------|---------|
| `ProjectConfig` | Value Object | `bootstrap/domain/project_config.go` | Holds config fields for TOML generation |

**ProjectConfig fields:**
- `name` (string) — from dir name or manifest
- `language` (string) — from `ProjectDetectionResult.Language()`
- `modulePath` (string) — parsed from go.mod/pyproject.toml/package.json
- `detectedTools` ([]string) — from `DetectionHandler.Detect()`

**Constructor:** `NewProjectConfig(name, language, modulePath string, tools []string) ProjectConfig`

### Interface Change

Current: `ContentProvider.ContentFor(path string, projectName string) string`
New: `ContentProvider.ContentFor(path string, config domain.ProjectConfig) string`

**Blast radius:**
- `bootstrap/application/bootstrap_handler.go:149` — call site, passes `filepath.Base(session.ProjectDir())`
- `bootstrap/application/bootstrap_handler.go:29-30` — port interface
- `bootstrap/infrastructure/content.go:19` — adapter implementation
- `bootstrap/application/bootstrap_handler_test.go:81-83` — fake implementation
- `composition/app.go:168` — adapter instantiation (no change, adapter is struct)

### Module Path Extraction

Add to `FileSystemProjectDetector` or new helper:
- **Go:** `go.mod` line 1: `module github.com/user/project` → extract after `module `
- **Python:** `pyproject.toml` `[project] name = "..."` → extract name
- **TypeScript:** `package.json` `"name": "..."` → extract name
- **Fallback:** directory name

### Where Detection Result Feeds In

`init.go` already calls `app.ProjectDetector.Detect(".")` and gets `ProjectDetectionResult`. This result must reach `ContentProvider` through the bootstrap flow:

Option A (simpler): Extract module path in `init.go`, build `ProjectConfig`, pass to handler
Option B (cleaner): Add `ProjectDetectionResult` to `BootstrapSession`, let handler build `ProjectConfig`

**Recommended: Option A** — keeps the handler unchanged, `init.go` already has the detection result, and `runInit` just needs to pass a richer object to `ContentFor` via a session field.

Actually, the cleanest path: `BootstrapHandler.Execute()` already calls `h.contentProvider.ContentFor()`. The handler needs the config. So:
1. Add `ProjectConfig` field to `BootstrapSession` (set during Preview or via new setter)
2. `ContentFor` receives `ProjectConfig` instead of just `projectName`
3. `init.go` calls a new `handler.SetProjectConfig(sessionID, config)` before Execute, OR passes it during Preview

**Simplest:** Change `Preview(projectDir)` to `Preview(projectDir, config ProjectConfig)`. The handler stores it in the session and uses it in Execute.

## TDD Workflow

### RED Phase

```go
// Domain
TestNewProjectConfig_WhenAllFields_ExpectAccessorsWork
TestNewProjectConfig_WhenEmptyName_ExpectDirectoryFallback
TestProjectConfig_ModulePath_WhenEmpty_ExpectProjectName

// Infrastructure  
TestAltyConfigContent_WhenGoProject_ExpectValidTOML
TestAltyConfigContent_WhenPythonProject_ExpectValidTOML
TestAltyConfigContent_WhenNoLanguage_ExpectMinimalTOML
TestAltyConfigContent_ParsedByTOMLLibrary

// Infrastructure — Module path extraction
TestExtractModulePath_GoMod
TestExtractModulePath_PyprojectToml
TestExtractModulePath_PackageJson
TestExtractModulePath_NoManifest_FallbackToDirName

// Application
TestBootstrapHandler_Execute_WhenConfigProvided_ExpectRicherTOML
```

### GREEN Phase

1. Create `ProjectConfig` VO in `bootstrap/domain/`
2. Add module path extraction to `FileSystemProjectDetector` (or new `ModulePathExtractor`)
3. Change `ContentProvider.ContentFor` signature to accept `ProjectConfig`
4. Update `ContentProviderAdapter.AltyConfigContent()` to render all sections
5. Update `BootstrapHandler` to pass `ProjectConfig` through session
6. Update `init.go` to build `ProjectConfig` from detection result
7. Update fakes in tests

### REFACTOR Phase

- Verify TOML output parses cleanly with `BurntSushi/toml`
- Ensure backward compat: existing `.alty/config.toml` files still work

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Enforcement |
|-----------|-------------|
| **S** | `ProjectConfig` is a VO with one job: hold config data |
| **O** | New TOML sections (like `[llm]`) can be added without changing existing code |
| **L** | `ContentProviderAdapter` still satisfies `ContentProvider` interface |
| **I** | `ContentProvider` stays focused: one method |
| **D** | Handler depends on `ContentProvider` interface, never on adapter |

## Steps

1. Create `ProjectConfig` VO in `bootstrap/domain/project_config.go`
2. Add `ExtractModulePath(projectDir, manifestPath string) string` to `FileSystemProjectDetector`
3. Change `ContentProvider` port signature: `ContentFor(path string, config domain.ProjectConfig) string`
4. Update `ContentProviderAdapter` to render richer TOML with `[project]`, `[tools]`, `[discovery]` sections
5. Update `BootstrapHandler` — store `ProjectConfig` in session, pass to `ContentFor`
6. Update `init.go` — build `ProjectConfig` from detection result + detection handler
7. Update all test fakes
8. Run quality gates

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Generated `.alty/config.toml` is valid TOML (verified by `BurntSushi/toml` in test)
- [ ] Config includes `[project]` section with name, language, module_path
- [ ] Config includes `[tools]` section with detected AI tools
- [ ] Config includes `[discovery]` section with `completed = false`
- [ ] Config includes commented `[llm]` placeholder for f0g epic
- [ ] `ContentProvider.ContentFor` accepts `ProjectConfig` instead of bare `projectName`
- [ ] Module path extracted from go.mod / pyproject.toml / package.json
- [ ] Fallback: missing manifest → project name only, no language
- [ ] All existing tests updated and passing

## Edge Cases

| Case | Input | Expected Output |
|------|-------|-----------------|
| No manifest | Empty project | `[project] name = "dirname"`, no language/module_path |
| go.mod present | `module github.com/user/foo` | language="go", module_path from first line |
| pyproject.toml | `[project] name = "bar"` | language="python", module_path="bar" |
| package.json | `{"name": "baz"}` | language="typescript", module_path="baz" |
| Multiple manifests | go.mod + package.json | First match wins (go.mod priority) |
| Malformed go.mod | No module line | Fallback to dir name |
| No AI tools | No .claude/.cursor | `detected = []` |

## Pre-Implementation Validation

- [ ] Read `docs/internal-formats.md` Section 1 — verify schema alignment
- [ ] Read `docs/research/20260314_llm_integration.md` — verify `[llm]` section format
- [ ] Confirm `BurntSushi/toml` is in go.mod (it is, v1.6.0 indirect)
- [ ] Read `bootstrap/application/bootstrap_handler.go` — trace ContentFor call site
- [ ] Read `bootstrap/infrastructure/content.go` — current AltyConfigContent
- [ ] Read `bootstrap/application/bootstrap_handler_test.go` — count fakes to update

## QA Before Close

- [ ] `go build ./...` — zero errors
- [ ] `go vet ./...` — zero errors
- [ ] `golangci-lint run ./...` — zero issues
- [ ] `go test ./... -race` — all pass
- [ ] TOML output validated by parser in test

## Risks / Dependencies

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| `ContentProvider` signature change breaks downstream | Only used in Bootstrap BC — contained blast radius |
| `[llm]` section format changes when f0g.2 lands | Use comments only (no actual fields) — f0g.2 adds real fields |
| Module path parsing fragile | Regex with fallback to dir name; test all manifest formats |
notes:
## Implementation Simulation (2026-03-15)

### Interface Chain Verified

1. `ContentProvider.ContentFor(path, projectName)` at `bootstrap/application/bootstrap_handler.go:29-30`
2. Called at `bootstrap_handler.go:149`: `h.contentProvider.ContentFor(action.Path(), filepath.Base(session.ProjectDir()))`
3. Implemented by `ContentProviderAdapter` at `bootstrap/infrastructure/content.go:19`
4. Fake in tests at `bootstrap_handler_test.go:81-83`

**Signature change:** `ContentFor(path string, config domain.ProjectConfig) string`
- 1 port interface change
- 1 adapter change
- 1 call site in handler (line 149)
- 1 fake in tests (line 81-83)
- 12+ test constructors use `&fakeContentProvider{}` — all need `ContentFor` signature update

### Module Path Extraction — Where To Put It

Option: Add `ExtractModulePath(projectDir, manifestPath string) string` as a standalone function in `bootstrap/infrastructure/` (not on the detector, since detection already ran). The init.go code calls it after detection.

### TOML Library Status

`BurntSushi/toml v1.6.0` is indirect dep (used by cobra/viper chain). Can use directly for validation in tests. For generation, raw `fmt.Sprintf` is fine — simpler than marshaling structs.

### Schema Compatibility

Current `docs/internal-formats.md` Section 1 shows:
```toml
project_name = "my-service"
version = "0.1.0"
```

New schema changes to `[project]` table. This is a BREAKING CHANGE for any existing `.alty/config.toml` files. Acceptable since:
- alty is pre-1.0
- No production users yet
- Update `docs/internal-formats.md` in same ticket

### f0g.1 LLM Config Section

From spike report, the `[llm]` section will have:
```toml
[llm]
provider = "anthropic"
model = "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"
api_key_env = "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
base_url = ""
timeout = "30s"
```

For 77p.2: emit as commented placeholder only. f0g.2 will uncomment and populate.
close_reason: Implemented: ProjectConfig VO, module path extraction in Detect(), richer TOML with [project]/[tools]/[discovery]/[llm] sections, ContentProvider signature change. All gates pass.

title: Auto-detect existing project state in alty init
description:
## Goal / Problem

`alty init` requires `--existing` flag for existing projects. Users must understand alty's internal model before starting. The tool should adapt to the project, not the other way around.

## Background / Context

- Issue 1 from .notes/issues.md
- Current behavior: `alty init` vs `alty init --existing` requires user decision
- Expected: auto-detect and choose the right path

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Bootstrap |
| Ubiquitous Language | ProjectState, DetectionResult |
| Layer | Application (detection logic) + Infrastructure (file system checks) |

## Design

### Detection Heuristics

1. Check if directory is a git repo (`git rev-parse --git-dir`)
2. Check for source files (`*.go`, `go.mod`, `*.py`, `pyproject.toml`, etc.)
3. Check for existing `docs/` folder and scan contents
4. Check for AI tool configs (`.claude/`, `.cursor/`, `CLAUDE.md`)
5. Based on findings, automatically choose init path

### Data Models

| Model | Type | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| `ProjectState` | Value Object | Represents detected project state |
| `DetectionResult` | Value Object | Aggregates detection findings |

## TDD Workflow

### RED Phase

```go
// internal/bootstrap/domain/project_state_test.go
TestDetectEmptyDirectory: should return NewProject state
TestDetectGitRepoWithGoMod: should return ExistingProject with Go language
TestDetectDocsFolder: should return ExistingProject with detected docs
TestDetectAIToolConfigs: should detect Claude/Cursor configs
```

### GREEN Phase

1. Implement ProjectState value object
2. Implement detection heuristics in infrastructure layer
3. Wire into init command to auto-select path

## Steps

1. Create ProjectState value object with NewProject/ExistingProject variants
2. Create FileSystemDetector adapter implementing detection port
3. Update init command to use detector instead of --existing flag
4. Add ambiguity handling: prompt user only when unclear

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `alty init` works without --existing flag
- [ ] Empty directories detected as new projects
- [ ] Go/Python projects detected from manifest files
- [ ] Existing docs detected and reported
- [ ] Ambiguous cases prompt user with findings

## Edge Cases

| Case | Input | Expected Output |
|------|-------|-----------------|
| Empty directory | No files | NewProject state |
| Git repo + go.mod | Go project | ExistingProject with Go |
| Docs but no source | Just docs/ | Prompt: "Found docs but no source..." |
| Mixed signals | go.mod + pyproject.toml | Prompt: "Found multiple languages..." |

## Quality Gates

```bash
golangci-lint run ./...
go vet ./...
go test ./... -race
```
notes:
## Grooming Review (2026-03-15)

### BC Confirmed: Bootstrap
- Detection heuristics belong in Bootstrap — this is about deciding the init path
- BUT: `DetectionResult` name already exists in `discovery/domain/detection_result.go` (tool/conflict detection)
- RENAME to `ProjectDetectionResult` or `ProjectState` to avoid collision

### Overlap with Rescue `ProjectScan`
- Rescue has `ProjectScan` port in `rescue/application/ports.go` that scans for existing docs/configs/structure
- 77p.1 overlaps: both detect go.mod, docs/, .claude/, etc.
- **Decision needed:** Should 77p.1 REUSE the Rescue `ProjectScan` adapter, or build its own?
- Recommendation: Build Bootstrap-specific `ProjectDetector` port (ISP). Rescue scans for gaps, Bootstrap scans for path selection — different concerns, different return types.

### Port Definition (missing from ticket)
```go
// internal/bootstrap/application/ports.go
type ProjectDetector interface {
    Detect(projectDir string) (ProjectDetectionResult, error)
}
```

### ProjectDetectionResult (new VO)
```go
// internal/bootstrap/domain/
type ProjectDetectionResult struct {
    hasSourceCode   bool
    language        string     // "go", "python", "typescript", ""
    hasDocsFolder   bool
    hasAltyConfig   bool
    hasAIToolConfig bool
    manifestPath    string     // "go.mod", "pyproject.toml", etc.
}
func (r ProjectDetectionResult) IsExistingProject() bool { ... }
func (r ProjectDetectionResult) IsAmbiguous() bool { ... }
```

### Impact on init.go
- Currently: `if existing { runRescue() } else { runInit() }`
- After 77p.1: auto-detect replaces `--existing` flag
- `--existing` stays as override (backward compat), but auto-detection is default

### Missing Template Sections
- [ ] GREEN Phase
- [ ] REFACTOR Phase
- [ ] SOLID Mapping (SRP: ProjectDetector only detects, DIP: handler depends on port)
- [ ] Pre-Implementation Validation
close_reason: Phase 2 complete — committed and pushed in 38ecd0c

title: Epic: Progressive Discovery
description:
## Goal / Problem

Discovery session doesn't persist when questions are skipped. User answered Q1, Q3, Q4, skipped Q2 and Q5–Q10 (each with a reason). Output said "Discovery complete." but all `alty generate` commands failed with "requires a completed discovery session".

Additionally, discovery is a one-shot quiz, not an iterative process. There is no way to:
- Come back later and refine answers
- Add new bounded contexts discovered during implementation
- Update the domain model when requirements change
- Run discovery incrementally

## DDD Alignment

| Bounded Context | Impact |
|----------------|--------|
| Discovery | Persistence layer for partial sessions |
| Discovery | Resume and update capabilities |

## Success Metrics

- Partial answers are saved and usable
- `alty guide --continue` resumes from last session
- Model can be updated incrementally without full re-run
- Skipped questions are tracked as open questions, not blockers

## Scope

**In scope**
- Persist partial discovery sessions
- Resume interrupted sessions
- Update specific answers without full re-run
- Track skipped questions as gaps (not blockers)

**Out of scope**
- Versioned model snapshots (future)
- Automatic re-discovery triggers

## Phases / Milestones

1. Phase 1 - Session persistence format design
2. Phase 2 - Implement partial session saving
3. Phase 3 - Implement --continue flag
4. Phase 4 - Implement answer update capability
5. Phase 5 - Gap tracking (skipped → open questions)

## Child Tasks (planned)

- Design session persistence format
- Save partial answers during guide
- Implement `alty guide --continue`
- Implement `alty guide --update-question N`
- Track skipped questions as open questions
- Allow generate commands with partial model + warnings

## Risks / Unknowns

- Session state migration between alty versions
- Conflict resolution when updating answers
- Determining "minimum viable model" for generate commands

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Partial sessions are saved to .alty/
- [ ] `alty guide --continue` resumes from saved state
- [ ] Individual answers can be updated
- [ ] Skipped questions don't block generate commands
- [ ] Generate commands warn about gaps but proceed
close_reason: all steps complete
