title: Scaffold Astro + Starlight in website/ subdirectory
description:
## Goal / Problem

Set up Astro with Starlight docs theme in a `website/` subdirectory, isolated from the Go project root. Configure the glob() content loader to pull markdown from `../docs/`.

## Background / Context

- Spike alty-cli-dkc confirmed Astro + Starlight as the recommended SSG
- Astro's glob() loader can reference `../docs/*.md` — verified in official docs
- No JS files (package.json, node_modules, etc.) should exist at repo root
- `website/.gitignore` should exclude node_modules

## Steps

1. Run `npm create astro@latest` in `website/`
2. Install Starlight: `npx astro add starlight`
3. Configure `astro.config.mjs` with Starlight integration
4. Set up content collection with glob() loader pointing to `../docs/guides/`
5. Add `.gitignore` for node_modules in `website/`
6. Add `website/README.md` with build instructions
7. Verify `npm run build` produces static output in `website/dist/`
8. Add repo root `.gitignore` entry for `website/node_modules/` and `website/dist/`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `website/` contains Astro project with Starlight
- [ ] No JS config files at repo root (all in `website/`)
- [ ] Content collection loads `../docs/guides/*.md` via glob()
- [ ] `cd website && npm run dev` serves docs locally
- [ ] `cd website && npm run build` produces static HTML in `dist/`
- [ ] Landing page placeholder exists at `website/src/pages/index.astro`

## Risks / Dependencies

- Depends on task 1 (user guides) for content to render
- Node.js required in CI for website builds
notes:
## Layer 2 Grooming (2026-03-14)

### Inputs from Layer 1
- 7 guide files in `docs/guides/` with Starlight frontmatter — ready to load via glob()
- Design research at `docs/research/20260314_website_design.md` §7 has file structure recommendation
- Docs page mockup shows sidebar IA that differs from guide filenames — reconcile during setup

### Sidebar IA Reconciliation
Mockup sidebar categories vs actual guide files:
- "Configuration" in mockup → no guide file (skip or create stub)
- "DDD Discovery" in mockup → maps to `new-project.md` + `concepts.md`
- "Challenge System" in mockup → no guide file (skip)
- `existing-project.md` and `ai-tool-integration.md` not in mockup sidebar → add them

**Decision needed:** Use guide filenames as-is for sidebar, or restructure to match mockup IA?
Recommendation: Use guide filenames as-is. The mockup is inspirational, not prescriptive.

### Tailwind NOT installed in this ticket
Per previous grooming: Tailwind installation deferred to qzv.4. This ticket produces a vanilla Starlight scaffold.

### Content collection config
Use Astro glob() loader, NOT Starlight docsLoader():
```js
import { defineCollection } from 'astro:content';
import { glob } from 'astro/loaders';
const guides = defineCollection({
  loader: glob({ pattern: '**/*.md', base: '../docs/guides' }),
});
```
close_reason: Layer 2 complete — Astro scaffold + design system delivered and reviewed

title: Write user guide documentation for alty scenarios
description:
## Goal / Problem

Before designing the website, we need the content. Write user-facing documentation covering all primary alty scenarios so the design phase has real content to work with.

## Background / Context

- alty has 14 user-facing commands (excluding `completion` and `help`)
- Existing internal docs in `docs/` (PRD.md, DDD.md, ARCHITECTURE.md) are reference, not user guides
- Target audience: developers, team leads, product owners (see PRD §3 personas)
- Terminal recordings (VHS) deferred to follow-up ticket — this ticket is prose only

## Content to Write

All guides go in `docs/guides/`. Each file MUST have Starlight-compatible frontmatter:

```yaml
---
title: Guide Title
description: One-line description for SEO
sidebar:
  order: 1
---
```

### Guides

1. **`quickstart.md`** — 5-minute getting started (install → `alty init -y` → first project). Shortest path to value.
2. **`installation.md`** — Detailed install: `go install`, binary download, prerequisites (Go 1.26+, beads).
3. **`new-project.md`** — Full walkthrough: write README → `alty init` → preview → confirm → guided discovery (10 questions) → generated artifacts (PRD, DDD, ARCH, .alty/, AGENTS.md, tickets).
4. **`existing-project.md`** — Rescue mode: `alty init --existing` → gap analysis → migration plan → branch-based scaffolding. Include `alty gap` for standalone analysis.
5. **`cli-reference.md`** — All 14 commands with flags and examples:

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `init` | Bootstrap new project (`--existing`, `--dry-run`, `--yes`) |
| `guide` | 10-question DDD discovery (`--no-tui`) |
| `gap` | Standalone gap analysis (`[project-dir]`) |
| `detect` | Scan for installed AI tools |
| `check` | Run quality gates |
| `fitness` | Architecture fitness testing |
| `generate` | Generate project artifacts |
| `kb` | Knowledge base operations |
| `doc-health` | Check doc freshness |
| `doc-review` | Manage doc review status |
| `ticket-health` | Ripple review report |
| `ticket-verify` | Verify ticket claims |

title: Generate .alty/ directory in alty init and wire guide flow
description:
## Goal / Problem

`alty init` preview lists 3 `.alty/` files (bootstrap_handler.go:34-36) but the Execute flow has no file writer — users see the plan but get nothing on disk. Additionally, `runInit` (init.go:39-48) only calls `Preview` and exits, telling the user to run `alty guide` separately. The full flow should be: Preview → Confirm → Execute (write scaffold) → Guide (discovery).

Merges former aqx.1 (content generators) and aqx.2 (wiring) — splitting them created artificial blocking since they share the same constructor change.

## Background / Context

- Bootstrap handler at `internal/bootstrap/application/bootstrap_handler.go` — `plannedFiles` at L29-37, `Execute` at L125-140
- `Execute` transitions session state but performs no I/O — needs FileWriter
- `runInit` at `cmd/alty/commands/init.go:39-48` — Preview-only, exits immediately
- `runGuide` at `cmd/alty/commands/guide.go:37-62` — detection + interactive discovery
- FileWriter adapter exists at `internal/shared/infrastructure/persistence/filesystem_file_writer.go`
- Composition root creates `fileWriter` at `app.go:103-104`, already used by 7 handlers
- **Pattern reference:** `internal/rescue/application/rescue_handler.go:159-173` (gap-to-file writing loop)

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Bootstrap (handler + content generators) |
| Ubiquitous Language | Seed, Bootstrap, Preview, FileAction, Execute |
| Layer | Application (handler) + Infrastructure (content generators) + CLI (init command) |

## Design

### Data Models

No new domain types. Content generators are infrastructure-layer pure functions returning strings.

### Sequence / Flow

```
CLI (init.go)         BootstrapHandler     FileWriter     Guide flow
    |                      |                  |                |
    |-- Preview ---------->|                  |                |
    |<-- show plan --------|                  |                |
    |-- user confirms ---->|                  |                |
    |-- Execute ---------->|                  |                |
    |                      |-- for each ------>|                |
    |                      |   FileAction      |                |
    |                      |   (CREATE only)   |                |
    |<-- scaffold done ----|                  |                |
    |-- runGuide --------->|                  |         10-question flow
    |<-- discovery done ---|                  |                |
```

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| **S**ingle Responsibility | Content generators: one function per file. Handler: orchestrates write loop. CLI: user interaction. |
| **O**pen/Closed | New planned files add entries to `plannedFiles` + a content function |
| **I**nterface Segregation | Reuses `sharedapp.FileWriter` (single method: WriteFile) |
| **D**ependency Inversion | Handler depends on FileWriter port, injected by composition root |

## TDD Workflow

### RED Phase

```
internal/bootstrap/infrastructure/content_test.go
test_alty_config_content_is_valid_toml: Generated config.toml parses as valid TOML
test_knowledge_index_content_is_valid_toml: Generated _index.toml parses
test_doc_registry_content_is_valid_toml: Generated doc-registry.toml parses

internal/bootstrap/application/bootstrap_handler_test.go
test_execute_writes_create_files: Execute calls FileWriter for each CREATE action
test_execute_skips_existing_files: Files marked Skip are not written
test_execute_write_failure_returns_error: FileWriter error propagates
```

Run: `go test ./internal/bootstrap/... -run TestExecute` → should FAIL

### GREEN Phase

1. Create content generator functions in `internal/bootstrap/infrastructure/content.go`
2. Add `FileWriter` field to `BootstrapHandler` struct
3. Update `NewBootstrapHandler` to accept FileWriter (4th param)
4. Wire file writing into `Execute`: iterate `session.Preview().FileActions()`, write CREATE-only files
5. Use `context.Background()` for FileWriter calls (matches publisher pattern at L137)
6. Update `runInit` in init.go: Preview → display plan → Confirm → Execute → call `runGuide` inline
7. Add `--dry-run` to init path (show preview, exit before Confirm)

### REFACTOR Phase

- Ensure content generators are pure functions (no side effects)
- Verify ubiquitous language matches docs/DDD.md

## Steps

1. Write content generator functions + tests in `internal/bootstrap/infrastructure/content.go`
2. Add FileWriter to BootstrapHandler — update constructor signature
3. Update ALL 9 test call sites in `bootstrap_handler_test.go` (L142, 169, 189, 203, 232, 250, 272, 293, 313) to pass mock FileWriter
4. Wire file writing into Execute: iterate `session.Preview().FileActions()`, write CREATE-only
5. Add new Execute tests: writes files, skips existing, handles write errors
6. Update composition root at `app.go:165` — pass existing `fileWriter` as 4th arg
7. Update `runInit` in `init.go`: add Confirm → Execute → call `runGuide(cmd.Context(), app, false)`
8. Add `--dry-run` handling to non-rescue init path
9. Run quality gates

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `BootstrapHandler.Execute` calls `FileWriter.WriteFile` for each planned file marked CREATE
- [ ] `.alty/config.toml` content is valid TOML with project name
- [ ] `.alty/knowledge/_index.toml` content has RLM scaffold structure
- [ ] `.alty/maintenance/doc-registry.toml` tracks PRD.md, DDD.md, ARCHITECTURE.md
- [ ] Files marked Skip in preview are NOT written
- [ ] `alty init` runs full flow: Preview → Confirm → Execute → Guide
- [ ] `alty init --dry-run` shows preview and exits (no writes, no guide)
- [ ] All 9 existing test call sites updated and passing
- [ ] Composition root compiles and `app_test.go` passes

## Edge Cases

| Case | Input | Expected Output |
|------|-------|-----------------|
| All files exist | Every planned file on disk | Zero writes, all Skip |
| Partial overlap | Some files exist, some don't | Only missing files written |
| Write failure | FileWriter returns error | Execute returns wrapped error, session not completed |
| User declines confirm | Cancel after preview | No files written, no guide |
| --dry-run | Flag set | Preview displayed, exit 0, no writes |

## Quality Gates

```bash
go build ./...
go vet ./...
golangci-lint run ./...
go test ./... -race
```

- [ ] Lint passes
- [ ] All tests pass with >= 80% coverage
- [ ] Edge cases have test coverage

## Pre-Implementation Validation

- [x] `sharedapp.FileWriter` at shared/application/ports.go:28-31 — confirmed, single method `WriteFile(ctx, path, content)`
- [x] FileWriter adapter at `shared/infrastructure/persistence/filesystem_file_writer.go` — confirmed exists
- [x] Composition root `fileWriter` at app.go:103-104 — confirmed, reuse as 4th arg at L165
- [x] `Execute` at bootstrap_handler.go:125 has no ctx — use `context.Background()` (matches publisher at L137)
- [x] 9 test call sites at bootstrap_handler_test.go (L142, 169, 189, 203, 232, 250, 272, 293, 313) — all need mock FileWriter
- [x] `runGuide` at guide.go:37 is a standalone function — can call inline from `runInit`
- [x] `app_test.go:21-41` asserts all handlers non-nil — auto-validates composition wiring

## Risks / Dependencies

- Adding FileWriter as 4th param to `NewBootstrapHandler` changes constructor — 9 test call sites + composition root + any MCP wiring must update
- TOML content generated as plain strings (no TOML library needed for generation; only for validation in tests)
- `runInit` calling `runGuide` inline means init needs access to `cmd.Context()` and TUI flags

title: Epic: Project Directory & Init Completion
description:
## Goal / Problem

`alty init` is the core user-facing command — it turns an idea into a production-ready project. Nine epics have delivered the domain logic (discovery, fitness, tickets, challenge, complexity, MCP) but the **init output pipeline has gaps** that prevent a user from running `alty init` and getting a complete, working project:

1. **`.alty/` directory not generated** — PRD §5.1 defines a per-project `.alty/` directory (`config.toml`, `knowledge/`, `maintenance/doc-registry.toml`). The bootstrap handler's `plannedFiles` list references these 3 files (bootstrap_handler.go:34-36), and the preview shows them, but **no infrastructure adapter writes the actual file content**. The user sees them in the plan but gets nothing on disk.

2. **Gap analysis not standalone** — PRD P0 requires: "scan existing project, compare against full alty structure, report what's missing/conflicting." The rescue context (`internal/rescue/domain/gap_analysis.go`) has the domain logic, but it's only reachable via `alty init --existing`. There's no `alty gap` command for users who want to see what's missing without committing to a full rescue flow.

These are the last P0 capability gaps against PRD.md §5 before alty can deliver its core promise end-to-end.

## DDD Alignment

| Bounded Context | Impact |
|----------------|--------|
| Bootstrap | Add file writers for `.alty/` directory contents (`config.toml`, knowledge index, doc-registry) |
| Rescue | Expose gap analysis as standalone query (reuse existing domain logic) |
| Shared | FileWriter port may need new adapters for TOML generation |

## Success Metrics

- `alty init` on a fresh directory creates a valid `.alty/` directory with `config.toml`, `knowledge/_index.toml`, and `maintenance/doc-registry.toml`
- `alty gap` runs standalone on any project directory and produces a gap report
- Both commands have integration tests
- Quality gates pass: go build, go vet, golangci-lint, go test -race

## Scope

**In scope**

- Infrastructure adapter to write `.alty/config.toml` with sensible defaults
- Infrastructure adapter to write `.alty/knowledge/_index.toml` (RLM index scaffold)
- Infrastructure adapter to write `.alty/maintenance/doc-registry.toml` (doc tracking scaffold)
- New `alty gap` CLI command that reuses rescue context's GapAnalysis domain logic
- Integration tests for both capabilities
- Verify `alty init` end-to-end produces all planned files

**Out of scope**

- Full knowledge base content population (`.alty/knowledge/ddd/`, `.alty/knowledge/tools/` — that's a separate epic for knowledge seeding)
- Deep mode discovery wiring (P1)
- Tool knowledge versioning (P1)
- Multi-tool config content (already handled by tooltranslation context)

## Phases / Milestones

1. Phase 1 — `.alty/` directory generation (write adapters + wire into bootstrap flow)
2. Phase 2 — Standalone gap analysis command (`alty gap`)
3. Phase 3 — Integration tests + end-to-end validation

## Child Tasks (planned)

1. Add TOML file writer adapters for `.alty/config.toml`, `knowledge/_index.toml`, `maintenance/doc-registry.toml`
2. Wire `.alty/` file generation into bootstrap handler's Execute flow
3. Add `alty gap` CLI command reusing rescue context's GapAnalysis
4. Integration tests for `.alty/` output and gap command

## Dependencies

- Epic alty-cli-ped (Config Generation Output) — COMPLETED (bootstrap handler exists)
- Epic alty-cli-ojl (Rescue Mode) — COMPLETED (gap analysis domain logic exists)

## Risks / Unknowns

- TOML generation — need to decide on library (BurntSushi/toml vs pelletier/go-toml) or use simple string templates
- `config.toml` schema — PRD defines the directory but not the exact config keys; need to define minimal viable schema
- Gap analysis reuse — rescue handler may need refactoring to extract the query path from the command path

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `alty init` in a fresh directory creates `.alty/config.toml` with valid TOML content
- [ ] `alty init` creates `.alty/knowledge/_index.toml` with RLM scaffold
- [ ] `alty init` creates `.alty/maintenance/doc-registry.toml` with doc tracking scaffold
- [ ] `alty gap` runs standalone and reports missing files, configs, and structure
- [ ] `alty gap` reuses rescue context domain logic (no duplication)
- [ ] All new code has unit tests (>= 80% coverage)
- [ ] Integration tests verify end-to-end file creation
- [ ] Quality gates pass: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `go test ./... -race`

title: Add classification questions to alty guide flow
description:
## Summary
Integrate subdomain classification questions into the `alty guide` discovery flow, following the Khononov decision tree from the research spike.

## Background
Research spike `docs/research/20260222_subdomain_classification_complexity_budget.md` defines:
1. BUY question: "Could you use an existing product without losing competitive advantage?"
2. COMPLEXITY question: "Is it mostly CRUD or complex rules?"
3. COMPETITOR question: "If copied exactly, would it threaten your business?"

These questions should be asked **per bounded context** after Q9 (boundary identification) is answered.

## Design

### New Question Phase
Add `PhaseClassification` after `PhaseBoundaries`. Classification questions are asked for EACH bounded context identified in Q9.

### New Questions (per bounded context)
For each bounded context discovered in Q9:
```
Q-CLASS-1 (BUY): "For [context name], could you use an off-the-shelf solution 
                  without losing what makes your business special?"
  → YES: GENERIC
  → NO: continue

Q-CLASS-2 (COMPLEXITY): "When your team talks about [context name], is it 
                         mostly storing/retrieving data, or are there 
                         complex rules and special cases?"
  → "Mostly storing/retrieving": SUPPORTING  
  → "Complex rules": CORE

Q-CLASS-3 (VALIDATE): "If a competitor copied [context name] exactly, 
                       would that threaten your business?"
  → YES: confirms CORE
  → NO + was CORE: reconsider SUPPORTING
```

### Domain Changes (internal/discovery/domain/)

**discovery_values.go:**
- Add `PhaseClassification QuestionPhase = "classification"` constant
- Update `AllQuestionPhases()` to include classification after boundaries

**classification_question.go (NEW):**
- `ClassificationQuestion` struct with context-aware text generation
- `ClassificationDecisionTree` that implements Khononov logic
- `ClassificationResult` value object (classification + rationale)

**discovery_session.go:**
- Add `contextClassifications map[string]ClassificationResult` field
- Add `ClassifyBoundedContext(contextName string, result ClassificationResult) error` command
- Add `ContextClassifications() map[string]ClassificationResult` accessor
- Modify `Complete()` to require all Q9 contexts have classifications

**discovery_events.go:**
- Add `BoundedContextClassified` domain event with fields:
  - `sessionID string`
  - `contextName string`
  - `classification vo.SubdomainClassification`
  - `rationale string`

### Application Changes (internal/discovery/application/)

**discovery_handler.go:**
- Add `ClassifyBoundedContext(sessionID, contextName string, result domain.ClassificationResult) error`
- This is the existing handler (not "GuideHandler" — that doesn't exist)

**ports.go:**
- Add `ClassifyBoundedContext` method to `Discovery` interface

### Sequence Diagram
```
User completes Q9 (boundaries) → Session enters PhaseClassification
  ↓
For each context in Q9 answer:
  Prompter.AskQuestion(Q-CLASS-1 for context)
    → If YES: classify as GENERIC, emit BoundedContextClassified, next context
    → If NO: continue
  Prompter.AskQuestion(Q-CLASS-2 for context)
    → "Mostly CRUD": classify as SUPPORTING
    → "Complex rules": preliminary CORE
  Prompter.AskQuestion(Q-CLASS-3 for context)
    → Confirm or downgrade CORE → SUPPORTING
  Session.ClassifyBoundedContext(contextName, result)
  Emit BoundedContextClassified event
  ↓
All contexts classified → Session can Complete()
```

## Files to Create
- internal/discovery/domain/classification_question.go

## Files to Modify
- internal/discovery/domain/discovery_values.go (add PhaseClassification)
- internal/discovery/domain/discovery_session.go (add classification storage + command)
- internal/discovery/domain/discovery_events.go (add BoundedContextClassified)
- internal/discovery/application/discovery_handler.go (add ClassifyBoundedContext)
- internal/discovery/application/ports.go (add to Discovery interface)

## TDD Plan

### RED Phase
1. `TestDiscoverySession_ClassifyBoundedContext_StoresClassification`
2. `TestDiscoverySession_ClassifyBoundedContext_EmitsBoundedContextClassified`
3. `TestDiscoverySession_Complete_FailsWithoutAllClassifications`
4. `TestClassificationDecisionTree_BuyYes_ReturnsGeneric`
5. `TestClassificationDecisionTree_ComplexitySimple_ReturnsSupporting`
6. `TestClassificationDecisionTree_CompetitorYes_ReturnsCore`

### GREEN Phase
Implement minimal code to pass each test.

### REFACTOR Phase
Extract decision tree logic into reusable `ClassificationDecisionTree`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `PhaseClassification` phase exists and is ordered after `PhaseBoundaries`
- [ ] Classification questions asked for each bounded context from Q9
- [ ] `ClassifyBoundedContext` command stores result in session
- [ ] `BoundedContextClassified` event emitted per context
- [ ] Plain-language questions (no DDD jargon for non-technical persona)
- [ ] Session completion blocked until all Q9 contexts classified
- [ ] golangci-lint passes with 0 issues

## Dependencies
- alty-cli-r3i.1 (ARCHITECTURE.md refresh — CLOSED)
close_reason: Implemented classification questions: ClassificationResult VO, ClassificationDecisionTree with Khononov logic, BoundedContextClassifiedEvent, ClassifyBoundedContext command on DiscoverySession, snapshot serialization. 12 tests, all quality gates pass.

title: Missing cross-context isolation rules in .golangci.yml
description:
## Summary

Current depguard config enforces layer boundaries (domain cannot import infrastructure) but does NOT prevent cross-context imports (bootstrap importing discovery internals).

**Resolution:** This will be fixed as part of the arch-go migration (epic alty-cli-awl). arch-go's `shouldNotDependsOn` rules will handle cross-context isolation:

```yaml
- package: "github.com/alty-cli/alty/internal/bootstrap/**"
  shouldNotDependsOn:
    internal:
      - "github.com/alty-cli/alty/internal/discovery/**"
      - "github.com/alty-cli/alty/internal/challenge/**"
```

## Impact

A developer could accidentally import `internal/discovery/domain/...` from `internal/bootstrap/...` and linter would not catch it.

## Fix

Implemented in ticket alty-cli-awl.2 (RenderArchGoYAML) which generates cross-context isolation rules from the bounded context map.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] arch-go.yml has cross-context isolation rules
- [ ] Rules match DDD.md context map relationships
- [ ] `arch-go` catches deliberate cross-context imports
close_reason: Fixed by alty-cli-awl.2 - RenderArchGoYAML now generates cross-context isolation rules from BoundedContextMap relationships

description:
## Summary

Add `alty fitness generate` CLI command that generates architecture fitness function configuration.

## Commands

- `alty fitness generate` — generates arch-go.yml with user confirmation
- `alty fitness generate --preview` — shows what will be generated without writing
- `alty fitness generate --brownfield` — generates with 80% compliance threshold

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Command registered in cmd/alty/fitness.go
- [ ] Delegates to FitnessGenerationHandler

design:
## Design

### DomainModel Source

CLI loads DomainModel from `.alty/bounded_context_map.yaml`:
1. Parse YAML with `BoundedContextMapParser` 
2. Convert `BoundedContextMap` → minimal `DomainModel` with contexts + relationships
3. Pass to `FitnessGenerationHandler.BuildPreview()`

### StackProfile Detection

Detect stack from project files:
- `go.mod` present → `GoModProfile{}`
- `pyproject.toml` present → `PythonUvProfile{}`
- Neither → `GenericProfile{}` (fitness unavailable)

### Command Flow

```
alty fitness generate [--preview] [--brownfield]
  1. Detect project dir (cwd)
  2. Parse .alty/bounded_context_map.yaml → BoundedContextMap
  3. Convert to DomainModel
  4. Detect StackProfile
  5. Call BuildPreview(model, projectName, profile, opts)
  6. If --preview: print YAMLContent and exit
  7. Else: confirm with user, call WriteFiles()
```

### Constructor Chain

```
app.FitnessGenerationHandler (from composition.App)
  → NewFitnessGenerationHandler(fileWriter, publisher) at app.go:167
  → BuildPreview(model, name, profile, &BuildPreviewOptions{Threshold: 80}) for brownfield
  → WriteFiles(ctx, preview, projectDir)
```

Uses BoundedContextMapParser to load contexts and FitnessGenerationHandler.BuildPreview for generation. All quality gates pass.

title: Implement RenderArchGoYAML in FitnessTestSuite
description:
## Summary

Add `RenderArchGoYAML(bcMap *BoundedContextMap, threshold int) (string, error)` method to FitnessTestSuite aggregate to generate arch-go configuration from bounded context definitions.

**Tool choice:** arch-go (MIT) instead of go-arch-lint. arch-go has both `shouldOnlyDependsOn` AND `shouldNotDependsOn` rules — no need for a second tool like depguard.

## Output Format

```yaml
version: 1
threshold:
  compliance: 100  # or 80 for brownfield
  coverage: 100

dependenciesRules:
  - package: "**.domain.**"
    shouldOnlyDependsOn:
      internal: ["**.domain.**", "**.shared.domain.**"]
      external: ["$gostd"]
    shouldNotDependsOn:
      internal: ["**.application.**", "**.infrastructure.**"]

  - package: "**.application.**"
    shouldNotDependsOn:
      internal: ["**.infrastructure.**"]

  # Cross-context isolation (from BoundedContextMap relationships)
  - package: "**/bootstrap/**"
    shouldNotDependsOn:
      internal: ["**/discovery/**"]  # Unless relationship allows it
```

## Design

### Method Signature
```go
func (s *FitnessTestSuite) RenderArchGoYAML(bcMap *BoundedContextMap, threshold int) (string, error)
```

### Parameters
- `bcMap`: BoundedContextMap from alty-cli-awl.7, provides:
  - `Contexts()` → []BoundedContextEntry (name, modulePath, classification, layers, relationships)
  - `RootPackage()` → string (e.g., "github.com/alty-cli/alty")
- `threshold`: Compliance percentage (100 for greenfield, 80 for brownfield)

### Cross-Context Isolation Rules
For each context in bcMap:
1. If context A has NO relationship to context B → generate shouldNotDependsOn rule
2. If context A has upstream relationship to B → A may depend on B (no rule)
3. If context A has downstream relationship to B → B should not depend on A

### Data Flow
```
BoundedContextMap.Contexts() → []BoundedContextEntry
  → For each entry:
     - entry.Classification() → layer strictness rules
     - entry.Relationships() → cross-context isolation rules
  → Render as YAML string
```

## TDD Phases

### RED — Write failing tests first
File: `internal/fitness/domain/fitness_test_suite_test.go`

| Test Name | Scenario |
|-----------|----------|
| `TestFitnessTestSuite_RenderArchGoYAML_ValidOutput` | Happy path with 2 contexts |
| `TestFitnessTestSuite_RenderArchGoYAML_DomainLayerRules` | shouldOnlyDependsOn for domain |
| `TestFitnessTestSuite_RenderArchGoYAML_ApplicationLayerRules` | shouldNotDependsOn infra |
| `TestFitnessTestSuite_RenderArchGoYAML_CrossContextIsolation` | Contexts without relationship |
| `TestFitnessTestSuite_RenderArchGoYAML_AllowedRelationship` | Upstream relationship allows dep |
| `TestFitnessTestSuite_RenderArchGoYAML_ThresholdGreenfield` | threshold=100 |
| `TestFitnessTestSuite_RenderArchGoYAML_ThresholdBrownfield` | threshold=80 |
| `TestFitnessTestSuite_RenderArchGoYAML_EmptyMap` | Error on empty BoundedContextMap |

### GREEN — Minimal implementation
Implement RenderArchGoYAML following pattern from RenderImportLinterTOML (line 182-232)

### REFACTOR — Clean up
Extract helper methods if YAML generation becomes complex

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] RenderArchGoYAML() generates valid arch-go.yml
- [ ] Domain layer rules use shouldOnlyDependsOn for positive model
- [ ] Domain layer rules use shouldNotDependsOn for negative model  
- [ ] Cross-context isolation rules generated from BoundedContextMap relationships
- [ ] Supports threshold parameter for brownfield (80%) vs greenfield (100%)
- [ ] Tests cover happy path and edge cases (8 tests minimum)
- [ ] Quality gates pass

```go
// internal/ticket/application/ports.go

    CreateEpic(ctx context.Context, title, description string) (epicID string, err error)
```

title: Implement ConflictDetectingFileWriter adapter
description:
## Goal / Problem

PRD requires "Never overwrite" existing files. Current `FilesystemFileWriter` blindly overwrites. Need a decorator that detects conflicts and renames alty-generated files to `*_alty.ext`.

## Background / Context

- PRD Section 5.2: "If target file exists, skip it" and "If alty needs to create a conflicting file, suffix ours: filename_alty.md"
- `FileWriter` port at [internal/shared/application/ports.go:21](internal/shared/application/ports.go#L21)
- `FilesystemFileWriter` at [internal/shared/infrastructure/persistence/filesystem_file_writer.go:20](internal/shared/infrastructure/persistence/filesystem_file_writer.go#L20)
- Wired at [internal/composition/app.go:98](internal/composition/app.go#L98): `fileWriter := persistence.NewFilesystemFileWriter()`
- **Pattern reference:** Decorator pattern - wrap inner FileWriter

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Shared (infrastructure) |
| Ubiquitous Language | ConflictStrategy, FileConflict, ConflictDetectingFileWriter |
| Layer | Infrastructure (decorator adapter) |

## Design

### Data Models

| Model | Type | Location | Purpose |
|-------|------|----------|---------|
| `ConflictStrategy` | Enum (string) | `shared/domain/valueobjects/` | Skip, Rename |
| `FileConflict` | Value Object | `shared/domain/valueobjects/` | originalPath, actualPath, strategy |
| `ConflictDetectingFileWriter` | Adapter | `shared/infrastructure/persistence/` | Wraps FileWriter |

### Interface (must match existing FileWriter)

```go
// FileWriter interface (existing - do not modify)
type FileWriter interface {
    WriteFile(ctx context.Context, path string, content string) error
}

// ConflictDetectingFileWriter (new)
type ConflictDetectingFileWriter struct {
    inner     FileWriter
    strategy  ConflictStrategy
    conflicts []FileConflict
}

func (w *ConflictDetectingFileWriter) WriteFile(ctx context.Context, path string, content string) error
func (w *ConflictDetectingFileWriter) Conflicts() []FileConflict
func (w *ConflictDetectingFileWriter) Reset()
```

### Sequence / Flow

```
ConfigGenerationHandler    ConflictDetectingFileWriter    FilesystemFileWriter    OS
        |                            |                           |                |
        |-- WriteFile(path, content)-->                          |                |
        |                            |-- os.Stat(path) ------------------------->|
        |                            |<-- exists=true ----------------------------|
        |                            |                           |                |
        |                            |-- computeRenamedPath(path)|                |
        |                            |   → "path_alty.ext"       |                |
        |                            |                           |                |
        |                            |-- inner.WriteFile(renamed, content) ------>|
        |                            |                           |-- write ------>|
        |                            |                           |<-- ok ---------|
        |                            |<-- ok --------------------|                |
        |                            |                           |                |
        |                            |-- recordConflict(original, actual, Rename) |
        |<-- ok ---------------------|                           |                |
```

### Rename Logic

```go
func computeRenamedPath(path string) string {
    ext := filepath.Ext(path)           // ".md"
    base := strings.TrimSuffix(path, ext) // "/foo/bar/CLAUDE"
    return base + "_alty" + ext         // "/foo/bar/CLAUDE_alty.md"
}

// If _alty already exists, increment: _alty_2, _alty_3, etc.
```

### Wiring Change (composition/app.go line 98)

**Current:**
```go
fileWriter := persistence.NewFilesystemFileWriter()
```

**After:**
```go
innerWriter := persistence.NewFilesystemFileWriter()
fileWriter := persistence.NewConflictDetectingFileWriter(innerWriter, persistence.ConflictStrategyRename)
```

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| **S**ingle Responsibility | Only handles conflict detection/rename |
| **O**pen/Closed | New decorator, doesn't modify FilesystemFileWriter |
| **L**iskov Substitution | Implements FileWriter interface exactly |
| **D**ependency Inversion | Depends on FileWriter interface, not concrete |

## TDD Workflow

### RED Phase

```go
// internal/shared/infrastructure/persistence/conflict_detecting_file_writer_test.go

func TestWriteFile_NoConflict(t *testing.T) {
    // path doesn't exist → write normally, no conflicts recorded
}

    // create file at path → WriteFile → verify written to path_alty.ext
```

title: bug(ticket): BeadsCommentWriter calls 'bd comment add <id>' but real bd CLI is 'bd comment <id> --stdin'
description:
## Symptom

Running `alto ticket-ripple <id>` against a ticket that has open dependents fails:

```
Error: executing command: ripple review: adding ripple comment to <dependent-id>: running bd comment add <dependent-id>: exit status 1
```

The underlying `bd` invocation prints `Error: resolving add: no issue found matching "add"`.

## Root cause

`internal/ticket/infrastructure/beads_comment_writer.go:72` invokes:

```go
exec.CommandContext(ctx, "bd", "comment", "add", ticketID)
```

But the actual `bd comment` CLI signature is `bd comment <id> [text...]` with `--stdin` flag for stdin streaming — there is no `add` subcommand. `bd` interprets the literal `"add"` as another ticket ID argument and fails resolution.

This bug shipped in alty-cli-2f9 (Wave 6). It went undetected because ripple invocations during Wave 6 (2f9 + bf7) and Wave 7a (1r0) all targeted leaf tickets with zero open dependents — the failure path was never exercised. It surfaced on Wave 7b/foundation's first ticket with a real dependent (alty-cli-08q → alty-cli-561 via the new dep wired this session).

## Fix

Change line 72 to:

```go
exec.CommandContext(ctx, "bd", "comment", ticketID, "--stdin")
```

Stdin streaming already works correctly (line 73: `cmd.Stdin = bytes.NewBufferString(body)`). The `--stdin` flag tells bd to consume the body from stdin instead of args.

Update the 6 tests in `beads_comment_writer_test.go` that assert the command shape. The fix is a one-arg-order change; behaviour is otherwise identical.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `internal/ticket/infrastructure/beads_comment_writer.go:72` uses `bd comment <id> --stdin`.
- Existing 6 tests updated to assert the new argv shape; all still pass.
- New RED regression test asserts the literal argv produced by execBDCommentCommand matches `["bd", "comment", "<id>", "--stdin"]` byte-for-byte (the previous tests apparently asserted the wrong shape, so the regression guard must pin the correct one).
- `alto ticket-ripple <ticket-with-open-dependents>` succeeds end-to-end against a real bd binary (smoke test post-fix).

## Source citations

- `internal/ticket/infrastructure/beads_comment_writer.go:72` (the wrong invocation)
- `internal/ticket/infrastructure/beads_comment_writer_test.go` (6 tests that need updating)
- Output of `bd comment --help` (the canonical signature)
close_reason: Fixed in commit a35a2c3. bdCommentArgs(ticketID) helper returns canonical ["bd", "comment", "<id>", "--stdin"] argv; execBDCommentCommand reuses it; wrap-error string now "running bd comment %s". Internal-package regression test pins the argv shape byte-for-byte. End-to-end smoke: alto ticket-ripple alty-cli-08q successfully posted ripple comment to dependent alty-cli-561 (previously errored with 'resolving add: no issue found matching "add"').

title: Spike: LSP + DAP for alto-scaffolded projects (oh-my-pi extraction)
description:
## Research Question

How do we surface project-appropriate LSP + debugger capabilities to agents working inside an alto-scaffolded project, taking inspiration from can1357/oh-my-pi (LSP + DAP wired into every edit) without re-implementing its Rust harness?

The scaffolded project can be ANY language that Claude Code's native LSP supports: TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, C, C++, C#, PHP, Kotlin, Ruby, HTML/CSS. The mechanism must be language-agnostic — driven by the detected primary language from PRD-aware stack detection (alty-cli-yl0).

Sub-questions:

1. What is Claude Code's native LSP surface today (the `LSP` tool: goToDefinition, findReferences, hover, documentSymbol, workspaceSymbol, goToImplementation, prepareCallHierarchy, incomingCalls, outgoingCalls)? How is it enabled per-language, and what plugin marketplaces exist (Piebald-AI/claude-code-lsps, ktnyt/cclsp)?
2. Does Claude Code have native DAP (debugger)? If not, what are the options — vendor an MCP DAP bridge, drive a per-language debugger CLI from Bash through a skill, or punt entirely? Per-language candidates: `node --inspect-brk` / Chrome DevTools Protocol (TS/JS), `debugpy` / `pdb` (Python), `dlv` (Go), `lldb` (Rust, C, C++), `jdb` (Java), `lldb` (C#/.NET via netcoredbg), Xdebug (PHP), Kotlin debugger (JVM), `rdbg` (Ruby).
3. Which of oh-my-pi's 13 LSP ops + 27 DAP ops translate to a usable subset for agents driven by Claude Code? Where is the ceiling (rename_file workspace edits? format-on-write? diagnostics-on-edit hook?)?
4. Since alto is a scaffold, how should the scaffolded project DECLARE its primary language so the alto-generated agent prompts (`alto-scaffold/agents/developer.md`, `alto-scaffold/commands/rca.md`, `alto-scaffold/commands/review.md`) reference the right LSP plugin AND the right debugger CLI? Tie-in with existing PRD-aware stack detection (alty-cli-yl0, just shipped). The seam must scale to all 11 languages without per-language hardcoding in alto's core.
5. Should the LSP/debugger guidance ship as new skills (`alto-scaffold/skills/lsp-navigate`, `alto-scaffold/skills/debug`) — slash-command-style entry points — or as inline guidance overlays on the existing developer/rca/review assets, or both?
6. **LSP-as-agent-tool thesis** — how do we re-cast the `LSP` tool as a first-class part of the developer and tech-lead agent toolbox, so agents default to *semantic, language-aware* operations instead of text/string search? Search via `workspaceSymbol`/`findReferences` is ONE example; the broader thesis covers blast-radius analysis, impact analysis before refactor, dependency understanding, dead-code detection, call-hierarchy mapping, type-aware navigation, and rename safety.

## Timebox

**Timebox:** 1 day (8 hours)

## Background / Context

- can1357/oh-my-pi (~27k lines of Rust) wires LSP into every write and runs DAP debugger sessions natively. Its key selling points are: format-on-write via language server, diagnostics-on-edit, 27 debug ops (set breakpoints, step, inspect threads/stack/variables, attach to live processes), 13 LSP ops, project-scoped workspace walker.
- Claude Code 2.0.74 (Dec 2025) shipped native LSP support — 11 languages out of the box: TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, C, C++, C#, PHP, Kotlin, Ruby, HTML/CSS. The `LSP` tool exposes 9 ops directly. Latency: ~50ms vs ~45s for grep on large codebases.
- Claude Code does NOT ship native DAP. The debugger ceiling for alto-scaffolded projects today is: bash-driven per-language CLI (`node --inspect-brk` for TS/JS, `debugpy` for Python, `dlv` for Go, `lldb` for Rust/C/C++, etc.) or an MCP bridge.
- alto is a scaffold-the-architect-runs-before-builders. It does not run debuggers itself; it produces guardrails that teach downstream agents in scaffolded projects to USE the right tooling for the detected language. Whatever this spike recommends must work for a TypeScript Next.js app, a Rust CLI, a C systems project, a Python ML script, and a Go service — without forking alto's core.
- Existing PRD-aware stack detection (closed in alty-cli-yl0) already infers primary language from README/PRD. That is the natural hook to drive per-language LSP plugin selection and per-language debugger guidance.
- Existing agents/commands that should plug into this: `alto-scaffold/agents/developer.md` (writes code — should use LSP for navigation), `alto-scaffold/commands/rca.md` (root cause — benefits from debugger), `alto-scaffold/commands/review.md` (review — benefits from findReferences blast-radius).
- **Today's anti-pattern:** agents reflexively use `grep`/`rg`/`Read` for ANY code question, even when the question is semantic ("where is this method called from?", "what implements this interface?", "what does this symbol resolve to in this scope?"). LSP answers these in 50ms with type-correct results; grep returns false positives across comments, strings, and shadowed identifiers. The new research note exists to flip this default for the developer + tech-lead profiles.

## Investigation Approach

1. **Survey Claude Code's LSP surface** across all 11 supported languages. Read https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference, the Piebald-AI/claude-code-lsps marketplace, ktnyt/cclsp MCP. Map each LSP op to a concrete `LSP` tool call. Document what ops require which plugin and what fails gracefully when no LSP is configured. Note any language with partial coverage (e.g. HTML/CSS has different ops than Go).
2. **Survey the DAP gap per language.** Verify Claude Code has no native DAP. For each of the 11 languages, name the canonical CLI debugger and its scriptable invocation surface. Evaluate 3 fill-gap options: (a) MCP DAP bridge — survey existing servers, evaluate language coverage, (b) per-language bash-driven debug skills — write a thin skill per language family (V8/Node, Python, Go, LLVM-family for Rust/C/C++, JVM for Java/Kotlin, etc.), (c) skip — punt to "use printf and tests" and document the tradeoff.
3. **Extract the oh-my-pi essence.** Read its README + DEVELOPMENT.md. List what is genuinely transferable as PROMPT GUIDANCE for a Claude Code agent vs what requires its Rust harness (format-on-write hook, diagnostics-on-edit hook, workspace walker). The transferable part becomes scaffold content.
4. **Design the scaffold-side integration.** The DESIGN must be one mechanism that works for all 11 languages — likely a per-language data table consumed by the asset emitter. Sketch how a scaffolded TypeScript project differs from a scaffolded Rust project differs from a scaffolded C project: which LSP plugin gets installed, what the `developer.project.md` overlay says about LSP usage, what `rca.project.md` says about the debugger, how the discovery layer signals the primary language to the asset emitter.
5. **Prototype at least 2 languages end-to-end** to prove the mechanism is language-agnostic. Pick from across the families: one V8/Node (TypeScript), one native (Go OR Rust). Write a candidate `alto-scaffold/skills/lsp-navigate.md` skill that wraps the most useful LSP ops, and a candidate `alto-scaffold/skills/debug.md` skill that switches debugger CLI on detected language. Try them on a representative codebase per language.
6. **Decide skill vs overlay.** Settle: do LSP/debug ship as new skill assets, as overlay edits to developer/rca/review, or both? Document the seam — and make sure the seam doesn't require alto core changes when a 12th language gets added.
7. **Write the LSP-as-agent-tool note.** Produce `docs/research/YYYYMMDD_lsp-as-agent-tool.md` aimed at the developer + tech-lead profiles. The note positions LSP semantic ops as the *default* code-interrogation tool, with text search relegated to the fallback when no language server is configured or when the question is genuinely textual (e.g. searching comments, README content, log strings). Enumerate at least 5 concrete agent use cases with worked examples (tool-call snippets):
   - **Blast-radius / impact analysis** before edit — `findReferences` + `incomingCalls`
   - **Refactor planning** — `prepareCallHierarchy` → `outgoingCalls` to walk the touched subgraph
   - **Interface implementation discovery** — `goToImplementation` instead of grepping `func.*ReceiverType`
   - **Dependency / coupling map** — `documentSymbol` across changed files to surface architectural drift
   - **Type-aware definition resolution** — `goToDefinition` + `hover` instead of guessing which `Foo` the symbol binds to
   - **Dead-code candidates** — `findReferences` returning 0 hits across the workspace
   - **Cross-file rename safety** — `findReferences` precursor to any string replace
   Each example shows the wrong (grep) vs right (LSP) approach side-by-side, the input file:line and the structured output shape. Conclude with a decision rubric the developer/tech-lead profile injects into its system prompt: "When the question is about a symbol, type, function, or reference — call `LSP` first. Use grep ONLY when the LSP tool returns no language-server-configured for the file, or when the question is textual."

## Research Guidelines

Please investigate and provide a clear research report with:

1. **Use Context7** for the Claude Code plugin marketplace API, MCP DAP servers, and per-language debugger CLI docs
2. **Web search** with year 2026 for Claude Code 2.x LSP changes and DAP MCP options
3. **Structured findings** — pros/cons table per option (skill vs overlay, MCP DAP vs bash debug, per-language plugin selection mechanism). Include a per-language coverage matrix: LSP plugin available? Debugger CLI scriptable? Any caveats?
4. **Clear recommendation** — name the path forward, including which files in alto-scaffold/ get touched in follow-up tickets
5. **Follow-up tickets** — file P2 implementation ticket(s) for the chosen path. Slice by mechanism (the language-agnostic seam) FIRST, then dogfood tickets per language family

## Expected Deliverables

- [ ] Research report at docs/research/YYYYMMDD_lsp-dap-for-scaffolded-projects.md (no absolute home paths per CLAUDE.md privacy rules)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All 6 research questions answered with citations
- [ ] Per-language matrix covers TS, Python, Go, Rust, Java, C, C++, C#, PHP, Kotlin, Ruby, HTML/CSS
- [ ] Decision tree captured: how does the scaffolded project's detected primary language drive (a) which LSP plugin the user is told to install, (b) which debugger sequence the developer/rca skills reference? The seam works for all 11 languages without per-language hardcoding in alto core
- [ ] Skill vs overlay decision is settled with a written rationale and approved by user before implementation tickets are filed

Note MUST: (a) state the thesis — agents default to LSP semantic ops over text/string search whenever the question is about a symbol, type, function, or reference; (b) enumerate at least 5 concrete agent use cases beyond simple search (blast-radius, refactor planning, interface implementation discovery, dependency/coupling map, type-aware definition resolution, dead-code detection, cross-file rename safety — pick at least 5); (c) for each use case show the grep/string-based approach side-by-side with the LSP-based approach including concrete `LSP` tool-call snippets and structured output examples; (d) end with a decision rubric ready to drop into the developer.md and tech-lead.md profiles' system prompts that tells the agent WHEN to reach for LSP vs WHEN to fall back to grep

title: feat(bootstrap): alto init scaffolds .beads/hooks/post-close that calls alto ticket-ripple
description:
## Goal / Problem

After alty-cli-2f9 ships the `alto ticket-ripple` subcommand, this ticket makes it fire automatically. `alto init --with-scaffold` writes `.beads/hooks/post-close` (and a Windows `.bat` shim) that invokes `alto ticket-ripple "$@"` so every `bd close` triggers ripple review without manual intervention, regardless of which tool/session ran the close (CLI, MCP, agent, or human).

Source: Superseded portion of alty-cli-i80 (Path A, hook-scaffold half). Original i80 closed as superseded.

## Background / Context

- alty-cli-2f9 (DEPENDS-ON): productizes the ripple flow as `alto ticket-ripple` Go subcommand.
- Beads honors hook scripts at `.beads/hooks/<event>` per beads documentation (see `docs/reference/beads-knowledge.md` for current local notes).
- Existing project-local workaround `bin/bd-close-hook` is a Claude-Code-only PostToolUse hook; this ticket replaces it with a tool-agnostic beads-native hook that fires in any session.
- alty-cli-6n4 (independent) restores the existing bash workaround in-repo until this ticket lands; that hook also references the new `.beads/hooks/post-close` path once present and falls back to manual call.

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Bootstrap (existing) |
| Ubiquitous Language | `scaffold`, `hook`, `BootstrapHandler.WriteScaffold` (existing surface) |
| Layer | Extends Bootstrap application + infrastructure. Adds one scaffold step. Domain unaffected. |
| Aggregate boundary | `ScaffoldParams` aggregate already governs the write — additive flag `IncludeHooks bool` (default true) |

## Design

### New scaffold step

`internal/bootstrap/application/bootstrap_handler.go` — `WriteScaffold` gains a step after `EmbedScaffoldWriter.WriteScaffold` returns:

```
if params.IncludeHooks {
    hookWriter.WriteBeadsPostCloseHook(ctx, targetDir, params.PrimaryTool)
}
```

### New port

`internal/bootstrap/application/ports.go` — additive:

```
type BeadsHookWriter interface {
    WriteBeadsPostCloseHook(ctx context.Context, targetDir string, primaryTool string) error
}
```

### Adapter

`internal/bootstrap/infrastructure/filesystem_beads_hook_writer.go` writes two files (when on Unix) or one + bat (when on Windows):

- `<targetDir>/.beads/hooks/post-close` — executable POSIX shell script: `#!/usr/bin/env bash\nexec alto ticket-ripple "$@"`
- `<targetDir>/.beads/hooks/post-close.bat` — Windows shim: `@echo off\nalto ticket-ripple %*`

The POSIX file gets 0o755 via `f.Chmod(mode)` on the open O_NOFOLLOW fd — same TOCTOU pattern alty-cli-766.6 used for `alto-scaffold/scripts/bd-ripple`.

### CLI flag

`cmd/alto/commands/init.go` — additive:

```
cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&noHooks, "no-hooks", false, "With --with-scaffold: skip writing .beads/hooks/* (advanced opt-out)")
cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&forceHooks, "force-hooks", false, "With --with-scaffold: overwrite existing .beads/hooks/post-close")
```

`IncludeHooks = !noHooks` threads into `ScaffoldParams`.

### Conflict handling

If `.beads/hooks/post-close` already exists and content differs from alto's template:
- Default: abort with a diff message ("hook exists; review and re-run with --force-hooks to overwrite").
- `--force-hooks`: overwrite (announced via [OVERWRITE] preview line, same channel as scaffold preview — leverages alty-cli-qh5's `WithPreviewWriter` once that lands; until then `os.Stderr`).
- `--no-hooks`: skip entirely.

If `.beads/` doesn't exist yet:
- bootstrap's existing dir-creation step runs `os.MkdirAll(targetDir + "/.beads/hooks", 0o755)`.

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| S | `BeadsHookWriter` has one job: render the hook + bat shim. Separate from `ScaffoldWriter` (which handles `alto-scaffold/` extraction). |
| O | New port, no modification to `ScaffoldWriter`. Future hook events (pre-create, post-update) drop in by extending the same port. |
| L | The adapter honors port semantics for both OS variants. |
| I | Narrow 1-method interface. |
| D | `BootstrapHandler` depends on `BeadsHookWriter` interface, not the filesystem adapter directly. |

## TDD Workflow

### RED Phase — tests by name

Adapter unit tests (`filesystem_beads_hook_writer_test.go`, tempdir):
- `TestBeadsHookWriter_Write_CreatesExecutablePostCloseHook`
- `TestBeadsHookWriter_Write_PostCloseHookExitsExecAltoTicketRipple`
- `TestBeadsHookWriter_Write_OnWindows_WritesBatShim`
- `TestBeadsHookWriter_Write_WhenHookExistsAndSame_NoOp`
- `TestBeadsHookWriter_Write_WhenHookExistsAndDiffers_ReturnsErrAlreadyExists`
- `TestBeadsHookWriter_Write_WhenForce_OverwritesExisting`
- `TestBeadsHookWriter_Write_CreatesParentDirectoriesIfMissing`
- `TestBeadsHookWriter_Write_FileMode_Is0o755`

Bootstrap handler tests (port mocks):
- `TestBootstrapHandler_WriteScaffold_WhenIncludeHooks_CallsHookWriter`
- `TestBootstrapHandler_WriteScaffold_WhenNoHooks_SkipsHookWriter`
- `TestBootstrapHandler_WriteScaffold_WhenHookWriterFails_ReturnsWrappedError`

CLI tests (Cobra):
- `TestInitCmd_NoHooksFlag_DisablesHookScaffold`
- `TestInitCmd_ForceHooksFlag_PassesThroughToParams`

Smoke test (manual / integration):
- Run `alto init --with-scaffold --project-name=tmp --ticket-prefix=tmp- --primary-tool=claude --target-dir=$TMPDIR` (depends on alty-cli-hgj for --target-dir; until that lands, use cwd of a tempdir).
- Run `bd init && bd create --title test` then `bd close <id>` and confirm `alto ticket-ripple` fires from the hook.

### GREEN Phase

1. Define `BeadsHookWriter` port in `internal/bootstrap/application/ports.go`.
2. Implement `FilesystemBeadsHookWriter` in `internal/bootstrap/infrastructure/filesystem_beads_hook_writer.go`.
3. Add `IncludeHooks bool` (default true) to `ScaffoldParams` in `internal/bootstrap/domain/`.
4. Wire the hook step into `BootstrapHandler.WriteScaffold`.
5. Add `--no-hooks` and `--force-hooks` flags + threading in `cmd/alto/commands/init.go`.
6. Wire `hookWriter` adapter in `internal/composition/app.go`.

### REFACTOR Phase

- Verify the template strings (POSIX + bat) are defined as untyped string constants near the adapter; not inline.
- Verify `[OVERWRITE]` preview path matches the writer's existing behavior at `embed_scaffold_writer.go:107`.
- Verify arch-go reports zero new cross-context imports.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `alto init --with-scaffold` (default behavior) writes `.beads/hooks/post-close` (Unix) AND `.beads/hooks/post-close.bat` (Windows-cross-compile-only check; smoke test runs current platform only)
- POSIX hook file contents are `#!/usr/bin/env bash\nexec alto ticket-ripple "$@"` (or equivalent — see template constant)
- POSIX hook file mode is 0o755 (executable bit set via `f.Chmod` on O_NOFOLLOW fd)
- Windows shim contents are `@echo off\nalto ticket-ripple %*`
- `--no-hooks` flag suppresses hook write
- `--force-hooks` overwrites existing hook; without it, existing differing hook aborts the init with a clear error
- Doc-health validates the POSIX hook script (bash_substitution_policy=quoted via the `"$@"` quoting) and reports zero issues
- After `alto init --with-scaffold` in a scratch beads repo, `bd close <some-open-id>` triggers `alto ticket-ripple <id>` (smoke test)
- All existing bootstrap tests pass with no regression
- `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... -race && golangci-lint run ./...` all clean
- arch-go: zero new cross-context imports

## Edge Cases

| Case | Expected |
|------|----------|
| `.beads/` doesn't exist | `os.MkdirAll(.beads/hooks, 0o755)` runs as part of write |
| `.beads/hooks/post-close` exists with identical content | no-op (idempotent re-run) |
| `.beads/hooks/post-close` exists with different content | abort with diff, suggest `--force-hooks` |
| Symlink at `.beads/hooks/post-close` | O_NOFOLLOW rejects; same pattern as scaffold writer |
| Operator without write permission on `.beads/hooks/` | bubble up `fmt.Errorf` with path context |
| `alto` binary not on PATH at hook fire time | hook exits 1; user sees beads's hook-failure message; documented in README |
| User runs `alto init --with-scaffold --no-hooks --force-hooks` | conflicting flags: error "--no-hooks and --force-hooks are mutually exclusive" |

## File Ownership

| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `internal/bootstrap/application/ports.go` | MODIFY (additive: `BeadsHookWriter`) |
| `internal/bootstrap/application/bootstrap_handler.go` | MODIFY (wire hook step into WriteScaffold) |
| `internal/bootstrap/domain/` (ScaffoldParams) | MODIFY (additive: `IncludeHooks bool`) |
| `internal/bootstrap/infrastructure/filesystem_beads_hook_writer.go` | NEW |
| `internal/bootstrap/infrastructure/filesystem_beads_hook_writer_test.go` | NEW |
| `cmd/alto/commands/init.go` | MODIFY (add --no-hooks, --force-hooks, thread params) |
| `cmd/alto/commands/init_test.go` | MODIFY |
| `internal/composition/app.go` | MODIFY (wire hookWriter) |
| `docs/guides/installation.md` OR `docs/guides/new-project.md` | MODIFY (document the hook) |

## Quality Gates

- `go build ./...` zero errors
- `go vet ./...` zero errors
- `golangci-lint run ./...` zero issues
- `go test ./... -race` all pass
- arch-go zero violations
- `alto doc-health` zero new violations

## Risks / Dependencies

- **DEPENDS ON alty-cli-2f9** — hook calls `alto ticket-ripple`; if 2f9 not deployed in user's PATH the hook fails. Acceptable: `alto init --with-scaffold` is run from the same alto binary that has ticket-ripple, so deployed-as-a-unit.
- Soft: beads's hook-firing contract (positional args, env vars, stdin) is the binding interface. Pin in adapter tests with whatever beads guarantees at write-time of this ticket.
- Soft: Windows behavior is template-validated only — no Windows CI yet. Acceptable for this OSS phase.

## Out of scope

- Removing alty-cli-6n4's in-repo bash workaround. Defer to a P3 cleanup once hook proves stable in the wild.
- Hook events beyond `post-close` (post-create, post-update). Future tickets.

## Labels

bootstrap, cli, dogfooding, supersedes-i80
close_reason: alto init scaffolds .beads/hooks/post-close (Wave 6 commit 1, bundled with alty-cli-2f9). 21 tests added; build/vet/lint/test clean. FilesystemBeadsHookWriter uses the f.Chmod O_NOFOLLOW TOCTOU pattern lifted verbatim from embed_scaffold_writer.go:225-237. IncludeHooks defaults to true; --no-hooks and --force-hooks mutually exclusive. AC #9 (smoke test) exercised at unit-level only; end-to-end can be verified by closing any open ticket and watching for the ripple comment. alty-cli-i80 productization complete.

title: feat(ticket): alto ticket-ripple <id> subcommand wires existing RippleReview aggregate to CLI
description:
## Goal / Problem

Productize the ripple-review flow as a Go subcommand. Most domain logic already exists — this ticket adds an application handler, 2 missing ports, 1 missing adapter, the Cobra command, and composition wiring. The current bash workaround at `alto-scaffold/scripts/bd-ripple` becomes obsolete after this lands (i80-b then ships the beads hook that calls this command automatically).

Source: Superseded portion of alty-cli-i80 (Path A, subcommand half). Original i80 closed as superseded.

## Background / Context — what already exists

Discovered during grooming (2026-06-01) — the Ticket bounded context is more built-out than the original i80 description assumed:

**Domain (READ-ONLY for this ticket):**
- `internal/ticket/domain/ripple_review.go` — `RippleReview` aggregate with `FlagTicket`, `ClearFlag`, `Complete`, `BuildRippleComment`. Builds the same comment shape as bash bd-ripple.
- `internal/ticket/domain/ticket_freshness.go` — `ContextDiff` value object (`NewContextDiff(summary, triggeringID, producedAt)`); `FreshnessFlag` value object.
- `internal/ticket/domain/ticket_freshness_events.go` — `TicketFlagged`, `FlagCleared`, `RippleReviewCreated` events.

**Application ports (extend, do not duplicate):**
- `internal/ticket/application/ports.go:52` `BeadsLabelWriter` — `AddLabel(ctx, ticketID, label)`, `RemoveLabel(ctx, ticketID, label)`.
- `internal/ticket/application/ports.go:39` `CommandRunner` — security-controlled exec wrapper (allowlist, timeout, no shell).
- `internal/ticket/application/ports.go:46` `TicketContentReader` — read description by ID.

**Infrastructure (READ-ONLY):**
- `internal/ticket/infrastructure/beads_label_writer.go` — `bd label add|remove`.
- `internal/ticket/infrastructure/beads_ticket_reader.go` — `bd query`, `bd comments` already wired.
- `internal/ticket/infrastructure/command_runner.go` — exec.CommandContext, security envelope.

**Reference implementation:** `alto-scaffold/scripts/bd-ripple` (bash). Port its logic, not its shape.

## What is missing (this ticket builds)

| Layer | New file | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| application | `internal/ticket/application/ripple_handler.go` | `RippleHandler.Handle(ctx, closedID, contextOverride)` — orchestrates aggregate via ports |
| application/ports.go | `BeadsGraphReader` interface (additive) | `ReadParent`, `ReadSiblings`, `ReadDependents`, `ReadRelated`, `ReadCloseContext` — graph traversal not covered by existing reader |
| application/ports.go | `BeadsCommentWriter` interface (additive) | `AddComment(ctx, ticketID, comment)` — wraps `bd comments add` |
| infrastructure | `internal/ticket/infrastructure/beads_graph_reader.go` | Wraps `bd show --json` + `bd children --json`, parses JSON, returns domain-typed graph data |
| infrastructure | `internal/ticket/infrastructure/beads_comment_writer.go` | Wraps `bd comments add` via `CommandRunner` |
| cmd | `cmd/alto/commands/ticketripple.go` | Cobra command `alto ticket-ripple <id> [--context "<summary>"]` |
| composition | `internal/composition/app.go` | Wire `RippleHandler` into `App`; thread reader+writer adapters |

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Ticket (existing) |
| Aggregate | `RippleReview` (existing) — handler creates one per invocation |
| Ubiquitous Language | `RippleReview`, `ContextDiff`, `FlaggedTicket`, `ReviewChecklistTemplate` (from existing domain) |
| Layer | New ports + handler in application/; new adapters in infrastructure/. Dependencies flow inward: cmd -> composition -> handler -> ports <- adapters. Zero domain changes. |
| Aggregate boundary | One `RippleReview` per CLI invocation; flagged-ticket count is the aggregate's state. No cross-aggregate transactions. |

## Design — Sequence

```
cmd/alto/commands/ticketripple.go (Cobra)
  -> composition.App.RippleHandler.Handle(ctx, closedID, ctxOverride)
       1. graph.ReadCloseContext(closedID) -> (status, closeReason, title)
          - reject if status != closed && !forceFlag
       2. resolve context: ctxOverride OR closeReason (error if both empty)
       3. NewContextDiff(summary, closedID, time.Now())  // domain VO
       4. NewRippleReview(uuid, closedID, contextDiff)    // domain aggregate
       5. graph.ReadParent(closedID) -> parentID
       6. graph.ReadSiblings(parentID) -> []openSiblings  // empty if no parent
       7. graph.ReadDependents(closedID) -> []openDependents
       8. graph.ReadRelated(closedID) -> []openRelated
       9. dedupe + filter to open status
       10. for each ticketID:
             aggregate.FlagTicket(ticketID, isOpen=true, now)
             label.AddLabel(ctx, ticketID, "review_needed")  // skip if already labeled
             comment.AddComment(ctx, ticketID, aggregate.BuildRippleComment())
       11. aggregate.Complete()  // emits RippleReviewCreated event
       12. return RippleReviewResult{FlaggedCount, EventCount}
  -> notifier prints summary to stdout
```

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| S | Handler orchestrates; ports do one thing each. `BeadsGraphReader` reads graph; `BeadsCommentWriter` writes comments. Neither overlaps `BeadsLabelWriter`. |
| O | New ports added to ports.go; existing ports unchanged. Future event-driven adapter (Watermill) drops in by implementing the same port. |
| L | All graph-reader adapters honor the interface contract — same return types across CLI / mock / future event adapter. |
| I | 2 narrow new interfaces. Handler depends on exactly 4 ports: graph reader, label writer, comment writer, time provider. |
| D | Handler depends on `application.BeadsGraphReader` interface, never on concrete CLI adapter. |

## TDD Workflow

### RED Phase — tests by name

Handler unit tests (`ripple_handler_test.go`, port mocks):
- `TestRippleHandler_Handle_WhenClosedTicketHasOpenSiblings_FlagsAndComments`
- `TestRippleHandler_Handle_WhenClosedTicketHasOpenDependents_FlagsAndComments`
- `TestRippleHandler_Handle_WhenClosedTicketHasOpenRelated_FlagsAndComments`
- `TestRippleHandler_Handle_WhenContextDiffEmpty_ReturnsInvariantViolation`
- `TestRippleHandler_Handle_WhenContextOmitted_UsesCloseReason`
- `TestRippleHandler_Handle_WhenAlreadyFlagged_AddsCommentSkipsLabel`
- `TestRippleHandler_Handle_WhenNoOpenDependents_ReturnsSuccessZeroFlagged`
- `TestRippleHandler_Handle_WhenAggregateAlreadyCompleted_ReturnsInvariantViolation`
- `TestRippleHandler_Handle_WhenStatusNotClosed_ReturnsInvariantViolation`
- `TestRippleHandler_Handle_DeduplicatesTicketsAcrossSiblingsDependentsRelated`

Adapter integration tests (`beads_graph_reader_test.go`, real `bd` CLI behind fixtures):
- `TestBeadsGraphReader_ReadCloseContext_ParsesBDShowJSON`
- `TestBeadsGraphReader_ReadParent_ExtractsParentChildDependency`
- `TestBeadsGraphReader_ReadSiblings_FiltersOpenOnly`
- `TestBeadsGraphReader_ReadDependents_ParsesDependentsArray`
- `TestBeadsGraphReader_ReadRelated_ParsesBidirectionalRelatedLinks`
- `TestBeadsGraphReader_WhenBDExitsNonZero_ReturnsWrappedError`

Comment writer adapter:
- `TestBeadsCommentWriter_AddComment_InvokesBDCommentsAdd`
- `TestBeadsCommentWriter_AddComment_WhenCommandRunnerFails_WrapsError`

Cobra command:
- `TestTicketRippleCmd_RequiresTicketIDArg`
- `TestTicketRippleCmd_ContextFlagPassesThroughToHandler`
- `TestTicketRippleCmd_ExitCodeOnInvariantViolation_IsNonZero`

### GREEN Phase

1. Add `BeadsGraphReader` + `BeadsCommentWriter` interfaces to `internal/ticket/application/ports.go`.
2. Implement `RippleHandler` in `internal/ticket/application/ripple_handler.go`.
3. Implement adapters in `internal/ticket/infrastructure/`.
4. Wire Cobra command in `cmd/alto/commands/ticketripple.go`.
5. Wire `App.RippleHandler` in `internal/composition/app.go`.

### REFACTOR Phase

- Extract dedupe + filter into private helper; unit-test directly.
- Verify port docstrings match adapter behavior.
- Verify all errors are wrapped with `fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err)`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `alto ticket-ripple <id>` flags open siblings + open dependents + open related tickets with `review_needed` label
- Each flagged ticket receives a structured comment built via existing `RippleReview.BuildRippleComment()` (parity with bash script comment format)
- `--context "<summary>"` flag overrides ticket close-reason
- Empty close-reason + no `--context` returns invariant-violation exit code (matches existing bash behavior at `alto-scaffold/scripts/bd-ripple:74`)
- `--force` flag bypasses the "must be closed" precondition (matches existing bash behavior at `alto-scaffold/scripts/bd-ripple:50`)
- Already-flagged tickets get the new comment but not a duplicate label (matches bash behavior at line ~145)
- Empty dep graph -> exits 0 with "No open siblings or dependents" message
- 5-second per-bd-invocation timeout via CommandRunner
- All existing ticket-BC tests pass (signature-preserving ports.go additions)
- `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... -race && golangci-lint run ./...` all clean
- Coverage on new files >= 80%

## Edge Cases

| Case | Expected |
|------|----------|
| Closed ticket has no parent | siblings step skipped; dependents+related still traversed |
| Ticket already has `review_needed` label | comment added; AddLabel skipped (no duplicate) |
| `bd children` returns empty | treated as no siblings, not error |
| `bd show` returns invalid JSON | wrapped error including stderr snippet |
| Ticket ID with invalid format | `bd show` error bubbled up with wrapped context |
| `bd` binary not on PATH | CommandRunner returns specific not-found error |
| Aggregate.Complete called twice | invariant violation (existing domain check) |
| Multiple ticket IDs in arg | error "exactly one ticket ID required" (deferred to a separate ticket — single-ID for v1) |
| Same ID appears as sibling AND dependent AND related | flagged once (dedupe before mutating) |

## File Ownership

| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `internal/ticket/application/ports.go` | MODIFY (additive: 2 new interfaces) |
| `internal/ticket/application/ripple_handler.go` | NEW |
| `internal/ticket/application/ripple_handler_test.go` | NEW |
| `internal/ticket/infrastructure/beads_graph_reader.go` | NEW |
| `internal/ticket/infrastructure/beads_graph_reader_test.go` | NEW |
| `internal/ticket/infrastructure/beads_comment_writer.go` | NEW |
| `internal/ticket/infrastructure/beads_comment_writer_test.go` | NEW |
| `cmd/alto/commands/ticketripple.go` | NEW |
| `cmd/alto/commands/ticketripple_test.go` | NEW |
| `internal/composition/app.go` | MODIFY (wire `RippleHandler`) |
| `internal/ticket/domain/ripple_review.go` | READ-ONLY |
| `internal/ticket/domain/ticket_freshness.go` (ContextDiff) | READ-ONLY |
| `alto-scaffold/scripts/bd-ripple` | READ-ONLY (reference; deprecation noted in i80-b) |

## Quality Gates

- `go build ./...` zero errors
- `go vet ./...` zero errors
- `golangci-lint run ./...` zero issues
- `go test ./... -race` all pass

title: feat(dochealth): add privacy/leak rule to docs/ scanner + split archival exemption to freshness-only
description:
Origin: White Hacker recommendation during alty-cli-766.8 review, corrected against source. The docs/ health path (internal/dochealth/application/doc_health_handler.go:48-84) runs ONLY ScanRegistered + ScanUnregistered, both of which check ONLY last_reviewed + broken links (filesystem_doc_scanner.go:66-186). There is NO secrets/leak/privacy rule on the docs/ tree at all — SecretsGrepRule + NoInternalLeaksRule are scaffold-only rules applied via the alto-scaffold/ walker. So home-path/username debt in docs/ has always been invisible to doc-health.

Two improvements:
1. Add a privacy/leak rule to the docs/ scanner (home-dir paths, usernames) so docs/ leaks are caught.
2. Re-shape the archival exemption (doc_health_handler.go:73 excludeDirs research+plans): exempt archival dirs from the FRESHNESS (last_reviewed) cadence only, while STILL running the privacy/leak rule on them. Wholesale dir exclusion from all rules is the real gap.
3. LOW coverage nit (WH): excludeDirs matches by path-segment basename anywhere under docs/, so a future living doc at e.g. docs/guides/research/foo.md would be silently skipped. Consider anchoring the exempt match to top-level docs/ children.
acceptance_criteria: docs/ scanner flags a planted home-path/username fixture; archival dirs (research/plans) are exempt from freshness but still privacy-scanned; exempt-match no longer skips nested same-named dirs; tests cover all three; gates green.

title: feat(dochealth): 4 WARNING rules + bash-policy + ARGUMENTS-in-bash + path-depth + walker scope extension
description:
> **Before Starting:** Confirm alty-cli-766.7 closed (4 ERROR rules + handler + walker shipped). This ticket EXTENDS that handler with WARNING-severity rules and additional ERROR rules deferred from the original scope split (FIX-2).

## Goal / Problem

alty-cli-766.7 shipped the 4 ERROR-severity rules (FrontmatterSchemaRule, PhaseEnumRule, NoInternalLeaksRule, OrphanOverlayRule) plus the `ScaffoldHealthHandler`, `FilesystemScaffoldWalker`, frontmatter parser, and `--paths` CLI flag. The 4 WARNING rules + 3 bash-related rules + path-substitution-depth rule were explicitly deferred per tech-lead FIX-2 scope split, with this fast-follow as the agreed home. Additionally, the walker scopes to `.alto/{commands,agents}/` only — alty-cli-766.6's FIX-1 sweep AC requires `--paths=.alto/lifecycle/in-progress/` to validate files written there by the meta-skill; this ticket extends the walker to recognise that subtree.

## Background / Context

- **Binding spike:** `docs/research/20260529_workflow-scaffold-generic.md` lines 805-819 (expanded Follow-up #5 ACs)
- **Origin tickets:**
  - alty-cli-766.7 (closed) — shipped 4 ERROR rules + handler + walker (scoped to commands/+agents/) + CLI flag
  - alty-cli-766.6 — meta-skill writing to `.alto/lifecycle/in-progress/`; FIX-1 sweep AC depends on walker recognising that dir
- **Walker scoping gap (compatibility finding from 766.7 close):**
  - `internal/dochealth/infrastructure/scaffold_walker.go:23` declares `scaffoldAssetDirs = []string{"commands", "agents"}`
  - Invoking `alto doc-health --paths=.alto/lifecycle/in-progress/` returns 0 violations regardless of content (walker looks for commands/+agents/ subdirs which don't exist there)
  - Two fixes possible — pick at grooming time:
    - (a) Add `"lifecycle/in-progress"` to `scaffoldAssetDirs` — works when caller passes `--paths=.alto/`
    - (b) Auto-detect: if altoDir contains no known subdir, walk altoDir as flat `*.md` directory — works when caller passes `--paths=.alto/lifecycle/in-progress/`
    - **Recommendation:** ship both — (a) for the canonical sweep, (b) for direct in-progress invocation

## Acceptance Criteria

### Walker scope extension
- `alto doc-health --paths=.alto/lifecycle/in-progress/` (direct flat-dir invocation) walks every `*.md` and applies ERROR + WARNING rules
- `alto doc-health --paths=.alto/` ALSO sweeps `lifecycle/in-progress/` (so the canonical command unblocks 766.6 FIX-1)
- Walker still skips `templates/` (templates use different schema; out of scope for the 8-field rules)

### 4 WARNING rules (severity SeverityWarning; do not block CI exit code)
- `BodySizeRule` — body line count >500 (merged `<name>.md` + `<name>.project.md` per FIX-3 from 766.7) emits WARNING
- `UnknownToolsRule` — `tools_required` entries not matching `^[A-Z][A-Za-z]+$|^mcp__[a-z0-9_]+__[a-z0-9_]+$` emit WARNING
- `SecretsGrepRule` — case-insensitive body match for `\\b(password|secret|api[_-]?key|token|bearer|private_key|client_secret|jwt|credentials|aws_access_key)\\b` OR `AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}` OR `gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,}` emit WARNING; tunable via `--secret-patterns=<path>` flag; body-only (frontmatter excluded)
- `LifecycleStalenessRule` — staleness threshold injected via `ScaffoldParams.defaultStalenessDays` (NOT hardcoded); emits WARNING

### 4 additional ERROR rules
- `BashSubstitutionPolicyRule` — frontmatter `bash_substitution_policy` 3-mode: `none` rejects ANY bash block (ERROR); `quoted` rejects unquoted `\$VAR`/`\$ARGUMENTS` inside bash blocks (ERROR); `unrestricted` warns (WARNING)
- `BashArgumentsRule` — inline + fenced regex pair rejecting unquoted `\$ARGUMENTS`, `\$ARGUMENTS[N]`, `\$N`, `\$<name>` (ERROR with mitigation hint)
- `BashWithParametersWarnRule` — warn (WARNING) when `tools_required` contains `Bash` AND `parameters:` is declared AND `disable_model_invocation` is not `true`
- `PathSubstitutionDepthRule` — reject more than 2 `..` segments in `\${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/../...` references (ERROR)

### Quality gates
- All rules satisfy compile-time interface checks in `rules/rules.go`
- Table-driven RED tests first per CLAUDE.md TDD section
- `go test ./internal/dochealth/... -race -coverprofile=cov.out` — ≥80% on changed packages
- `go run ./cmd/alto doc-health --paths=.alto/` still returns 0 violations (no GENERIC file in actual repo trips the new rules)
- `arch-go` — 100% compliance

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Doc Health (same as 766.7) |
| Ubiquitous Language | All terms inherited from 766.7. New: `BashSubstitutionPolicy` VO (string enum for `none`/`quoted`/`unrestricted`), `SecretPattern` VO (compiled regex) |
| Layer | Domain: minor — possibly add `BashSubstitutionPolicy` VO. Application: NO new ports — extend `DefaultScaffoldRules()` factory only. Infrastructure: 8 new rule files in `internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/` + walker scope extension in `scaffold_walker.go` |

## File Ownership

| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `internal/dochealth/infrastructure/scaffold_walker.go` | MODIFY — append `lifecycle/in-progress` to `scaffoldAssetDirs`; add flat-dir auto-detect when no known subdir found |
| `internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/body_size_rule.go` | NEW (+ test) |
| `internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/unknown_tools_rule.go` | NEW (+ test) |
| `internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/secrets_grep_rule.go` | NEW (+ test) |
| `internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/lifecycle_staleness_rule.go` | NEW (+ test) |
| `internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/bash_substitution_policy_rule.go` | NEW (+ test) |
| `internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/bash_arguments_rule.go` | NEW (+ test) |

| `cmd/alto/commands/dochealth.go` | EXTEND — `--secret-patterns=<path>` flag for `SecretsGrepRule` tunability |

## Why fast-follow (not in original scope)

Tech-lead FIX-2 scope split (768.5+) capped 766.7 at "4 ERROR rules + handler" to keep the wave-2 PR reviewable. Spike Follow-up #5 (lines 805-819) explicitly enumerates the deferred rules; this ticket instantiates them. The walker scope extension is a compatibility finding surfaced by 766.7's close-out review (alty-cli-766.6 FIX-1 sweep would otherwise be silently broken).
