title: feat(scaffold): /write-a-workflow-asset meta-skill for authoring new commands/agents/templates
description:
> **Before Starting:** Confirm `alty-cli-766.2` closed (`alto-scaffold/lifecycle/in-progress/` must exist). Note: spike `docs/research/20260529_workflow-scaffold-generic.md:789` (follow-up #4 design body) lists 5 prompt fields, but the canonical schema at lines 224-244 requires 8 — **the canonical schema is binding (FIX-10)**.
>
> **Freshness:** Run `bd label list <this-id>` for `review_needed` before claiming. This ticket was groomed against the post-Wave-3 codebase: paths are `alto-scaffold/` (not `.alto/`), and `ihk` walker scope + 8-rule dochealth are shipped.

## Goal / Problem

Contributors adding new workflow assets (commands, agents, templates) today have no guided path — they copy an existing file, forget required frontmatter fields, pick the wrong `alto-scaffold/` subdir, and discover the omission only when `alto doc-health` runs. This ticket ships a meta-skill `alto-scaffold/commands/write-a-workflow-asset.md` that walks a contributor interactively through authoring any new workflow asset, enforces the 8 required frontmatter fields from the spike's canonical schema (`docs/research/20260529_workflow-scaffold-generic.md:224-244`), validates `name` before touching the filesystem, and writes the final file to `alto-scaffold/lifecycle/in-progress/<name>.md`. Instantiates spike follow-up #4 (lines 781-795). The meta-skill dogfoods the scaffold — itself a workflow asset stored under `alto-scaffold/commands/` in the format it enforces.

## Background / Context

- **Spike (binding):** `docs/research/20260529_workflow-scaffold-generic.md`
  - Lines 224-244 — **canonical 8-field schema** (this is binding)
  - Lines 215-219 — write target `alto-scaffold/lifecycle/in-progress/`
  - Line 251 — Bash+parameters safety rule
  - Lines 781-795 — follow-up #4 design body
- **FIX-10 — spike self-inconsistency.** Spike line 789 (follow-up #4 body) lists 5 prompts: `name`, `kind`, `phase`, `when_to_use`, `tools_required`. The canonical schema at lines 224-244 requires 8: those 5 plus `description`, `bash_substitution_policy`, `license`. **The canonical schema wins.** Verified shipped: `internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/frontmatter_schema_rule.go:13-22` lists exactly the 8 fields.
- **Dependency:** `bd dep add <this-id> alty-cli-766.2` already set. The refactor's single PR includes Phase 5 (symlink bridge), so `alto-scaffold/lifecycle/in-progress/` exists and `.claude/commands/<name>.md → ../../alto-scaffold/commands/<name>.md` symlinks work.
- **Relationship to alty-cli-766.7 + ihk (shipped):** dochealth ships the 8-rule validator with walker scope `commands` + `agents` + `lifecycle/in-progress` (`internal/dochealth/infrastructure/scaffold_walker.go:24`). Frontmatter rule, phase enum, bash_substitution_policy rule, and name regex `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$` are all shipped and exactly match this ticket's design (see Compatibility section).
- **Permission gates:** `.claude/settings.json:4` contains only `WebFetch(domain:buildingbetter.tech)` in the allow list. No Write-tool restriction. Skill's Write to `alto-scaffold/lifecycle/in-progress/<name>.md` is unblocked.
- **Pattern references:** `alto-scaffold/commands/design-ticket.md`, `groom.md`, `launch-team.md` — frontmatter + `# /<name>` header + body sections. New skill must produce output conforming to the spike canonical schema (uses `tools_required`, not the legacy `allowed-tools`).

## Architecture Decision: Option A — Pure Markdown Deliverable

**Recommendation: Option A.** Deliverable is the single file `alto-scaffold/commands/write-a-workflow-asset.md`. No new Go code.

**Rationale:**

1. The validation logic is a checklist against a fixed schema — executable by Claude inline.
2. Programmatic frontmatter validation already ships in `internal/dochealth/` (via 766.7 + ihk). Adding a `alto workflow-asset validate` subcommand would duplicate the doc-health path.
3. Spike line 787: "no production Go code unless the meta-skill needs validation logic in `internal/tooltranslation/application/`." It doesn't — the validator lives in doc-health.
4. The meta-skill self-dogfoods. A workflow-asset-authoring skill, written as a workflow asset, in the directory it teaches contributors to write into.

**Compatibility (verified post-Wave-3):**

| Concept | Shipped at | Confirmed |
|---|---|---|
| 8 canonical fields | `internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/frontmatter_schema_rule.go:13-22` | ✓ exact match |
| `kind` enum | `frontmatter_schema_rule.go:25-30` — `{command, agent, template, skill}` | ✓ exact match |
| `phase` enum | `internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/phase_enum_rule.go` — `{design, groom, implement, review, close}` | ✓ exact match |
| name regex `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$` | `frontmatter_schema_rule.go:33` | ✓ exact match |
| Walker visits `lifecycle/in-progress` | `internal/dochealth/infrastructure/scaffold_walker.go:24` | ✓ shipped via ihk |
| `bash_substitution_policy` enum `{none, quoted, unrestricted}` | `internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/bash_substitution_policy_rule.go` | ✓ shipped via ihk |

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | N/A — markdown-only deliverable; no Go layer added. |
| Ubiquitous Language | `workflow asset`, `lifecycle folder`, `in-progress`, `frontmatter schema` (all from spike lines 22-27). **FIX-8:** grep `docs/DDD.md` during grooming for collisions with any of these four terms before claiming. None expected, but verify. |
| Layer | N/A. If a future revision needs Go validation logic, spike line 787 designates `internal/tooltranslation/application/`. |

## Design

### Skill File: `alto-scaffold/commands/write-a-workflow-asset.md`

The skill's own frontmatter (the 8 canonical schema fields):

```yaml
---
name: write-a-workflow-asset
description: Interactive meta-skill for authoring a new workflow asset with enforced frontmatter schema
kind: command
phase: design
when_to_use: When a contributor needs to create a new command, agent, or template in alto-scaffold/
tools_required: [Read, Write, Glob]
bash_substitution_policy: none
license: Apache-2.0
---
```

Body structured in 4 phases.

**Phase 1 — Gather inputs.** Prompt for each field one at a time. No blank answers.

| Field | Validation |
|-------|------------|
| `name` | Must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`. **FIX-3:** This regex is the SOLE path-traversal control — `.`, `/`, `\` can never pass it, so the resolved path `<root>/alto-scaffold/lifecycle/in-progress/<name>.md` cannot escape the lifecycle dir. No `filepath.Clean` reasoning needed (a markdown skill can't run it anyway). |
| `description` | Under 1,536 chars; non-empty. |
| `kind` | Enum `{command, agent, template, skill}`. |
| `phase` | Enum `{design, groom, implement, review, close}`. |
| `when_to_use` | Non-empty. |
| `tools_required` | Non-empty list. **FIX-6:** Warn-and-confirm for unknown tool names (MCP tools like `mcp__context7__query-docs`, plus `WebFetch`/`WebSearch`/`Task`) instead of hard-rejecting. Known enum: `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Bash`, `Agent`. Unknowns trigger: "Tool '<value>' not in the known enum; confirm it's a real Claude Code tool / MCP tool name. Continue?" |
| `bash_substitution_policy` | Enum `{none, quoted, unrestricted}` per `BashSubstitutionPolicyRule`. Default `none` if contributor leaves blank — but ask. |
| `license` | Non-empty SPDX. Default `Apache-2.0` for assets in this repo. |

**Phase 2 — Validate.** Before any Write:

1. `name` regex check (per FIX-3).
2. **FIX-2:** Collision Glob across **5 directories** (the full taxonomy from spike lines 213-219): `alto-scaffold/lifecycle/in-progress/<name>.md`, `alto-scaffold/commands/<name>.md`, `alto-scaffold/agents/<name>.md`, `alto-scaffold/templates/<name>.md`, `alto-scaffold/skills/<name>.md`. Any match → surface conflict, abort unless contributor explicitly confirms overwrite.
3. **Bash+parameters safety (spike line 251):** if `tools_required` contains `Bash` AND contributor declares any `parameters:`, require `disable_model_invocation: true`. Prompt explicitly. This is a **Claude Code skill-metadata concept** distinct from the body-fence `bash_substitution_policy` field — both checks coexist; do not fold one into the other.
4. Enum + length checks on all other fields.

**Phase 3 — Assemble and Write.** Compose full YAML frontmatter + a skeleton body (Usage / Process / Rules sections with placeholder steps). Write via the Write tool to `alto-scaffold/lifecycle/in-progress/<name>.md`.

**Phase 4 — Post-write guidance.** After Write succeeds, print:

```
Written: alto-scaffold/lifecycle/in-progress/<name>.md

Next steps:
1. Fill in the body sections.
2. Run `alto doc-health --paths=alto-scaffold/lifecycle/in-progress/` to validate the new file
   (walker scopes to commands + agents + lifecycle/in-progress already).
3. When stable, promote with:
     git mv alto-scaffold/lifecycle/in-progress/<name>.md alto-scaffold/<kind>s/<name>.md
   (e.g. for kind: command → alto-scaffold/commands/<name>.md)
4. After promotion, the Claude Code symlink at .claude/commands/<name>.md → ../../alto-scaffold/commands/<name>.md
   already points at the new location (assuming alty-cli-766.2's Phase 5 wired it; if you renamed during promotion, add the symlink manually).
```

**FIX-9:** the promotion `git mv` step is architect-introduced, not spike-quoted. Spike lines 213-219 establish the lifecycle taxonomy but don't script the promotion. The wording above is the recommended convention for this epic.

### Sequence

```
Contributor          /write-a-workflow-asset       filesystem
     |                       |                          |
     |- invoke ------------->|                          |
     |<- prompt: name? ------|                          |
     |- enter "foo" -------->|                          |
     |                       |- regex check (FIX-3)     |
     |                       |- Glob 5 dirs (FIX-2)---->|
     |<- prompt: description |                          |
     ... (8 fields total) ...
     |                       |- Bash+params rule check  |
     |                       |- enum + length checks    |
     |                       |- assemble frontmatter+body|
     |                       |- Write tool ------------>|
     |<- post-write guidance |                          |
```

## SOLID Mapping

N/A — Option A markdown-only deliverable. The Go side (FrontmatterSchemaRule + PhaseEnumRule + BashSubstitutionPolicyRule) already SOLID-honors via the `ValidationRule` interface.

## TDD Workflow

Markdown deliverable. RED/GREEN/REFACTOR phrased as fitness assertions.

### RED Phase

- `ls alto-scaffold/commands/write-a-workflow-asset.md` returns "No such file".
- Invoking `/write-a-workflow-asset` in Claude Code returns "skill not found".

### GREEN Phase

1. Write `alto-scaffold/commands/write-a-workflow-asset.md` with frontmatter + body per Design section.
2. **Smoke A (happy path):** invoke `/write-a-workflow-asset`, supply valid inputs for all 8 fields, confirm `alto-scaffold/lifecycle/in-progress/<name>.md` written with valid frontmatter.
3. **Smoke B (name rejection):** supply `name: My Command` (space + uppercase), confirm abort before Write.
4. **Smoke C (path-traversal regex defense, FIX-3):** supply `name: ../commands/evil`, confirm abort — `/` fails the regex, no path composition reached.
5. **Smoke D (5-dir collision, FIX-2):** create a dummy `alto-scaffold/templates/test-asset.md`, then invoke with `name: test-asset, kind: command`. Confirm collision surfaces against `alto-scaffold/templates/` even though the contributor is writing a command.
6. **Smoke E (unknown tool warn, FIX-6):** supply `tools_required: [WebFetch, mcp__context7__query-docs]`, confirm warn-and-confirm prompt appears (not hard reject).
7. **Smoke F (FIX-1 post-write sweep):** after Smoke A's file lands, run `alto doc-health --paths=alto-scaffold/lifecycle/in-progress/` and confirm 0 violations on the new file.

title: fix: algorithmic boundary detector produces unusable context names
description:
## Goal / Problem

The AlgorithmicBoundaryDetector produces bounded context names like 'Sentence diagram-Story yaml file' and 'Context map-Updated context yaml'. These are hyphenated work-object pairs, not meaningful bounded context names. Users see these in DDD.md and context-map.yaml — they're confusing and require manual cleanup.

## Background / Context

Root cause confirmed in `internal/discovery/infrastructure/algorithmic_detector.go:697-723` — function `deriveName`:
- Line 698-709 gathers ALL work-object names (or actor names if no WOs).
- Line 715 sorts alphabetically (loses any notion of dominance).
- Line 718-720 caps to 2 entries.
- Line 722 joins them with "-".

`capitalize` at line 726-732 only uppercases the first letter — "context map" → "Context map", not "Context Map".

A TODO at line 696 already notes "plural stripping deferred — add in follow-up ticket". Plural stripping stays deferred in THIS ticket.

The LLM detector (`llm_boundary_detector.go`) produces good names but requires an API key. The algorithmic path is the only option without LLM.

## DDD Alignment

| Bounded Context | Impact |
|----------------|--------|
| Discovery | Enhancement: infrastructure layer (algorithmic_detector.go) |

Port `BoundaryDetector` at `internal/discovery/application/ports.go:209-213` — UNCHANGED.
Domain type `BoundedContextSketch` at `internal/discovery/domain/bounded_context_sketch.go:23-60` — UNCHANGED (Name field still populated, just with better values).

## Design

### Algorithm

For each cluster of stories:
1. Walk the cluster's stories and build `woCounts map[string]int` — for each sentence whose object is one of the cluster's work objects, increment that WO's count.
2. For each WO name, apply `canonicalizeName`:
   - Trim whitespace
   - Strip case-insensitive leading prefixes: "Updated ", "New ", "Modified "
   - Title-case via stdlib helper `titleCase` (split on whitespace, uppercase each word's first rune)
3. Merge counts under canonical keys: "Context Map" (3x) + "Updated Context Map" (2x) → "Context Map" (5x).
4. Pick the canonical name with the highest sentence count. Tie-break alphabetically.
5. If the picked name is empty OR the cluster has no actors AND no work objects, fallback to `Context <N>` where N is the 1-based cluster index.

### Data-flow choice

Pass `stories []*domain.DomainStory` (cluster slice) through to `deriveName` and recount per call. Avoids reshaping `signalWithContext.workObjects` (used by 3 signal detectors + cluster fallback). Keeps the change localized to one file.

New signature:
```go
func deriveName(stories []*domain.DomainStory, actors, workObjects map[string]struct{}, clusterIdx int) string
```

Callers at line 478 (`detectWorkObjectClusters`) and line 540 (`clusterAndScore`) already iterate clusters — pass a 1-based `clusterIdx`.

### Helpers (new, stdlib only — no new deps)

- `canonicalizeName(s string) string` — trim + strip prefix + title-case
- `titleCase(s string) string` — split on whitespace, uppercase first rune of each token using `unicode.ToUpper`

Verified `golang.org/x/text` is NOT in go.mod — stdlib `unicode`/`strings` is sufficient.

### SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| S | `canonicalizeName`, `titleCase` are single-purpose helpers; `deriveName` keeps cluster→name responsibility |
| O | Extension via new helpers; no existing signatures changed outside `deriveName` |
| L | N/A — no interface contracts touched |
| I | N/A — `BoundaryDetector` port unchanged |
| D | N/A — no new dependencies |

## Steps

1. RED: `TestTitleCase_HandlesMultipleWords` — "context map" → "Context Map"
2. RED: `TestTitleCase_HandlesEmpty` — "" → ""
3. RED: `TestCanonicalizeName_StripsUpdatedPrefix` — "Updated Context Map" → "Context Map"
4. RED: `TestCanonicalizeName_CaseInsensitivePrefix` — "updated context map" → "Context Map"
5. RED: `TestCanonicalizeName_PreservesCanonical` — "Context Map" → "Context Map"
6. GREEN: Implement `titleCase` and `canonicalizeName` in algorithmic_detector.go
7. RED: `TestDeriveName_PicksDominantByCount` — feed cluster where "context map" appears 5x, "story" 2x → "Context Map"
8. RED: `TestDeriveName_TieBreaksAlphabetically` — equal counts → alphabetical first
9. RED: `TestDeriveName_MergesPrefixedVariantCounts` — "Context Map" (3x) + "Updated Context Map" (2x) → "Context Map" (5x total → wins)
10. RED: `TestDeriveName_FallsBackToContextN` — empty actors + empty workObjects → "Context 1"
11. GREEN: Update `deriveName` signature + body; rewire callers at line 478 and line 540 to pass stories + 1-based clusterIdx
12. REFACTOR: Run existing 5 WorkObjectCluster tests (lines 516-663) — they assert sketch count/signal type, NOT specific names, so no assertion changes expected. Confirm.
13. Quality gates

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Boundary proposals use canonicalized dominant work-object names (title-cased, prefix-stripped), not hyphenated pairs
- [ ] "Updated", "New", "Modified" prefixes stripped case-insensitively from context names
- [ ] Counts from prefixed and non-prefixed variants merge under the canonical key
- [ ] Ties resolve alphabetically (deterministic)
- [ ] Empty/no-WO clusters fall back to "Context <N>" where N is 1-based cluster index
- [ ] LLM detector path (`llm_boundary_detector.go`) unchanged — verify via `git diff`
- [ ] Existing 5 WorkObjectCluster tests still pass without assertion changes
- [ ] `go test ./internal/discovery/... -race` all pass
- [ ] `golangci-lint run ./internal/discovery/...` zero issues
- [ ] No new entries in go.mod

## Edge Cases

| Case | Expected |
|------|----------|
| Single work object in cluster | Canonicalized name of that object |
| All WOs share "Updated" prefix | Strip prefix → canonical base name |
| Two WOs tied for highest count | Alphabetical first |
| Empty actors AND empty workObjects | "Context <clusterIdx>" |
| All WOs canonicalize to empty string | "Context <clusterIdx>" |
| Mixed case: "context map" + "Context Map" | Merge under "Context Map" |

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| internal/discovery/infrastructure/algorithmic_detector.go | New `titleCase`, `canonicalizeName`; updated `deriveName` signature + body; callers at lines 478, 540 rewired |
| internal/discovery/infrastructure/algorithmic_detector_test.go | 9 new test functions for the new helpers/`deriveName` paths |

## Files NOT Modified

- `internal/discovery/application/ports.go` (port unchanged)
- `internal/discovery/application/boundary_detection_handler.go`
- `internal/discovery/domain/bounded_context_sketch.go`
- `internal/discovery/infrastructure/llm_boundary_detector.go`
- `internal/discovery/infrastructure/hybrid_detector.go`

## Quality Gates

- `go build ./...` zero errors
- `go vet ./...` zero errors
- `golangci-lint run ./...` zero issues
- `go test ./... -race` all pass

## Pre-Implementation Validation

- [x] `algorithmic_detector.go:697-723` — `deriveName` bug confirmed
- [x] `algorithmic_detector.go:726-732` — `capitalize` only handles first letter
- [x] `algorithmic_detector.go:696` — TODO for plural stripping (stays deferred)
- [x] `ports.go:209-213` — port signature unchanged
- [x] `algorithmic_detector_test.go:516-663` — existing WO-cluster tests do NOT assert names
- [x] `bounded_context_sketch.go:35-60` — Name validated non-empty → "Context N" fallback safe
- [x] `go.mod` — `golang.org/x/text` not present; stdlib-only solution chosen

title: fix: --existing mode shows misleading error when LLM unavailable
description:
## Goal / Problem

When `alto guide --existing` finds docs in `docs/` but the LLM is unavailable (no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) AND the regex fallback can't parse them, the CLI prints "No documentation found for inference. Falling through to storytelling..." — which is wrong. Docs WERE found; inference failed. Users think their docs weren't detected.

## Background / Context

Two collaborating sites:

- `internal/discovery/application/doc_inference_handler.go:51-53` — when `ReadDocs` returns ≥1 doc but `llmReader.InferModel` returns `llm.ErrLLMUnavailable` AND `regexImporter.Import` then fails, the handler returns `fmt.Errorf("regex fallback failed: %w", regexErr)` — no mention of which docs were found.
- `doc_inference_handler.go:46-48` — when LLM returns an error that is NOT `ErrLLMUnavailable`, returns `fmt.Errorf("LLM inference failed: %w", err)` — also drops doc context.
- `cmd/alto/commands/guide.go:217-223` — `runGuideExistingWithDeps` calls `InferFromDocs("docs")`, falls back to `InferFromDocs(".")` on ANY error, and then prints one generic message for THREE distinct failure modes: (a) no docs anywhere, (b) docs exist but inference failed, (c) I/O error.

The "no docs" path produces the message `no documentation found in %q` at `doc_inference_handler.go:36-38` — this string is the only legitimate trigger for "No documentation found".

## DDD Alignment

| Bounded Context | Impact |
|----------------|--------|
| Discovery | Bug fix: new typed error in domain, wrap in application handler, branch in CLI |

Layer rules respected: domain owns the error type; application wraps; CLI presents. No port signatures change.

## Design

### Typed error in domain

Add to `internal/discovery/domain/errors.go`:

```go
// ErrInferenceFailed is a sentinel returned via errors.Is for the case where
// docs were found but the inference step (LLM or regex fallback) failed.
var ErrInferenceFailed = errors.New("inference failed")

// InferenceFailedError carries the source documents that were available when
// inference failed, so the CLI can surface useful context.
type InferenceFailedError struct {
    Docs   []string // sorted doc names (file basenames or relative paths)
    Reason error    // underlying failure (regex error, LLM error, etc.)
}

func (e *InferenceFailedError) Error() string {
    return fmt.Sprintf("inference failed (found %d doc(s)): %v", len(e.Docs), e.Reason)
}

func (e *InferenceFailedError) Unwrap() error { return e.Reason }

func (e *InferenceFailedError) Is(target error) bool {
    return target == ErrInferenceFailed
}
```

### Handler wraps both failure paths

In `doc_inference_handler.go`:

1. Build `sourceDocs []string` (sorted) BEFORE attempting LLM, so we can attach it on either failure path.
2. Line 47: `LLM inference failed` → wrap in `*InferenceFailedError{Docs: sourceDocs, Reason: err}`.
3. Line 53: `regex fallback failed` → wrap in `*InferenceFailedError{Docs: sourceDocs, Reason: regexErr}`.
4. Line 36-38: `no documentation found in %q` → UNCHANGED (this is the legitimate "no docs" signal).

### CLI branches on error type

In `runGuideExistingWithDeps` at `guide.go:217-224`:

1. Try `InferFromDocs("docs")`. Capture both attempts' errors.
2. If "docs" returned `*InferenceFailedError` (docs found but inference broken), do NOT silently fall through to `.` — print the typed error's doc list + reason immediately, then proceed to storytelling.
3. If "docs" returned a "no documentation found" error (sentinel match TBD — see note), try `.`.
4. After exhausting both: if final error is `*InferenceFailedError`, print:
   `Found N doc(s) (file1.md, file2.md, ...) but inference failed: <reason>. Falling through to storytelling...`
5. Else print: `No documentation found for inference. Falling through to storytelling...` (current behaviour for the genuine "no docs" case).

**Note on "no docs" sentinel:** Line 37 currently returns a `fmt.Errorf("no documentation found in %q", ...)` — no sentinel. We have two options:
(a) Add `ErrNoDocsFound` sentinel in `errors.go` and wrap line 37 with it.
(b) Detect via `errors.As` for `*InferenceFailedError` — anything else is treated as "no docs / I/O" for the fallback decision.

**Choice: (a).** Adds `ErrNoDocsFound` for explicit semantics; CLI fall-back from `docs/` to `.` only fires when the error matches `ErrNoDocsFound`. Any other error type (including `*InferenceFailedError`) is surfaced immediately. Document this in the design.

### SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| S | Domain owns the error type; handler owns wrapping; CLI owns presentation |
| O | Adding new sentinels/types — no existing signatures changed |
| L | N/A — no interface contracts touched |
| I | N/A — handler/port signatures unchanged |
| D | CLI depends on the domain error abstraction via errors.Is/As, not concrete strings |

## Steps

1. RED: `TestInferenceFailedError_ErrorIncludesDocCount` — `(&InferenceFailedError{Docs: []string{"a.md","b.md"}, Reason: errors.New("x")}).Error()` contains "2 doc(s)"
2. RED: `TestInferenceFailedError_IsMatchesSentinel` — `errors.Is(&InferenceFailedError{...}, ErrInferenceFailed)` is true
3. RED: `TestInferenceFailedError_UnwrapReturnsReason` — `errors.Unwrap` returns the inner error
4. GREEN: Add `ErrInferenceFailed`, `ErrNoDocsFound`, `InferenceFailedError` to `internal/discovery/domain/errors.go`
5. RED: `TestDocInferenceHandler_RegexFallbackFailure_WrapsAsInferenceFailed` — LLM returns `ErrLLMUnavailable`, regex returns error → handler returns `*InferenceFailedError` with the source doc names
6. RED: `TestDocInferenceHandler_LLMErrorNotUnavailable_WrapsAsInferenceFailed` — LLM returns non-unavailable error → handler returns `*InferenceFailedError`
7. RED: `TestDocInferenceHandler_NoDocsFound_ReturnsErrNoDocsFound` — `ReadDocs` returns empty map → error matches `ErrNoDocsFound`
8. RED: `TestDocInferenceHandler_RegexSuccess_NoError` — LLM unavailable but regex succeeds → InferenceResult, no error (unchanged behaviour)
9. GREEN: Update `doc_inference_handler.go`: build `sourceDocs` early; wrap LLM error (line 47) and regex error (line 53) with `*InferenceFailedError`; wrap "no docs" (line 37) with `ErrNoDocsFound`
10. RED: `TestRunGuideExistingWithDeps_InferenceFailedWithDocs_PrintsDocNames` — mock handler returns `*InferenceFailedError`; assert output contains "Found N doc(s)" and the file names
11. RED: `TestRunGuideExistingWithDeps_NoDocsFound_PrintsGenericMessage` — mock handler returns `ErrNoDocsFound`; assert output contains "No documentation found for inference"
12. RED: `TestRunGuideExistingWithDeps_DocsFails_DotSucceeds` — first call returns `ErrNoDocsFound`, second returns InferenceResult; assert no error message printed
13. GREEN: Update `guide.go:217-224` to use `errors.Is`/`errors.As` on the typed errors
14. REFACTOR: Quality gates

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `*InferenceFailedError` carries `Docs []string` and `Reason error`, implements `Error()`, `Unwrap()`, `Is(ErrInferenceFailed) bool`
- [ ] `ErrNoDocsFound` sentinel exists in `internal/discovery/domain/errors.go`
- [ ] Handler wraps BOTH the LLM-error path AND the regex-fallback path with `*InferenceFailedError`
- [ ] Handler wraps the "no docs" path with `ErrNoDocsFound`
- [ ] CLI's "No documentation found" message is printed ONLY when error matches `ErrNoDocsFound` for both `docs/` and `.` attempts
- [ ] When docs were found but inference failed, the CLI message names the found files and includes the underlying reason
- [ ] Storytelling fallback still fires in all failure paths (returns `domain.ErrInferenceDismissed` as today)
- [ ] `go test ./internal/discovery/... ./cmd/alto/... -race` all pass
- [ ] `golangci-lint run ./...` zero issues

## Edge Cases

| Case | Expected |
|------|----------|
| No `docs/` dir AND no docs in `.` | `ErrNoDocsFound` → "No documentation found for inference. Falling through..." (unchanged) |
| `docs/` has 2 files, LLM unavailable, regex fails | `*InferenceFailedError` with both file names → "Found 2 doc(s) (a.md, b.md) but inference failed: <regex error>. Falling through..." |
| `docs/` has 1 file, LLM unavailable, regex succeeds | `InferenceResult` with confidence "low" (unchanged) |
| `docs/` has 1 file, LLM returns non-unavailable error | `*InferenceFailedError` (no double-fallback attempt to `.`) |
| `docs/` empty AND `.` has 3 files, LLM unavailable, regex succeeds | Falls back to `.`, succeeds with `InferenceResult` |
| `docs/` empty AND `.` has 3 files, LLM unavailable, regex fails | `*InferenceFailedError` with `.`'s 3 file names |

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| internal/discovery/domain/errors.go | Add `ErrInferenceFailed`, `ErrNoDocsFound`, `InferenceFailedError` struct |
| internal/discovery/domain/errors_test.go | NEW: tests for `InferenceFailedError` methods (Error/Unwrap/Is) |
| internal/discovery/application/doc_inference_handler.go | Build `sourceDocs` early; wrap LLM error (line 47) and regex error (line 53) with `*InferenceFailedError`; wrap "no docs" (line 37) with `ErrNoDocsFound` |
| internal/discovery/application/doc_inference_handler_test.go | NEW or EXTEND: 4 new test cases for the wrapping paths |
| cmd/alto/commands/guide.go | Update `runGuideExistingWithDeps` (lines 217-224) to branch on `errors.Is`/`errors.As` |
| cmd/alto/commands/guide_test.go | NEW or EXTEND: 3 new test cases for the message branches |

## Files NOT Modified

- `internal/discovery/application/ports.go` (port signatures unchanged)
- `internal/shared/infrastructure/llm/*` (uses existing `ErrLLMUnavailable` without change)
- `internal/discovery/infrastructure/*` (no adapter changes)

## Quality Gates

- `go build ./...` zero errors
- `go vet ./...` zero errors
- `golangci-lint run ./...` zero issues
- `go test ./... -race` all pass

## Pre-Implementation Validation

- [x] `doc_inference_handler.go:36-38` — "no documentation found" path confirmed
- [x] `doc_inference_handler.go:46-48` — LLM-error path drops doc context (will wrap)
- [x] `doc_inference_handler.go:51-53` — regex-fallback path drops doc context (will wrap)
- [x] `doc_inference_handler.go:57-58` — `sourceDocs` built only on success path; need to move earlier
- [x] `guide.go:217-224` — generic error message confirmed at line 222

title: fix: algorithmic boundary detector produces unusable context names
description:
## Goal / Problem

The `AlgorithmicBoundaryDetector.deriveName()` function produces bounded context names like "Sentence diagram-Story yaml file" and "Context map-Updated context yaml". These are raw work-object name pairs joined with hyphens — not meaningful bounded context names. Users see these names in:

- CLI output during boundary detection results display
- `docs/DDD.md` bounded context sections
- `.alto/context-map.yaml`

This causes confusion and requires manual cleanup for every `alto guide` run.

**Observed output** (3 stories, Rapid mode):
```
Boundary Detection Results:
  - Sentence diagram-Story yaml file (generic, confidence: 0.33)
  - Context map-Updated context yaml (generic, confidence: 0.33)
  - Glossary entry-Updated glossary yaml (generic, confidence: 0.33)
```

**Expected output** (after fix):
```
Boundary Detection Results:
  - Sentence Diagram (generic, confidence: 0.33)
  - Context Map (generic, confidence: 0.33)
  - Glossary (generic, confidence: 0.33)
```

## Background / Context

- The `deriveName` function at `internal/discovery/infrastructure/algorithmic_detector.go:697` iterates all work objects in a cluster, capitalizes the first letter of each, sorts alphabetically, takes the first 2, and joins them with a hyphen. No cleaning, deduplication, or summarization.
- Work object names from domain stories are multi-word descriptive strings like "sentence diagram", "story yaml file", "updated context yaml", "glossary entry". When two of these are hyphen-joined, the result is gibberish as a bounded context name.
- The LLM boundary detector path (`internal/discovery/infrastructure/llm_boundary_detector.go`) does not produce context names — it returns `BoundarySignal` values that are merged by the `HybridBoundaryDetector`. The algorithmic path's `deriveName` is responsible for ALL sketch naming when running in algorithmic-only mode (offline / no LLM).
- There is an existing TODO at line 696: `// TODO: plural stripping deferred — add in follow-up ticket.`
- **Pattern reference:** The `capitalize()` helper at line 726 is the only name-cleaning logic that exists today.

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Discovery |
| Ubiquitous Language | BoundedContextSketch, WorkObject, BoundarySignal, deriveName |
| Layer | Infrastructure (algorithmic_detector.go is an adapter implementing the BoundaryDetector port) |

The fix is entirely within the infrastructure layer. No domain types change. The `BoundedContextSketch` value object accepts any non-empty string as a name (validated at `bounded_context_sketch.go:46-48`), so improved names pass existing invariants without domain changes.

## Design

### Data Models

No new types required. The fix modifies the existing `deriveName` function and adds a `cleanContextName` helper function in the same file.

| Model | Type | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| `deriveName` (existing) | Private function | Selects dominant work object as context name instead of joining pairs |
| `cleanContextName` (new) | Private function | Applies heuristic cleaning: strip noise prefixes, title-case words, pick dominant term |

### Name-Cleaning Heuristics (implemented in `cleanContextName`)

1. **Strip noise prefixes** — Remove leading "Updated", "New", "Modified", "Existing" from each work object name (these are verb participles, not domain terms).
2. **Strip noise suffixes** — Remove trailing "file", "yaml", "json", "xml", "config" (these are format descriptors, not domain terms).
3. **Title-case each word** — "sentence diagram" becomes "Sentence Diagram".
4. **Deduplicate** — After cleaning, remove duplicate names (e.g., "context yaml" and "context map" both clean to have "context" as a component).
5. **Pick dominant name** — Use the single most frequent cleaned work object name as the context name. If tied, pick alphabetically first. Do NOT join multiple names with hyphens.

### Sequence / Flow

```
deriveName(actors, workObjects)
    |
    |-- for each workObject name:
    |     |-- cleanContextName(name) -> cleaned
    |     |-- add cleaned to frequency map
    |
    |-- pick highest-frequency cleaned name
    |     (tie-break: alphabetically first)
    |
    |-- if no work objects: fall back to actor-based name (same logic)
    |
    |-- return Title Cased single name (no hyphens)
```

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| **S**ingle Responsibility | `cleanContextName` handles string cleaning only; `deriveName` handles selection logic only |
| **O**pen/Closed | Adding new noise words to strip lists does not change function signatures |
| **L**iskov Substitution | Not applicable (no interfaces changed) |
| **I**nterface Segregation | Not applicable (no port changes) |
| **D**ependency Inversion | Not applicable (infrastructure-internal change) |

## TDD Workflow

### RED Phase

Write failing tests in `internal/discovery/infrastructure/algorithmic_detector_test.go`:

```go
// Test signatures (add to existing test file)
func TestDeriveName_WhenMultiWordWorkObjects_ReturnsDominantCleanedName(t *testing.T)
func TestDeriveName_WhenNoisePrefix_StripsUpdatedNew(t *testing.T)
func TestDeriveName_WhenNoiseSuffix_StripsFileYaml(t *testing.T)
func TestDeriveName_WhenDuplicatesAfterCleaning_Deduplicates(t *testing.T)
func TestDeriveName_WhenEmptyAfterCleaning_FallsBackToActors(t *testing.T)
func TestDeriveName_WhenNoWorkObjectsOrActors_ReturnsUnknown(t *testing.T)

// Integration-level test
func TestAlgorithmicDetector_WorkObjectCluster_ProducesCleanContextNames(t *testing.T)
```

Since `deriveName` is unexported, the unit tests will use the integration path through `DetectBoundaries` with crafted stories that have multi-word work object names. The integration test verifies end-to-end that names like "Sentence diagram-Story yaml file" no longer appear.

Run: `go test ./internal/discovery/infrastructure/ -run TestAlgorithmicDetector_WorkObjectCluster_ProducesCleanContextNames` -> should FAIL

### GREEN Phase

1. Add `cleanContextName` function to `internal/discovery/infrastructure/algorithmic_detector.go`
2. Modify `deriveName` to call `cleanContextName` on each work object name, use frequency-based selection, and return a single title-cased name

Run: `go test ./internal/discovery/infrastructure/ -run TestAlgorithmicDetector_WorkObjectCluster_ProducesCleanContextNames` -> should PASS

### REFACTOR Phase

- Extract noise-word lists as package-level `var` for maintainability
- Ensure all existing `algorithmic_detector_test.go` tests still pass
- Run full quality gates

## Steps

1. **Add integration test for clean names** — In `internal/discovery/infrastructure/algorithmic_detector_test.go`, add `TestAlgorithmicDetector_WorkObjectCluster_ProducesCleanContextNames` that creates stories with work objects like "sentence diagram", "story yaml file", "updated context yaml" and asserts the produced sketch names do NOT contain hyphens and DO contain title-cased domain terms. Run -> FAIL.

2. **Implement `cleanContextName` helper** — In `internal/discovery/infrastructure/algorithmic_detector.go`, add a private function `cleanContextName(name string) string` that: (a) lowercases, (b) strips noise prefixes ("updated", "new", "modified", "existing"), (c) strips noise suffixes ("file", "yaml", "json", "xml", "config"), (d) trims whitespace, (e) title-cases each word. Returns empty string if nothing remains after cleaning.

3. **Rewrite `deriveName` to use dominant-name selection** — Replace the current join-with-hyphens logic. For each work object, call `cleanContextName`, build a frequency map of cleaned names, pick the most frequent (tie-break: alphabetically first). Return a single title-cased name. Fall back to actors if all work object names clean to empty. Return "Unknown" if both are empty.

4. **Run all tests, verify existing tests unbroken** — `go test ./internal/discovery/infrastructure/ -v -race`. Existing tests may need name assertion updates since sketch names will change from hyphenated to single-term.

5. **Run quality gates** — `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `go test ./... -race`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `deriveName` never produces hyphenated names (no "-" in output)
- [ ] Work object names with noise prefixes ("Updated context yaml") produce clean domain names ("Context")
- [ ] Work object names with noise suffixes ("story yaml file") produce clean domain names ("Story")
- [ ] Multi-word domain terms are title-cased ("sentence diagram" -> "Sentence Diagram")
- [ ] When all work objects clean to empty, falls back to actor-based naming
- [ ] When both work objects and actors are empty, returns "Unknown"
- [ ] All existing `algorithmic_detector_test.go` tests pass (may need name assertion updates)
- [ ] LLM boundary detector path is unchanged (no modifications to `llm_boundary_detector.go`)
- [ ] `go build ./...` passes
- [ ] `go vet ./...` passes
- [ ] `golangci-lint run ./...` passes
- [ ] `go test ./... -race` passes with >= 80% coverage for changed code

## Edge Cases

| Case | Input | Expected Output |
|------|-------|-----------------|
| All noise words | "updated new yaml file" | "" (empty -> fall back to actors) |
| Single meaningful word | "invoice" | "Invoice" |
| Multi-word domain term | "sentence diagram" | "Sentence Diagram" |
| Noise prefix + domain term | "updated context yaml" | "Context" |
| Noise suffix only | "yaml file" | "" (empty -> fall back to actors) |
| Duplicate after cleaning | {"context map", "context yaml"} -> both clean to "Context" | "Context" (deduplicated) |
| Empty work objects | {} | Fall back to actors |
| Empty actors and work objects | {}, {} | "Unknown" |
| Already clean name | "Order" | "Order" |
| Mixed case input | "UPDATED Invoice" | "Invoice" |

## Quality Gates

```bash
go build ./...
go vet ./...
golangci-lint run ./...
go test ./... -race
```

- [ ] Build passes
- [ ] Vet passes
- [ ] Lint passes (zero issues)
- [ ] All tests pass with race detector

## Pre-Implementation Validation

- [ ] `deriveName` is called at lines 499 and 601 of `algorithmic_detector.go` — both call sites will benefit from the fix without changes
- [ ] `cleanContextName` is a new private helper — no existing interfaces change
- [ ] `BoundedContextSketch.NewBoundedContextSketch` accepts any non-empty trimmed string as name (`bounded_context_sketch.go:46-48`) — cleaned names will pass validation
- [ ] No constructor parameters change — no existing tests break from signature changes
- [ ] No external libraries needed — uses only `strings` stdlib package

## QA Before Close

- [ ] Happy path: stories with multi-word work objects produce clean, readable context names
- [ ] Edge cases covered (see Edge Cases section)
- [ ] Error handling: empty-after-cleaning falls back correctly
- [ ] No regressions: existing algorithmic detector tests pass (with updated name assertions)
- [ ] Domain layer untouched: no changes to `internal/discovery/domain/`

## Risks / Dependencies

- **Risk:** Existing tests assert specific sketch names (e.g., hyphenated names). These assertions will need updating in the GREEN/REFACTOR phase. This is expected and documented in Steps.
- **Risk:** If work object names in production stories are already clean single words (e.g., "Invoice", "Order"), the fix is a no-op for those cases. The fix only improves multi-word descriptive names.
- No formal dependencies (standalone bug fix).

title: Create 5-min meetup talk slide deck (Marp)
description:
## Goal / Problem

Create a polished Marp slide deck for a 5-minute meetup lightning talk about alto. The talk tells the personal story of evolving from markdown-based ticket tracking to Beads + DDD, and why domain discovery (DDD.md) was the missing piece that made AI-assisted coding actually sustainable.

## Background / Context

- **Reference deck:** `/home/kusanagi/AI/gpumod/docs/gpumod-5min.md` — same author, same Marp format, same meetup series. Follow the slide structure, CSS theming, and speaker-notes pattern.
- **Marp tooling:** VS Code extension `marp-team.marp-vscode` for preview and PDF export. Present from HTML export (GIF animations do not work in PPTX).
- **Talk structure:** ~2 min story + problem, ~2-3 min demo (pre-recorded VHS GIF), ~30s CTA.
- **Target audience:** Developers using AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) who ship fast but struggle with maintainability.
- **VHS terminal recorder:** Charmbracelet VHS v0.11.0 confirmed working on this machine. Produces deterministic GIF recordings from `.tape` scripts. Dependencies: ttyd v1.7.7, ffmpeg, google-chrome (all installed).

## Story Arc

1. **Personal journey** — Started using AI tools for coding. Created tickets with markdown files. Grew quickly, dependencies broke, hard to maintain.
2. **Beads helped** — Switched to Beads (https://github.com/steveyegge/beads, git-native issue tracking). Template-driven tickets with SOLID + TDD. Better, but still not enough.
3. **The missing piece** — Had README.md, PRD.md, ARCHITECTURE.md but NO DDD.md. Without domain discovery, AI tools build wrong abstractions. alto fills this gap: Domain Storytelling before coding.
4. **Demo** — Pre-recorded VHS GIF showing alto commands (detect, guide, generate). Deterministic, zero risk of failure.
5. **CTA** — Open source, Go, Apache 2.0.

## Design

|---|-------|---------|------|

- Output: `docs/alto-demo.gif` — embedded in slide 5 via `![w:1000](./alto-demo.gif)`

VHS settings:
```

```

### CSS Theme

- Follow gpumod deck pattern: custom CSS in frontmatter, Inter + JetBrains Mono fonts
- Adapt color palette to alto brand: midnight teal (oklch-based), not gpumod red/blue
- Section classes: title, problem, story, solution, demo, cheat, commands, cta
- Speaker notes in HTML comments with SAY:/TIMING:/TRANSITION: markers

## Grooming Notes

title: [Phase 7] EXISTING mode — alto guide --existing for doc-based domain inference
description:
## Goal / Problem

Epic alty-cli-1wu AC: "EXISTING mode infers domain from codebase (README + code structure)." No --existing flag, no inference flow, no CLI wiring exists. Users with existing codebases must start from a blank storytelling session rather than getting a model seeded from their docs.

This adds alto guide --existing which calls DocInferenceHandler.InferFromDocs, shows inference summary (confidence, source docs), asks user to confirm/decline/skip, and writes artifacts on confirmation. Falls through to normal storytelling if user declines or inference fails.

NOTE: This is NOT ModeExisting in Discovery's DiscoveryMode enum. It bypasses storytelling entirely when inference succeeds. DDD.md assigns gap analysis to Rescue (alto init --existing) and doc inference to Guided Discovery (alto guide --existing). Different bounded contexts, different flows.

## Background / Context

- DDD.md line 303: DocInference = "LLM's interpretation of domain model elements from existing documentation" — Guided Discovery context
- DDD.md line 277: Rescue Mode owns alto init --existing (gap analysis), NOT doc inference
- composition/app.go:237-240,270 — DocInferenceHandler fully wired (fsDocReader + llmDocReader + regexFallback)
- composition/app.go:227,270 — ArtifactGenerationHandler fully wired
- doc_inference_handler.go:31 — InferFromDocs(ctx, docsDir) (*InferenceResult, error)
- inference_result.go:32-43 — Model(), Confidence(), SourceDocs()
- guide.go:28-73 — current flags: --no-tui, --continue, --agent, --ingest, --legacy. No --existing.
- guide.go:88-90 — init guard: os.Stat(".alto/config.toml")
- guide.go:440-450 — markDiscoveryCompleted(".alto") already exists
- filesystem_doc_reader.go:25-49 — ReadDocs reads single dir (no recursion into subdirs)

**TL review fixes applied:**
- C1: GenerateArtifacts method doesn't exist on ArtifactGenerationHandler. Need GenerateFromModel(ctx, model, docsDir, projectDir) method or manual render+write.
- C2: ReadDocs(".") skips directories — misses docs/ subdir. Fix: try "docs" first, fallback to ".".
- I3: Sentinel error for "user declined" defined in discovery/domain/.
- I4: markDiscoveryCompleted called on "yes" path confirmed.

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | CLI orchestration (cmd/alto/commands/) + Discovery application layer (DocInferenceHandler, ArtifactGenerationHandler) |
| Ubiquitous Language | DocInference (DDD.md:303), InferenceConfirmation (DDD.md:305), InferenceResult (inference_result.go:13) |
| Layer | CLI calls application handlers. No new domain types. One new application method (GenerateFromModel). |

## Design

### Sequence

```
User                guide.go              DocInferenceHandler      Prompter
 |-- alto guide      |                         |                     |
 |   --existing ---->|                         |                     |
 |                   |-- init guard            |                     |
 |                   |-- InferFromDocs("docs") |                     |
 |                   |   (fallback to ".")   ->|                     |
 |                   |<-- InferenceResult      |                     |
 |                   |-- print summary         |                     |
 |                   |-- AskChoice(confirm?) --|-------------------->|
 |<-- prompt --------|                         |                     |
 |-- "yes" --------->|                         |                     |
 |                   |-- GenerateFromModel     |                     |
 |                   |-- markDiscoveryCompleted |                     |
 |<-- done           |                         |                     |
```

Three AskChoice outcomes:
- "y" (Yes, use inferred model): GenerateFromModel + markDiscoveryCompleted + return nil
- "n" (No, run guided storytelling): fall through to normal runGuide storytelling path
- "s" (Skip for now): return nil without marking completed

### Doc directory resolution

Try InferFromDocs("docs") first. If error (no docs found), try InferFromDocs("."). If both fail, print warning and fall through to storytelling. This handles standard layout (docs/) and flat layout (README.md at root).

### New method: GenerateFromModel

ArtifactGenerationHandler needs a new method since no existing method accepts *ddd.DomainModel directly:

```go
// GenerateFromModel renders and writes artifacts from an inferred domain model.
func (h *ArtifactGenerationHandler) GenerateFromModel(
    ctx context.Context,
    model *ddd.DomainModel,
    docsDir string,
    projectDir string,
) error
```

Follows same render+write pattern as GenerateFromStories (line 158-197).

### Sentinel for fallthrough

```go
// discovery/domain/errors.go or discovery_values.go
var ErrInferenceDismissed = errors.New("user dismissed inference result")
```

Used by runGuideExistingWithDeps when user selects "n". Caller (runGuideExisting) catches with errors.Is and calls runGuide for storytelling.

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| S | runGuideExisting: one job — call inference, display, confirm, write |
| O | NewGuideCmd extended with --existing flag; existing branches untouched |
| L | Same *composition.App used by all guide branches |
| I | StorytellingPrompter.AskChoice used for confirmation — no new interface |
| D | runGuideExistingWithDeps takes handler + prompter as params for testability |

## TDD Workflow

### RED Phase

File: cmd/alto/commands/guide_existing_test.go

```
TestGuideExisting_FlagRegistered
TestGuideExisting_NoConfig_ReturnsInitError
TestGuideExisting_NoDocsFound_FallsThrough
TestGuideExisting_LLMUnavailable_ShowsLowConfidence
TestGuideExisting_UserConfirms_MarksCompleted
TestGuideExisting_UserSkips_DoesNotMarkCompleted
TestGuideExisting_MutualExclusion_Agent
TestGuideExisting_MutualExclusion_Continue
TestGuideExisting_MutualExclusion_Legacy
TestGuideExisting_DocsDir_TriesDocsThenRoot
```

### GREEN Phase

1. Add --existing flag to guide.go NewGuideCmd
2. Add mutual exclusion guards
3. Add GenerateFromModel to ArtifactGenerationHandler
4. Implement runGuideExisting and runGuideExistingWithDeps
5. Add ErrInferenceDismissed sentinel
6. Wire doc dir resolution (try "docs" then ".")

### REFACTOR Phase

- Extract printInferenceSummary helper
- golangci-lint pass

## Steps

1. Add --existing flag to NewGuideCmd in guide.go. Register Bool("existing", false, "..."). Add mutual exclusion guards with --agent, --continue, --legacy.
2. Add ErrInferenceDismissed sentinel to discovery/domain/ (or shared errors).
3. Add GenerateFromModel method to ArtifactGenerationHandler — follows GenerateFromStories pattern.
4. Implement runGuideExisting in guide.go — wire prompter (noTUI selection), delegate to WithDeps form.
5. Implement runGuideExistingWithDeps — try InferFromDocs("docs"), fallback to "."; on success show summary + AskChoice; on "y" call GenerateFromModel + markDiscoveryCompleted; on "n" return ErrInferenceDismissed; on "s" return nil.
6. In runGuideExisting, catch ErrInferenceDismissed and call runGuide for storytelling fallthrough.
7. Write guide_existing_test.go with 10 test cases.
8. Update guide.go Long help text to document --existing.
9. Run all quality gates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] alto guide --existing is a recognized flag in --help output
- [ ] Without prior alto init (missing .alto/config.toml), returns "not initialized" error
- [ ] Calls InferFromDocs with "docs" first, falls back to "." — covers standard and flat layouts
- [ ] Displays confidence level and source doc names to stdout before confirmation
- [ ] On "yes": GenerateFromModel writes artifacts, markDiscoveryCompleted flips config.toml
- [ ] On "no": falls through to normal storytelling flow
- [ ] On "skip": exits with nil, discovery.completed remains false
- [ ] On inference failure (no docs found): prints warning and falls through to storytelling
- [ ] --existing is mutually exclusive with --agent, --continue, --legacy
- [ ] Does NOT add ModeExisting to DiscoveryMode enum
- [ ] GenerateFromModel method added to ArtifactGenerationHandler
- [ ] go test ./... -race passes (10+ new test cases)
- [ ] golangci-lint run ./... zero issues

## Edge Cases

| Case | Input | Expected |
|------|-------|----------|
| No .alto/config.toml | alto guide --existing | Error: "not initialized" |
| No .md files anywhere | InferFromDocs both dirs fail | Warning, falls through to storytelling |
| LLM unavailable | regex fallback, confidence="low" | Shows "low", confirmation offered |
| User Ctrl-C at prompt | AskChoice returns error | Error propagated |
| --existing + --agent | Both flags | Error: mutually exclusive |
| --existing + --continue | Both flags | Error: mutually exclusive |
| GenerateFromModel fails | Artifact write error | Error propagated with wrapping |

## Quality Gates

- [ ] go build ./... — zero errors
- [ ] go vet ./... — zero errors
- [ ] go test ./... -race — all pass
- [ ] golangci-lint run ./... — zero issues

## Pre-Implementation Validation

- [ ] app.DocInferenceHandler wired at composition/app.go:237-240,270
- [ ] app.ArtifactGenerationHandler wired at composition/app.go:227,270
- [ ] InferFromDocs(ctx, docsDir) signature at doc_inference_handler.go:31
- [ ] InferenceResult.Model(), Confidence(), SourceDocs() at inference_result.go:32-43
- [ ] AskChoice(ctx, prompt, []Choice, recommended) at ports.go:165-167
- [ ] markDiscoveryCompleted(altoDir) at guide.go:440 — same package, accessible
- [ ] init guard at guide.go:88-90 fires before --existing branch

title: [Phase 7] AskChoice re-grounding via prompt composition
description:
## Goal / Problem

Epic alty-cli-1wu AC: "One decision per interaction with re-grounding, plain-English explanation, recommendation, lettered options." AskChoice has lettered options and recommended parameter, but no mechanism re-states prior decisions before presenting a question. Users get decontextualised prompts without recap of what they already decided.

This ticket composes re-grounding text into the prompt string at each AskChoice call site. No interface changes — all adapters work unchanged.

## Background / Context

### Call sites (3 — TL review removed call site 1)

| 2 | cli_discovery_adapter.go:394 | "Would you like to tell another story?" (Resume) | Same — especially important after resume |
| 3 | storytelling_handler.go:223 | "This sentence contains branching..." | Story context helps decide whether to split |

| Bounded Context | Discovery |

## Design

### Data Models

| RegroundingContext | Application-layer struct | Snapshot of session state: Mode, Persona, StoryCount |

### Method Signatures

```go
// application/reground_prompt.go

    Mode       string
    Persona    string   // empty when not yet set
    StoryCount int
}

// NewRegroundingContext builds from a live session.

// BuildRegroundingPrompt prepends [Mode: X | Persona: Y | Stories told: N] header.

```

### Output Format

```

```

Rules:
- Zero-value RegroundingContext -> return basePrompt unchanged (safe for agent mode + tests)
- StoryCount == 0 -> omit "Stories told" field

title: [Phase 7] CoherenceValidator — cross-story contradiction detection
description:
## Goal / Problem

The GlossaryExtractor deduplicates terms across stories using case-insensitive merging (glossary_extractor.go:69) but does not validate whether the same term carries conflicting structural definitions across stories. A term declared as ActorTypePerson in one story and ActorTypeSystem in another represents a genuine contradiction in the ubiquitous language — both definitions survive into glossary.yaml without warning.

A second class of contradiction is undeclared references: StorySentence.Subject() and StorySentence.Object() may name an actor that appears nowhere in any story's Actors() list across the entire corpus. DomainStory.Validate() (domain_story.go:119) catches this within a single story, but cross-story referential integrity is not checked.

Closes AC gap on epic alty-cli-1wu: "Coherence validation flags contradictions between stories (same term different meaning, missing actors, etc.)" Scope is structural contradiction detection only — semantic contradictions (requires LLM) are out of scope.

## Background / Context

- Epic: alty-cli-1wu — Domain Storytelling Discovery Redesign (Phase 7 gap closure)
- glossary_extractor.go:62-91 — addOrMerge convention: case-insensitive key via strings.ToLower(term); on collision, higher trust wins; first definition preserved
- domain_story.go:213-225 — Actors(), WorkObjects(), Sentences() return defensive copies
- story_actor.go:114,117 — Name() string, Type() ActorType
- work_object.go:130,133 — Name() string, Type() WorkObjectType
- story_sentence.go:115,118,121,127,136 — Subject(), Activity(), Object(), IndirectObject(), HasIndirectObject()
- glossary_export_handler.go:26-53 — Export signature: (ctx, storyPaths, contextMap, outputPath) error
- ticket_implementability.go:21-32 — ImplementabilityFinding naming pattern reference
- Pattern: GlossaryExtractor (zero-value domain service, stateless)

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Guided Discovery |
| Ubiquitous Language | CoherenceValidator, CoherenceFinding, CoherenceReport, CoherenceSeverity (local to discovery domain — NOT FindingSeverity from ticket domain) |
| Layer | Domain (pure function, zero I/O) + Application (Export returns findings to caller) |

## Design

### Data Models

| Model | Type | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| CoherenceFinding | Value Object | Single contradiction: severity + location + description |
| CoherenceReport | Value Object | Aggregates findings from one validation run; immutable |
| CoherenceValidator | Domain Service | Stateless struct; Validate([]*DomainStory) CoherenceReport |
| CoherenceSeverity | Enum (string) | Local severity type — CoherenceSeverityWarning only |

### Method Signatures

```go
// domain/coherence_validator.go
type CoherenceSeverity string
const CoherenceSeverityWarning CoherenceSeverity = "warning"

type CoherenceFinding struct {
    severity    CoherenceSeverity
    location    string
    description string
}
func NewCoherenceFinding(severity CoherenceSeverity, location, description string) (CoherenceFinding, error)
func (f CoherenceFinding) Severity() CoherenceSeverity
func (f CoherenceFinding) Location() string
func (f CoherenceFinding) Description() string

type CoherenceReport struct { findings []CoherenceFinding }
func NewCoherenceReport(findings []CoherenceFinding) CoherenceReport
func (r CoherenceReport) Findings() []CoherenceFinding  // defensive copy
func (r CoherenceReport) IsCoherent() bool               // len == 0
func (r CoherenceReport) HasFindings() bool

type CoherenceValidator struct{}
func (v CoherenceValidator) Validate(stories []*DomainStory) CoherenceReport
```

### Detection Rules

Rule 1 — Term Type Conflict: Walk all stories. For each actor/work-object, collect strings.ToLower(name) -> type + storyTitle. On collision with different type, emit finding. Cross-dimension conflict (same name as actor in story A, work object in story B) also flagged.

Rule 2 — Cross-Story Undeclared Refs: Build global actor and work-object name sets across all stories. Walk every sentence. If Subject() not in global actor set -> finding. If Object() not in global actor set AND not in global work-object set -> finding. If HasIndirectObject() && IndirectObject() not in either set -> finding.

### Integration — GlossaryExportHandler

Export signature changes from error to ([]CoherenceFinding, error). Caller in cmd/ decides display. Validator inserted between story assembly (line 41) and extraction (line 43). Export still writes glossary.yaml regardless of findings.

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| S | CoherenceValidator has one job: detect structural contradictions |
| O | New detection rules are private methods; Validate contract unchanged |
| L | Value objects, no subtyping involved |
| I | No new port interface needed — domain service called directly |
| D | GlossaryExportHandler holds validator as zero-value struct field |

## TDD Workflow

### RED Phase

```
TestCoherenceValidator_Validate_EmptyStories
TestCoherenceValidator_Validate_SingleStory_NoConflicts
TestCoherenceValidator_Validate_ActorTypeConflict_AcrossStories
TestCoherenceValidator_Validate_WorkObjectTypeConflict_AcrossStories
TestCoherenceValidator_Validate_CrossDimensionConflict_ActorVsWorkObject
TestCoherenceValidator_Validate_CaseInsensitiveNormalization
TestCoherenceValidator_Validate_SameTermSameType_NoConflict
TestCoherenceValidator_Validate_UndeclaredCrossStoryRef_Subject
TestCoherenceValidator_Validate_CrossStoryValidRef_NotFlagged
TestCoherenceValidator_Validate_TrulyUndeclaredRef_NotInAnyStory
TestCoherenceValidator_Validate_IndirectObject_TrulyUndeclared
TestCoherenceValidator_Validate_MultipleConflicts_AllReturned
TestCoherenceFinding_Constructor_EmptyDescription_ReturnsError
TestCoherenceReport_Findings_DefensiveCopy
```

### GREEN Phase

1. Create coherence_validator.go — types and Validate
2. Modify glossary_export_handler.go — add validator, change Export return
3. Update Export callers for new return type

### REFACTOR Phase

- Verify case-insensitive normalization matches glossary_extractor.go:69
- Run golangci-lint, add DDD.md glossary entries

## Steps

1. Create internal/discovery/domain/coherence_validator_test.go — all RED tests
2. Create internal/discovery/domain/coherence_validator.go — types + service
3. Modify internal/discovery/application/glossary_export_handler.go — add validator, change return to ([]CoherenceFinding, error)
4. Update Export callers for new return signature
5. Add handler-level test for advisory warning path
6. Update docs/DDD.md glossary
7. Run all quality gates

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] CoherenceValidator.Validate identifies actors with same case-insensitive name but different ActorType across stories
- [ ] CoherenceValidator.Validate identifies work objects with same name but different WorkObjectType across stories
- [ ] CoherenceValidator.Validate flags cross-dimension conflicts (same name as actor in one story, work object in another)
- [ ] CoherenceValidator.Validate flags sentence subjects not declared as actors in any story in corpus
- [ ] CoherenceValidator.Validate does NOT flag sentence objects referencing actors/work-objects declared in a different story
- [ ] All name comparisons use strings.ToLower normalization
- [ ] CoherenceReport.Findings() returns defensive copy
- [ ] GlossaryExportHandler.Export returns ([]CoherenceFinding, error) — findings are advisory
- [ ] Export writes glossary.yaml even when contradictions found
- [ ] NewGlossaryExportHandler parameter list unchanged
- [ ] CoherenceValidator has zero imports outside discovery/domain + shared kernel + stdlib
- [ ] Severity type named CoherenceSeverity (not FindingSeverity)
- [ ] docs/DDD.md glossary updated
- [ ] go test ./... -race passes
- [ ] Domain coverage for coherence_validator.go >= 90%

## Edge Cases

| Case | Input | Expected |
|------|-------|----------|
| Nil stories | Validate(nil) | IsCoherent() true |
| Same term, same type, N stories | "Customer" ActorTypePerson x3 | No finding |
| Case variation, different type | "CUSTOMER" Person + "customer" System | 1 finding |
| Cross-dimension | "Invoice" as actor + work object | 1 finding |
| Valid cross-story ref | Subject in story B, actor declared in story A | No finding |
| Truly undeclared subject | "Ghost" not in any Actors() | 1 finding |
| Multiple conflicts | 3 type + 1 undeclared | All 4 returned |
| Empty description | NewCoherenceFinding("","","") | Error |

## Quality Gates

- [ ] go build ./... — zero errors
- [ ] go vet ./... — zero errors
- [ ] go test ./... -race — all pass
- [ ] golangci-lint run ./... — zero issues

## Pre-Implementation Validation

- [ ] GlossaryExtractor.Extract signature confirmed: glossary_extractor.go:17-20
- [ ] addOrMerge key normalization: strings.ToLower — glossary_extractor.go:69
- [ ] DomainStory.Actors() returns []StoryActor — domain_story.go:213-215
- [ ] StoryActor.Name(), Type() — story_actor.go:114,117
- [ ] WorkObject.Name(), Type() — work_object.go:130,133
- [ ] StorySentence.Subject(), Object(), IndirectObject(), HasIndirectObject() — story_sentence.go:115,121,127,136
- [ ] NewGlossaryExportHandler takes (reader, writer) — glossary_export_handler.go:18
- [ ] Export injection point: stories assembled by line 41, extraction at line 43

## Risks / Dependencies

- Risk: False positives on cross-story refs if global sets built per-story instead of corpus-first. Test guards against this.
- Risk: Export return signature change affects callers — small impact, grep for call sites.
- No blocking dependencies on open tickets.

title: PRD-aware stack detection — ExtractLanguageFromText + README fallback + genericSourceLayout rename
description:
## Goal / Problem

When a user runs `alto guide` in a project directory that has no `go.mod` or `pyproject.toml`, `stack.DetectProfile` returns `GenericProfile` and the generated artifacts hard-code Python defaults. If the project's README mentions a language explicitly (e.g., "This is a Go CLI tool" or "Built with Python"), alto should detect that and produce correct language-specific artifacts.

The fix decomposes into three precisely scoped changes:

1. Add `ExtractLanguageFromText(text string) string` to `internal/shared/infrastructure/stack/detector.go` — a pure keyword scan that returns a canonical language string (e.g., `"go"`, `"python"`). No profile construction here; that is domain logic.
2. Wire the fallback in `internal/composition/app.go`: after `DetectProfile` returns `GenericProfile`, read `README.md`, call `ExtractLanguageFromText`, and use the existing `discoverydomain.ResolveProfile` to map the language string to a `StackProfile`.
3. Rename `pythonSourceLayout()` to `genericSourceLayout()` in `internal/discovery/infrastructure/markdown_artifact_renderer.go` — this function is the generic fallback for any profile whose `SourceLayout()` returns nil, not a Python-specific function.

## Background / Context

- `stack.DetectProfile` at `internal/shared/infrastructure/stack/detector.go:14` returns `vo.GenericProfile{}` when no manifest file exists.
- `discoverydomain.ResolveProfile` at `internal/discovery/domain/stack_resolver.go:12` already maps `"go"` → `GoModProfile`, `"python"` → `PythonUvProfile`, anything else → `GenericProfile`. No new domain code is needed.
- `vo.NewTechStack(language, packageManager string) TechStack` at `internal/shared/domain/valueobjects/tech_stack.go:15` is the correct constructor.
- `vo.GenericProfile{}` is a concrete struct at `internal/shared/domain/valueobjects/stack_profile.go:71`. Type assertion `_, ok := profile.(vo.GenericProfile)` is correct.
- `internal/composition/adapters.go:12` already imports `discoverydomain`. Adding the same import to `app.go` is a per-file addition, not a new cross-context dependency.
- `sourceLayoutBlock` at `markdown_artifact_renderer.go:64` calls `pythonSourceLayout()` as fallback when `dirs` is nil or empty.
- `stackProfile` in `app.go` is assigned at line 129, consumed at lines 132 and 142 — the fallback block must be inserted between these.

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Shared Kernel (`internal/shared/infrastructure/stack`) for text parsing; Discovery (`internal/discovery/domain`) for profile resolution; Composition Root (`internal/composition`) for wiring |
| Ubiquitous Language | `StackProfile`, `TechStack`, `GenericProfile`, `ResolveProfile` |
| Layer | `ExtractLanguageFromText`: Infrastructure (pure text parsing). Fallback chain: Composition Root (wiring only). `genericSourceLayout` rename: Infrastructure (rendering adapter). |

## Design

### Sequence / Flow

```
app.go / NewApp()
    |-- stack.DetectProfile(projectDir) --> GoModProfile or PythonUvProfile
    |       if result is vo.GenericProfile{}
    |           os.ReadFile("README.md")
    |           stack.ExtractLanguageFromText(readmeText) --> "go" | "python" | ""
    |               if lang != ""
    |                   ts := vo.NewTechStack(lang, "")
    |                   discoverydomain.ResolveProfile(&ts) --> GoModProfile | PythonUvProfile
    stackProfile (vo.StackProfile)
    |-- discoveryinfra.NewMarkdownArtifactRenderer(stackProfile)
    |-- fitnessinfra.NewSubprocessGateRunner("", stackProfile)
```

### Method Signatures

```go
// internal/shared/infrastructure/stack/detector.go
func ExtractLanguageFromText(text string) string
```

Keyword list is an ordered slice of `struct{ keyword, lang string }`, not a map.
Go group: `"go.mod"`, `"golang"`, `" go "`, `"package main"`.
Python group: `"python"`, `"pyproject"`, `"pip install"`, `".py"`.
Uses `strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(text), keyword)`. Returns first match.

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| S | `ExtractLanguageFromText` does only keyword scanning. Profile construction is `ResolveProfile`'s job. |
| O | Adding new language keywords extends `ExtractLanguageFromText` without touching other components. |
| L | `GoModProfile`, `PythonUvProfile`, `GenericProfile` all satisfy `StackProfile`. |
| I | `ExtractLanguageFromText` takes `string`, returns `string` — no coupling to ports. |
| D | `artifactRenderer` and `gateRunner` depend on `vo.StackProfile` interface, not concrete types. |

## TDD Workflow

### RED Phase

`internal/shared/infrastructure/stack/detector_test.go` — add:
```
TestExtractLanguageFromText_WhenGoModMentioned_ExpectGo
TestExtractLanguageFromText_WhenGolangMentioned_ExpectGo
TestExtractLanguageFromText_WhenPythonMentioned_ExpectPython
TestExtractLanguageFromText_WhenPyprojectMentioned_ExpectPython
TestExtractLanguageFromText_WhenEmptyText_ExpectEmptyString
TestExtractLanguageFromText_WhenUnrecognizedLanguage_ExpectEmptyString
TestExtractLanguageFromText_WhenBothGoAndPython_ExpectGo
TestExtractLanguageFromText_WhenCaseInsensitiveGolang_ExpectGo
```

### GREEN Phase
1. Add `ExtractLanguageFromText` to `detector.go`
2. Rename `pythonSourceLayout` → `genericSourceLayout` in `markdown_artifact_renderer.go` (line 77 decl, line 67 call)
3. Wire the fallback in `app.go`

### REFACTOR Phase
- Verify keyword order comment explains deterministic precedence
- Verify `sourceLayoutBlock` comment updated to reference `genericSourceLayout`
- Run full quality gates

## Steps

1. Add `ExtractLanguageFromText` to `internal/shared/infrastructure/stack/detector.go` after `DetectProfile`.
2. Rename `pythonSourceLayout` → `genericSourceLayout` in `markdown_artifact_renderer.go` (function decl + call site).
3. Wire README fallback in `app.go` between line 129 and 132. Add `discoverydomain` and `path/filepath` imports.
4. Write tests in `detector_test.go` with BDD naming convention.
5. Run all quality gates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `stack.ExtractLanguageFromText("This project uses Go modules and go.mod")` returns `"go"`
- [ ] `stack.ExtractLanguageFromText("Built with Python and pyproject.toml")` returns `"python"`
- [ ] `stack.ExtractLanguageFromText("No language mentioned")` returns `""`
- [ ] `stack.ExtractLanguageFromText("")` returns `""`
- [ ] When both `"golang"` and `"python"` appear in text, Go wins (deterministic precedence)
- [ ] `stack.ExtractLanguageFromText` is case-insensitive
- [ ] `pythonSourceLayout` no longer exists as a function name (grep returns zero)
- [ ] `genericSourceLayout` referenced in `sourceLayoutBlock`
- [ ] When `DetectProfile` returns `GenericProfile` and README contains `"golang"`, `NewApp` produces `StackID() == "go-mod"`
- [ ] When README is absent, `stackProfile` remains `GenericProfile`, no error
- [ ] When `go.mod` present, README fallback NOT consulted
- [ ] All existing tests pass with no regressions
- [ ] `golangci-lint run ./...` reports zero issues

## Edge Cases

| Case | Input | Expected Output |
|------|-------|-----------------|
| Empty text | `""` | `""` |
| Unrecognized language | `"This is a Rust project"` | `""` |
| Both Go and Python | `"golang python"` | `"go"` (Go checked first) |
| Case variation | `"GOLANG"` | `"go"` |
| README absent | `os.ReadFile` fails | `GenericProfile` retained, no error |
| `go.mod` present + Python README | Manifest detection fires first | `GoModProfile` (manifest wins) |
| Nil dirs in `sourceLayoutBlock` | `dirs` is `nil` | calls `genericSourceLayout()` |

## Quality Gates

- [ ] `go build ./...` — zero errors
- [ ] `go vet ./...` — zero errors
- [ ] `golangci-lint run ./...` — zero issues
- [ ] `go test ./... -race` — all pass

## Pre-Implementation Validation

- [x] `vo.NewTechStack(language, packageManager string)` exists — `tech_stack.go:15`
- [x] `discoverydomain.ResolveProfile(*vo.TechStack)` exists — `stack_resolver.go:12`

title: fix: bootstrap no longer stubs docs that artifact pipeline owns
description:
## Goal / Problem

When `alto init -y --no-commit` chains to `alto guide`, bootstrap creates stub `docs/DDD.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/PRD.md` (3-line TODOs). The artifact pipeline then writes real content to the same paths. `ConflictDetectingFileWriter` detects the stubs and renames the real content to `_alto` suffix files. User gets stubs as primary filenames, real content hidden.

The fix: remove `docs/PRD.md`, `docs/DDD.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` from bootstrap's `plannedFiles`. These files are owned by the artifact pipeline.

Discovered during E2E simulation alty-cli-3k3 (round 4), Issue #2.

## Background / Context

- `bootstrap_handler.go:34-42` — `plannedFiles` declares all three artifact-pipeline paths
- `content.go:20-33` — `ContentFor` returns "TODO: Fill in content." stub for docs
- `artifact_generation_handler.go:113-133` — `WriteArtifacts` targets `docs/PRD.md`, `docs/DDD.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`
- `conflict_detecting_file_writer.go:40-75` — detects existing files, renames with `_alto` suffix
- `composition/app.go:124-126` — both handlers share the same `fileWriter`
- `init.go:153` — `runInit` chains directly to `runGuide`

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Bootstrap |
| Ubiquitous Language | `plannedFiles`, `FileAction`, `ContentProvider`, `PreviewAction` |
| Layer | Application (bootstrap_handler.go) — no domain or shared kernel changes |

## Design

Remove 3 entries from `plannedFiles` at `bootstrap_handler.go:34-42`:
- `"docs/PRD.md"` — owned by artifact pipeline
- `"docs/DDD.md"` — owned by artifact pipeline
- `"docs/ARCHITECTURE.md"` — owned by artifact pipeline

Remaining: `"AGENTS.md"`, `".alto/config.toml"`, `".alto/knowledge/_index.toml"`, `".alto/maintenance/doc-registry.toml"`.

**Additional fixes (from TL review):**
1. Update comment at `content.go:29` — AGENTS.md is the only remaining default-case file
2. Add comment at `content.go:108-120` — doc-registry entries are forward references for artifact pipeline
3. Update all bootstrap tests that enumerate plannedFiles (lines 176, 336, 437, 451-454, 558 in bootstrap_handler_test.go)

No changes to: ConflictDetectingFileWriter, ArtifactGenerationHandler, composition/app.go, init.go.

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| S | Fix restores SRP — bootstrap owns scaffolding, artifact pipeline owns DDD/arch/PRD |
| O | No interfaces modified |
| L | N/A |
| I | No interface changes |
| D | No dependency changes |

## TDD Workflow

### RED
- Assert docs/PRD.md, DDD.md, ARCHITECTURE.md absent from Preview().FileActions()
- Assert Execute does not call WriteFile for those paths
- Assert AGENTS.md is still present and written

### GREEN
Remove 3 paths from plannedFiles. Update content.go comments.

### REFACTOR
Update existing bootstrap tests. Run quality gates.

## Steps

1. Write RED tests asserting absence of 3 doc paths
2. Remove 3 paths from plannedFiles at bootstrap_handler.go:34
3. Update content.go:29 comment (AGENTS.md is only remaining default)
4. Add forward-reference comment at content.go:108-120
5. Update all existing bootstrap tests that enumerate plannedFiles
6. Run quality gates

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After init+guide, docs/DDD.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, PRD.md contain real generated content
- [ ] No _alto suffixed docs files created in chained flow
- [ ] AGENTS.md, .alto/config.toml, knowledge/, maintenance/ still created by bootstrap
- [ ] Preview() does not include the 3 artifact-pipeline paths
- [ ] Standalone alto guide still writes artifacts normally
- [ ] User's hand-crafted docs still trigger ConflictDetectingFileWriter rename
- [ ] All quality gates pass

## Edge Cases

| Case | Expected |
|------|----------|
| init-only (no guide) | docs/ dir exists but PRD/DDD/ARCH don't — correct |
| User has hand-crafted DDD.md | ConflictDetectingFileWriter still renames — unchanged |
| Standalone guide | Writes artifacts normally — no regression |
| Repeated init | AGENTS.md skipped, .alto/* skipped — unchanged |
| --dry-run | Preview shows only AGENTS.md + .alto/* as creates |

## Quality Gates

- [ ] `go vet ./...` zero errors
