title: fix: skip writing bounded_context_map.yaml when empty in story-based artifact pipeline
description:
## Goal / Problem

`GenerateFromStories` in the story-based discovery path calls `WriteArtifacts` with an `ArtifactPreview` whose `BoundedContextMapYAML` field is always the empty string. `WriteArtifacts` unconditionally passes that empty string to `h.writer.WriteFile`, producing a 0-byte `.alto/bounded_context_map.yaml` file.

The `alto fitness` command reads `.alto/bounded_context_map.yaml` to generate arch-go rules (`cmd/alto/commands/fitness.go:74`). A 0-byte file there causes fitness to fail or produce empty output on the very session that just ran the full story-based guide flow. Meanwhile, the real boundary data is correctly persisted to `.alto/context-map.yaml` by `runBoundaryDetection` in `cli_discovery_adapter.go:344`.

The fix is a single guard in `WriteArtifacts`: skip the write when `BoundedContextMapYAML` is empty.

Discovered during E2E simulation alty-cli-3k3 (round 4), Issue #1.

## Background / Context

1. `GenerateFromStories` assembles an `ArtifactPreview` at `artifact_generation_handler.go:188-193` without setting `BoundedContextMapYAML`. The field defaults to `""`.
2. `WriteArtifacts` at `artifact_generation_handler.go:128-131` unconditionally writes that empty string to `.alto/bounded_context_map.yaml`.
3. The Q&A path (`BuildPreview`, lines 96-107) correctly populates `BoundedContextMapYAML` by calling `renderBoundedContextMapYAML(model)`.
4. The real context map for the story path is written by `runBoundaryDetection` in `cli_discovery_adapter.go:344`.
5. Two MCP callers at `mcp/tools_bootstrap.go:218` and `mcp/tools_bootstrap.go:618` both use `BuildPreview` first — unaffected by the guard.
6. `TestArtifactGenerationHandler_WriteArtifacts / "writes four files"` at line 220-254 exercises Q&A path — must stay green (4 files).
7. `TestArtifactGenerationHandler_GenerateFromStories_HappyPath` at line 1021 asserts `>= 3` — update to `== 3`.

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Discovery — `internal/discovery/application/` |
| Ubiquitous Language | `ArtifactPreview`, `BoundedContextMapYAML`, `WriteArtifacts`, `GenerateFromStories` |
| Layer | Application — no domain or infrastructure changes |

## Design

Single guard in `WriteArtifacts` at `artifact_generation_handler.go:128`:

```go
if preview.BoundedContextMapYAML != "" {
    bcMapPath := filepath.Join(projectDir, ".alto", "bounded_context_map.yaml")
    if err := h.writer.WriteFile(ctx, bcMapPath, preview.BoundedContextMapYAML); err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("write bounded context map: %w", err)
    }
}
```

No other production files require modification.

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| S | Guard is local to WriteArtifacts, same concern |
| O | No interfaces modified |
| L | ArtifactPreview contract unchanged — BoundedContextMapYAML was always optional |
| I | FileWriter interface untouched |
| D | No new dependencies |

## TDD Workflow

### RED
- `TestArtifactGenerationHandler_GenerateFromStories_DoesNotWriteBCMap` — assert writer.written does NOT contain "bounded_context_map.yaml"
- `TestArtifactGenerationHandler_WriteArtifacts_SkipsBCMapWhenEmpty` — assert exactly 3 files written when BoundedContextMapYAML == ""
- Update `TestArtifactGenerationHandler_GenerateFromStories_HappyPath` from `>= 3` to `== 3`

### GREEN
Apply the single guard at line 128.

### REFACTOR
Run quality gates. Verify Q&A path test ("writes four files") still passes.

## Steps

1. Write RED tests
2. Apply guard in WriteArtifacts
3. Update HappyPath test assertion
4. Run quality gates

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] GenerateFromStories no longer writes .alto/bounded_context_map.yaml
- [ ] WriteArtifacts with empty BoundedContextMapYAML writes exactly 3 files
- [ ] WriteArtifacts with non-empty BoundedContextMapYAML (Q&A path) still writes 4 files
- [ ] HappyPath test updated to assert == 3
- [ ] All existing tests pass with no regressions
- [ ] All quality gates pass

## Edge Cases

| Case | Expected |
|------|----------|
| Story path, no context map | 3 files written, no bounded_context_map.yaml |
| Q&A path with populated YAML | 4 files written, unchanged |
| BoundedContextMapYAML is whitespace | Treated as non-empty — guard is != "", do NOT use TrimSpace |
| Empty ArtifactPreview{} | All fields empty, guard skips bcmap write |

## Quality Gates

- [ ] `go build ./...` zero errors
- [ ] `go vet ./...` zero errors
- [ ] `golangci-lint run ./...` zero issues
- [ ] `go test ./... -race` all pass

## Pre-Implementation Validation

- [x] Line 188-193: GenerateFromStories builds ArtifactPreview without BoundedContextMapYAML
- [x] Line 128-131: WriteArtifacts unconditional write confirmed
- [x] Line 96-107: BuildPreview correctly populates BoundedContextMapYAML
- [x] Two MCP callers use BuildPreview first — unaffected
- [x] Composition root at app.go:225 — no wiring changes needed
- [x] Line 1021: HappyPath asserts >= 3 (needs tightening to == 3)

## Risks / Dependencies

- No blocking dependencies
- MCP callers unaffected (both use BuildPreview which populates the field)
- Future story path population of BoundedContextMapYAML would automatically be picked up by the guard

title: fix: strip subtitle from README H1 when extracting project name
description:
## Goal / Problem

resolveProjectName() returns the full H1 README heading verbatim, including any tagline/subtitle after a separator character. When a project README begins with # kura — Personal Knowledge Garden for Developers, both config.toml and context-map.yaml receive the full string as the project name instead of just "kura".

Two callers are affected:
- cmd/alto/commands/init.go:92 → populates domain.ProjectConfig → written to config.toml
- internal/discovery/infrastructure/cli_discovery_adapter.go:236 → populates domain.ContextMap → written to context-map.yaml

## Background / Context

The basic README H1-extraction logic was added for alty-cli-vhs, but subtitle stripping was not in scope. Both implementations use strings.CutPrefix(line, "# ") then strings.TrimSpace(after) returned as-is.

Bug sites (verified):
- cmd/alto/commands/init.go:229-234 — returns full heading
- internal/discovery/infrastructure/cli_discovery_adapter.go:353-359 — identical logic

Existing tests (no separator coverage):
- cmd/alto/commands/resolve_project_name_test.go — 6 tests, all plain headings
- internal/discovery/infrastructure/resolve_project_name_test.go — 2 tests, same

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Bootstrap (cmd/alto/commands) and Discovery (internal/discovery/infrastructure) |
| Ubiquitous Language | ProjectName — the short identifier for a project |
| Layer | Infrastructure only — no domain changes |

## Design

Add private stripSubtitle(heading string) string helper in each file. Scans for first occurrence of known separator, returns text before it:

Separators (checked in order, earliest match wins):
  " — "   (em dash U+2014 with surrounding spaces)
  " - "   (ASCII hyphen with surrounding spaces)
  ": "    (colon + space)
  " | "   (pipe with surrounding spaces)

Guard: idx > 0 ensures empty-before-separator falls back to full heading.

Duplication rationale: the two resolveProjectName implementations are already duplicated (standalone function in cmd/ vs method on CLIDiscoveryAdapter). Per project conventions: "Three similar lines of code is better than a premature abstraction."

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| SRP | stripSubtitle does one thing: strip subtitle from heading string |
| OCP | New separator patterns added to slice without modifying call sites |

## TDD Workflow

### RED
- TestResolveProjectName_WhenH1HasEmDashSubtitle_ReturnsNameOnly
- TestResolveProjectName_WhenH1HasHyphenSubtitle_ReturnsNameOnly
- TestResolveProjectName_WhenH1HasColonSubtitle_ReturnsNameOnly
- TestResolveProjectName_WhenH1HasPipeSubtitle_ReturnsNameOnly
- TestResolveProjectName_WhenH1IsHyphenatedNameNoSubtitle_ReturnsFullName
- TestCLIDiscoveryAdapter_resolveProjectName_WhenH1HasEmDashSubtitle_ReturnsNameOnly
- TestCLIDiscoveryAdapter_resolveProjectName_WhenH1IsHyphenatedNameNoSubtitle_ReturnsFullName

### GREEN
1. Add stripSubtitle to init.go, update resolveProjectName line 234
2. Add stripSubtitle to cli_discovery_adapter.go, update line 359

### REFACTOR
Verify separator order. Run golangci-lint.

## Steps

1. Add RED tests to cmd/alto/commands/resolve_project_name_test.go (5 new tests)
2. Add RED tests to internal/discovery/infrastructure/resolve_project_name_test.go (2 new tests)
3. Implement stripSubtitle in init.go, update resolveProjectName
4. Implement stripSubtitle in cli_discovery_adapter.go, update resolveProjectName
5. Run full quality gates

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] resolveProjectName returns "kura" for all 4 separator patterns
- [ ] resolveProjectName returns "my-project" unchanged for hyphenated names (no subtitle)
- [ ] All existing tests continue to pass
- [ ] config.toml written during alto init contains name = "kura" (not full heading)
- [ ] context-map.yaml written during alto guide contains project: kura

## Edge Cases

| Case | Input | Expected |
|------|-------|----------|
| Em dash | # kura — Personal Knowledge Garden | "kura" |
| Hyphen with spaces | # kura - A CLI tool | "kura" |
| Colon | # kura: Personal Knowledge Garden | "kura" |
| Pipe | # kura | Fast Knowledge Capture | "kura" |
| Hyphenated name, no subtitle | # my-project | "my-project" |
| Plain name | # MyProject | "MyProject" |
| Separator at start (idx=0) | # — subtitle only | full heading returned |
| No README | directory only | filepath.Base(absDir) |
| Multiple separators | # kura — foo - bar | "kura" (first match) |

## Quality Gates

- [ ] go build ./... — zero errors
- [ ] go vet ./... — zero errors
- [ ] golangci-lint run ./... — zero issues
- [ ] go test ./... -race — all pass

## Pre-Implementation Validation

- [x] init.go:221-241 — resolveProjectName exists, bug at line 234
- [x] cli_discovery_adapter.go:336-366 — resolveProjectName exists, bug at line 359
- [x] Single caller each: init.go:92 and cli_discovery_adapter.go:236
- [x] resolve_project_name_test.go exists in both packages, no separator tests
- [x] No external libraries needed — strings.Index and strings.TrimSpace are stdlib
- [x] No new files needed

## Risks / Dependencies

- No blocking dependencies. Self-contained string-processing fix.
- Low risk: project names legitimately containing " - " or ": " would be truncated. Mitigated by requiring surrounding spaces for hyphen. Acceptable trade-off.

title: qa: E2E re-simulation of kura bootstrap after bug fixes
description:
## Goal / Problem

Re-run the full E2E user simulation (originally alty-cli-3k3) after all bug fixes are applied. The original simulation found 5 bugs — 3 fixed in alty-cli-9xm (shared scanner, MkdirAll, last_actor interpolation), 2 addressed in alty-cli-m6h (boundary detector fallback) and alty-cli-vhs (README project name). This ticket validates that all fixes work end-to-end.

## Background / Context

- Original simulation: alty-cli-3k3 (PARTIAL PASS — bugs found)
- Bug fix tickets: alty-cli-9xm (CLOSED), alty-cli-m6h (OPEN), alty-cli-vhs (OPEN)
- Test input: .notes/side-project/README.md (kura project README), .notes/side-project/PRD.md (domain reference)
- Side project dir cleaned to only PRD.md + README.md — ready for fresh simulation

## Simulation Phases

### Phase 1: Setup

title: fix: derive project name from README heading in init and guide flows
description:
## Goal / Problem

alto init writes project.name = "kura-sim" into .alto/config.toml — the directory name — instead of "kura", which is the actual project name in the README # kura heading. Same defect in alto guide: context-map.yaml uses the directory name as project.

**Desired behavior:** Both config.toml and context-map.yaml should use the first # Heading from README.md as the project name, falling back to filepath.Base(projectDir) when no README or no heading is found.

## Background / Context

**Call site 1 — config.toml (bootstrap flow)**
- File: cmd/alto/commands/init.go:92
- Code: projectName := filepath.Base(mustAbs(projectDir))
- Passed to domain.NewProjectConfig(projectName, ...) at line 93

**Call site 2 — context-map.yaml (discovery flow)**
- File: internal/discovery/infrastructure/cli_discovery_adapter.go:333-347
- Method: (a *CLIDiscoveryAdapter) resolveProjectName() (string, error)
- Currently: os.Getwd() then filepath.Base(dir)

**Arch constraint:** arch-go.yml forbids cross-context imports between bootstrap and discovery. The ~10-line README-reading logic must be duplicated as private helpers in each location.

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Bootstrap (config.toml) + Discovery (context-map.yaml) |
| Ubiquitous Language | ProjectName — human-readable name sourced from project documentation |
| Layer | Infrastructure / CLI cmd — file-system I/O, no domain changes |

## Design

### New helper in cmd/alto/commands/init.go

```go
func resolveProjectName(projectDir string) string {
    for _, candidate := range []string{"README.md", "README"} {
        content, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(projectDir, candidate))
        if err != nil {
            continue
        }
        for _, line := range strings.Split(string(content), "\n") {
            if after, ok := strings.CutPrefix(line, "# "); ok {
                if name := strings.TrimSpace(after); name != "" {
                    return name
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return filepath.Base(mustAbs(projectDir))
}
```

**Note:** init.go version is infallible (no error return) — matches current call site pattern. mustAbs is incorporated into fallback path, so it remains used.

Replace init.go:92 inline expression with resolveProjectName(projectDir).

### Updated method in cli_discovery_adapter.go:333-347

Same logic but returns (string, error) to match existing method signature. Adds "strings" to imports.

### Sequence

```
runInit()
    |-- resolveProjectName(".") --> checks README.md, README
    |                              --> returns "kura" OR filepath.Base()
    |-- domain.NewProjectConfig("kura", ...)

CLIDiscoveryAdapter.Complete()
    |-- a.resolveProjectName() --> checks README.md, README
    |                            --> returns "kura" OR filepath.Base()
    |-- domain.NewContextMap("kura", ...)
```

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| S | Each helper has one job: resolve best available project name |
| O | No existing behavior modified, only source of name changes |
| L | Not applicable — no interfaces changed |
| I | Not applicable — no new interfaces |
| D | Both use stdlib only; no new abstractions needed |

## TDD Workflow

### RED Phase

cmd/alto/commands/init_test.go:
- TestResolveProjectName_WhenReadmeMdHasH1_ReturnsHeading
- TestResolveProjectName_WhenNoReadme_FallsBackToBaseName
- TestResolveProjectName_WhenReadmeHasNoH1_FallsBackToBaseName
- TestResolveProjectName_WhenReadmeExistsButNoMd_ReturnsHeading
- TestResolveProjectName_WhenReadmeMdEmpty_FallsBackToBaseName
- TestResolveProjectName_WhenH1HasExtraSpaces_ReturnsTrimmed

internal/discovery/infrastructure/cli_discovery_adapter_test.go:
- TestCLIDiscoveryAdapter_resolveProjectName_WhenReadmeMdHasH1_ReturnsHeading
- TestCLIDiscoveryAdapter_resolveProjectName_WhenNoReadme_FallsBackToBaseName

### GREEN Phase
1. Add resolveProjectName to init.go, replace line 92
2. Replace body of resolveProjectName() in cli_discovery_adapter.go, add "strings" import

### REFACTOR Phase
- Verify mustAbs still used (incorporated in fallback)
- Run full quality gates

## Steps

1. Write tests (RED)
2. Add resolveProjectName helper to init.go, replace line 92 expression
3. Update cli_discovery_adapter.go resolveProjectName() body, add "strings" import
4. Run quality gates

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] alto init in dir with README.md "# kura" produces config.toml name = "kura"
- [ ] alto guide in same dir produces context-map.yaml project: kura

- [ ] README with no # heading falls back to dir base name

| Extra spaces | #  My App   | "My App" (trimmed) |

title: fix: AlgorithmicDetector falls back to work-object clustering when no boundary signals found
description:
## Goal / Problem

When AlgorithmicDetector.DetectBoundaries processes stories from a simple single-developer domain (e.g. kura CLI), all three heuristics return 0 signals and the method returns nil, nil — the user sees no bounded context proposals at all.

**Root cause:** algorithmic_detector.go:64-66 silently returns nil, nil when len(allSignals) == 0. The three heuristics require structural patterns (multi-actor flows, org splits, cross-story verb divergence) that do not appear in small, single-developer domains.

**Outcome needed:** When all three heuristics produce 0 signals, the detector falls back to a 4th heuristic — detectWorkObjectClusters — that groups stories by shared work objects and emits one BoundedContextSketch per cluster.

## Background / Context

- Failing guard: internal/discovery/infrastructure/algorithmic_detector.go:64-66
- Three existing heuristics: detectSameObjectDiffContext (:90), detectOneWayFlow (:169), detectOrgBoundary (:335) — all require cross-story actor/object diversity
- Signal type registry: internal/discovery/domain/boundary_signal.go:36-46 (validSignalTypes map)
- AllSignalTypes() function: internal/discovery/domain/boundary_signal.go:59-71
- Scoring formula: internal/discovery/domain/boundary_scoring.go:26-33
- BoundedContextSketch constructor: internal/discovery/domain/bounded_context_sketch.go:35-84
- Reusable helpers: buildWorkObjectNameSet (:621), buildActorNameSet (:633), deriveName (:581), setToSlice (:645)
- Test helper: algorithmic_detector_test.go:26 (makeStoryWithActorsAndObjects)

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Discovery |
| Ubiquitous Language | BoundarySignal, BoundedContextSketch, WorkObject, DomainStory, AlgorithmicDetector, SignalType |
| Layer | Domain (signal type + scoring constant) + Infrastructure (fallback heuristic) |

## Design

### Data Models

| Model | Type | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| SignalTypeWorkObjectCluster | SignalType constant (domain) | New signal type for fallback heuristic |
| BaseConfidenceWorkObjectCluster | float64 constant (domain) | Base confidence 0.15 — intentionally lowest, signals "inferred from structure only" |
| detectWorkObjectClusters | private method on AlgorithmicDetector | 4th heuristic: cluster stories by shared work objects |

### Domain Touch Points (ALL 3 REQUIRED)

1. Add SignalTypeWorkObjectCluster to const block in boundary_signal.go
2. Add entry to validSignalTypes map in boundary_signal.go:36-46 — without this, NewBoundarySignal rejects the type at runtime
3. Add to AllSignalTypes() return slice in boundary_signal.go:59-71

### Algorithm: detectWorkObjectClusters

1. Build index: workObjectName (lowercase) -> []storyIndex
2. Union-find over story indices — union stories sharing any work object name
3. Group story indices by union-find root
4. For each group: collect actors/WOs/titles, create BoundarySignal(WorkObjectCluster), compute score, build BoundedContextSketch
5. Sort sketches by name for deterministic output

### Integration Point

Replace guard at algorithmic_detector.go:64-66:
```go
// BEFORE: return nil, nil
// AFTER:  return d.detectWorkObjectClusters(stories)
```

### Sequence / Flow

```
DetectBoundaries(ctx, stories, mode)
    |-- detectSameObjectDiffContext --> []signalWithContext
    |-- detectOneWayFlow            --> []signalWithContext
    |-- detectOrgBoundary           --> []signalWithContext
    |
    |-- len(allSignals) == 0?
    |       YES --> detectWorkObjectClusters(stories) --> []BoundedContextSketch
    |       NO  --> clusterAndScore(allSignals)       --> []BoundedContextSketch
```

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| S | detectWorkObjectClusters has one job: cluster by WO when primary heuristics yield nothing |
| O | Existing heuristics untouched; new private method extends behavior |
| L | AlgorithmicDetector still satisfies BoundaryDetector interface |
| I | BoundaryDetector port (ports.go:211-213) unchanged |
| D | BoundaryDetectionHandler depends on interface, not concrete |

## TDD Workflow

### RED Phase

```
TestAlgorithmicDetector_WorkObjectCluster_FallbackWhenNoSignals
TestAlgorithmicDetector_WorkObjectCluster_SharedWOsMergeIntoOneCluster
TestAlgorithmicDetector_WorkObjectCluster_UniqueWOsProduceMultipleSketches
TestAlgorithmicDetector_WorkObjectCluster_PrimarySignalsSuppressFallback
TestAlgorithmicDetector_WorkObjectCluster_ConfidenceIsLow
```

### GREEN Phase
1. Add SignalTypeWorkObjectCluster to const + validSignalTypes + AllSignalTypes()
2. Add BaseConfidenceWorkObjectCluster = 0.15 to boundary_scoring.go
3. Implement detectWorkObjectClusters on AlgorithmicDetector
4. Replace nil guard with fallback call

### REFACTOR Phase
- Reuse existing helpers (no reimplementation)
- Sort output for determinism
- Run full quality gates

## Steps

1. Add SignalTypeWorkObjectCluster to boundary_signal.go (const + validSignalTypes map + AllSignalTypes slice — all 3 required)
2. Add BaseConfidenceWorkObjectCluster = 0.15 to boundary_scoring.go
3. Implement detectWorkObjectClusters in algorithmic_detector.go
4. Replace nil guard at :64-66 with fallback call
5. Write 5 new tests
6. Update affected existing tests (see Test Impact below)
7. Run quality gates

## Test Impact Analysis (3 tests affected)

| Test | Why allSignals=0 | Action Needed |
|------|-------------------|---------------|
| SingleContext_NoSplit (line 433) | Same actor, same verb, same object | MUST UPDATE: assert.Empty -> assert 1 sketch with WorkObjectCluster signal |
| SameVerbNoSignal (line 141) | Same verb, same actor, no actor-to-actor flow | DOCUMENT: passes by accident (checks signal types only), behavior now returns sketch |
| NotificationVerbDiscounted (line 240) | Notification discount eliminates all signals | DOCUMENT: passes by accident, behavior changes |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] DetectBoundaries never returns nil, nil for valid 2+ story input
- [ ] Fallback fires iff all primary heuristics return 0 signals
- [ ] Stories with overlapping WOs merge into same cluster sketch
- [ ] Stories with no WO overlap produce separate sketches
- [ ] All fallback sketches carry SignalTypeWorkObjectCluster signal
- [ ] Fallback confidence never reaches ConfidenceLevelHigh
- [ ] Primary heuristics producing signals suppresses fallback
- [ ] SignalTypeWorkObjectCluster registered in validSignalTypes AND AllSignalTypes()
- [ ] All 5 new tests + all existing tests pass
- [ ] golangci-lint run ./... reports 0 issues

## Edge Cases

| Case | Input | Expected Output |
|------|-------|-----------------|
| All stories share identical WOs | 3 stories all with ["note"] | 1 cluster sketch with all 3 stories |
| Each story unique WOs | 3 stories no WO overlap | 3 separate sketches |
| Mixed overlap | 2 share WO, 1 unique | 2 sketches |
| Primary heuristics fire | SameObjectDiffContext returns 1+ signal | Fallback NOT called |

## Quality Gates

```bash
go build ./...
go vet ./...
golangci-lint run ./...
go test ./... -race
```

## Risks / Dependencies

- Deliberate behavior change: SingleContext_NoSplit test must be updated
- Add "WorkObjectCluster" to docs/DDD.md glossary during implementation
- No composition root changes needed (AlgorithmicDetector constructor unchanged)
close_reason: AlgorithmicDetector work-object clustering fallback + README project name. 5+8 new tests, 1 existing test updated. All 4 quality gates pass.

title: bug: .alto/stories/ directory not auto-created by alto guide
description:
## Reproduction
```
mkdir /tmp/test && cd /tmp/test && git init
alto init -y --no-commit
alto guide --no-tui  # with stdin script
```

## Expected
alto guide creates .alto/stories/ if it doesn't exist, then writes story YAML files there.

## Actual
Write fails because .alto/stories/ doesn't exist. Directory must be created manually with mkdir -p.

## Root Cause
Either alto init should create .alto/stories/ as part of project scaffolding, or the story file writer in the guide flow should call os.MkdirAll before writing.

## Fix Direction
Add os.MkdirAll to the story writer (infrastructure layer) before writing files. This is the safer fix since it doesn't depend on init having run.

description:

### Explicitly Excluded

## Design

### guide.go Short/Long Replacement (TL fix — specific text)

Short: "Run the Domain Storytelling guided discovery flow"

Long:
```
Run the Domain Storytelling guided discovery flow.

alto acts as a domain consultant, moderating a structured conversation:
  1. Detection of installed AI coding tools
  2. Domain Storytelling moderator conversation (actors, activities, work objects
     structured into stories through opening → narration → deepening → closing)
  3. Boundary detection on accumulated stories (bounded context sketches)

Flags:
  --no-tui     Disable TUI prompts, use plain stdin/stdout (accessibility, CI)
  --continue   Resume a previously interrupted storytelling session
  --agent      Output discovery session as JSONL for AI agent consumption
  --ingest     Ingest answers from JSONL file (or "-" for stdin); requires --agent

```

### CLI Reference Flag Table

### new-project.md Replacement Section

Replace "The 10 questions" with "Domain Storytelling moderator conversation" covering:
1. StorytellingFlow selected by DiscoveryMode (ModeRapid: 3 stories, ModeThorough: 5+)
2. NarrationPhase progression: opening → narration → deepening → closing
3. StorySentence structure: [Actor] [activity] [WorkObject]

title: Auto-ripple review on ticket close (alto after-close protocol)
description:
## Goal / Problem

When a ticket is closed (via bd close), the after-close protocol (ripple review, flagging dependents, compatibility check, template compliance) must run automatically. Currently it depends on the closing agent/human remembering to run bin/bd-ripple manually. When team agents close tickets in separate sessions, the ripple review is missed.

This is a dogfooding issue: we hit this problem during Phase 3 development. Team agents closed P3-0, P3-1, P3-2 in their tmux sessions, but ripple review only ran when we manually triggered it in the main session.

## Background / Context

- PRD Scenario 6: Ticket Freshness & Ripple Review
- PRD Phase 7 roadmap: alto ticket-health, doc-health, drift detection, ripple review
- PRD risk table: "Ticket context decay (AI implements stale specs) — High/High — Ripple review flags dependents on close"

## Current Workaround (dogfooding, project-local)

Two scripts in bin/:
1. **bin/bd-close-hook** — Claude Code PostToolUse hook. Detects bd close in Bash commands, auto-runs bd-ripple. Fast-exit pattern: string-matches CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT for "bd close" before parsing JSON (skips 99%+ of Bash commands instantly).
2. **bin/bd-ripple** — Traverses dependency graph, flags dependents/siblings with review_needed, adds context comment, and now checks template compliance (required sections: Goal, Acceptance Criteria, Design, TDD Workflow).

Wired in .claude/settings.local.json:
\`\`\`json
"hooks": {
  "PostToolUse": [{"matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "bin/bd-close-hook"}]}]
}
\`\`\`

### Limitations of workaround:
1. **Claude Code only** — doesn't fire for manual terminal bd close, MCP calls, or non-Claude agents
2. **Project-local** — users must set up the hook themselves in each project
3. **PostToolUse on all Bash** — the matcher can't filter to "bd close" commands only; relies on fast-exit in the hook script
4. **Template check is grep-based** — checks section headers exist but doesn't validate content quality

## What Users Need (product solution)

When a user runs alto in their project and closes a ticket, alto should automatically:
1. Traverse the dependency graph (dependents + siblings)
2. Flag open tickets with review_needed
3. Add a context diff comment explaining what changed
4. Check template compliance on flagged tickets (required sections per beads template)
5. Optionally run claim verification (alto ticket-verify)

This should work regardless of which session/tool closes the ticket — CLI, MCP, agent team, or human.

## Design Options

1. **alto post-close hook** — alto generates a beads post-close hook during alto init. When bd close fires, the hook runs alto's ripple logic. This is the cleanest: works in any session, no Claude Code dependency.
2. **alto close wrapper** — alto provides its own close command (alto ticket-close) that wraps bd close + ripple + template check. Downside: users must remember to use alto's command.
3. **Event-driven** — alto subscribes to beads close events via Watermill and reacts. Most architecturally pure but requires beads to emit events.

Recommendation: Option 1 (post-close hook). alto init scaffolds the hook, users get it for free.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Ripple review runs automatically on every ticket close, regardless of session
- [ ] No manual bin/bd-ripple step needed
- [ ] Works for team agents in separate tmux sessions
- [ ] Works for MCP tool calls
- [ ] Flagged tickets get review_needed label + context comment
- [ ] Template compliance checked on flagged tickets (Goal, AC, Design, TDD required)
- [ ] Non-empty context required (close reason or provided summary)
- [ ] Template gaps reported with specific missing sections
- [ ] alto init scaffolds the hook (user doesn't configure manually)
notes:
## Grooming refresh — 2026-06-01 (pre-claim updates)

### Stale-path scrub
Three occurrences of `bin/bd-ripple` in the original description should now read `alto-scaffold/scripts/bd-ripple` — file moved in commit 56fdd29 (Wave-3 close). Apply during impl description rewrite or treat the original text as referring to the new location.

### Live workaround is BROKEN in this repo
The PostToolUse hook described under "Current Workaround" no longer fires correctly. `bin/bd-close-hook:51` still hardcodes `RIPPLE="$PROJECT_ROOT/bin/bd-ripple"` but `bin/bd-ripple` was renamed/moved. `.claude/settings.local.json:65,89` also retains stale `Bash(bin/bd-ripple:*)` permission entries. Fast-follow defect ticket filed separately to fix in-repo NOW; i80 remains the long-term productization.

### Design decision — Path A selected
Of the 3 options in the original description, Path 1 wins, refined as:

**Path A — `alto ticket-ripple <id>` Go subcommand + `alto init`-scaffolded beads hook.**

Wiring:
- New command `cmd/alto/commands/ticket-ripple.go` (Cobra)
- Application handler in `internal/ticket/application/` with ports `BeadsClient` (graph traversal + label/comment mutation) and `RippleNotifier` (terminal/log output)
- Adapter `internal/ticket/infrastructure/cli_beads_client.go` wraps the beads CLI
- `alto init` writes `.beads/hooks/post-close` (executable script that calls `alto ticket-ripple "$@"`); Windows gets a `.bat` shim from the same scaffold step

Rejected: Path B (ship bash verbatim via scaffold + symlink) — bash brittleness, Windows hassle, harder to unit-test the ripple logic.
Rejected: Path C (Watermill event subscribe) — requires beads to emit events; deferred per scope.

### Suggested ticket split (not yet applied — TL decision at wave kickoff)
Path A naturally decomposes:
- i80-a: `alto ticket-ripple <id>` subcommand + handler + ports + beads adapter (`internal/ticket/...` + `cmd/alto/commands/ticket-ripple.go`). Standalone — invocable manually.
- i80-b: `alto init` hook-scaffolding step that wires `.beads/hooks/post-close -> alto ticket-ripple`. Depends on i80-a.

Single-ticket alternative: dev lands a+b in one PR. Either choice is acceptable.

### Bounded context
Lives in existing `internal/ticket/` (already has domain/application/infrastructure layers — see internal/ticket/...). No new context required.

### Wave-coupling note
Wave 5 pairs i80 with yl0. Both insert into internal/composition/app.go (yl0 at the stackProfile fallback block ~line 133-137; i80-a likely registers a new `ripple` handler in `NewApp`). Merge order: yl0 first (smaller insertion), i80-a rebases against it. TL coordinates per launch-team Step 3 (shared-file detection).

title: Ticket design verification in alto guide pipeline
description:
## Goal / Problem

When alto generates tickets for users (Phase 6 of the guide pipeline), those tickets need the same architecture verification we do manually: trace constructor chains, verify port signatures against actual code, check DDD layer compliance, and validate that every dependency is named (no "TBD"). Without this, generated tickets contain "magic happens here" gaps that waste implementation time.

## Background / Context

**Dogfooding discovery:** During Phase 2 ticket creation for the Domain Storytelling epic, we found that tickets created from rough bullet points consistently had issues:
- Missing shared fields on VOs (ContextRelationship lacked shared[])
- Method signatures that didn't match actual code
- File:line references that were stale or wrong
- Unclear which layer owns which responsibility

We solved this with a two-agent chain: code-architect designs the ticket (reads code, traces callers), tech-lead reviews against DDD/ARCHITECTURE docs. This is codified in .claude/commands/design-ticket.md.

**Product opportunity:** alto already has ImplementabilityValidator (Ticket Freshness context) and CodebasePortScanner concepts in DDD.md. This ticket connects those to the actual ticket generation pipeline so users get verified tickets out of the box.

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|---|---|
| Bounded Context | Ticket Pipeline + Ticket Freshness |
| Ubiquitous Language | ImplementabilityValidator, DesignTraceResult, CodebasePortScanner, PortDefinition, FindingSeverity |
| Layer | Application (validation handler) + Infrastructure (AST scanner) |

## What alto should verify for each generated ticket

1. **Section completeness** — Goal, Design, AC, TDD, Steps all present
2. **Unspecified dependencies** — No "performs web search" without naming the port/adapter
3. **Port signature verification** — Scan actual Go interfaces, compare against ticket's claimed signatures
4. **Constructor chain tracing** — NewHandler(port) → port interface → adapter → composition root wiring
5. **DDD layer compliance** — Domain types don't import infrastructure, application depends only on domain + ports
6. **Ubiquitous language check** — Type names match the project's DDD.md glossary

## Relationship to existing concepts

- ImplementabilityValidator (DDD.md:256) → checks 1, 2
- CodebasePortScanner (DDD.md:257) → check 3
- DesignTraceResult (DDD.md:254) → structured output of all checks
- NEW: ConstructorChainTracer → check 4
- NEW: LayerComplianceChecker → check 5
- NEW: GlossaryMatcher → check 6

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Generated tickets pass the same verification that /design-ticket command applies
- [ ] Findings are reported as DesignTraceResult with severity levels
- [ ] CRITICAL findings block ticket creation (user must resolve first)
- [ ] MAJOR findings are warnings (ticket created with caveats)
- [ ] Port signatures are verified against actual Go AST, not just string matching

## Risks / Dependencies

- Depends on: Ticket Pipeline context implementation (not yet started)
- Depends on: alto guide pipeline completing (Phase 6)
- This is a quality gate on ticket generation, not a blocker for Phase 2 development

title: Auto-commit init output on created branch
description:
## Goal / Problem

alty init creates files on the alty/init branch but leaves them untracked. Any subsequent command checking for a clean tree fails. Auto-commit the generated scaffold.

## Background / Context

- Issue 7 from .notes/issues.md
- P4 (GitOps shared port) is DONE — GitOps interface at shared/application/ports.go:40-59 with HasGit, IsClean, CreateBranch, etc.
- GitOpsAdapter at rescue/infrastructure/git_ops_adapter.go implements all git operations via exec.CommandContext
- BootstrapHandler.Execute() writes files at bootstrap_handler.go:165-177 then publishes events — commit goes AFTER file writing
- BLOCKER: GitOps interface has NO Add or Commit methods — only branch/checkout ops. Must extend.
- BootstrapHandler has NO GitOps dependency — must add it

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Bootstrap (application + infrastructure) |
| Ubiquitous Language | ScaffoldCommit, GitCommitter |
| Layer | Application (handler) + Infrastructure (git adapter) |

## Design

### ISP Decision

Per CLAUDE.md: "Bootstrap should define its own narrow GitCommitter interface when implementing 77p.4 (ISP, define where consumed)."

Do NOT reuse the full GitOps interface. Define a focused port:

```
// In bootstrap/application/ports.go
type GitCommitter interface {
    HasGit(ctx context.Context, projectDir string) (bool, error)
    StageFiles(ctx context.Context, projectDir string, paths []string) error
    Commit(ctx context.Context, projectDir string, message string) error
}
```

### Adapter

New file: bootstrap/infrastructure/git_committer_adapter.go
- Implements GitCommitter using exec.CommandContext
- HasGit: git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree

In Execute(), after file writing (line 177):

2. If !gitCommitter.HasGit(ctx, projectDir) -> skip with log
3. Collect written file paths from FileActions
4. gitCommitter.StageFiles(ctx, projectDir, writtenPaths)

### CLI Changes

Add --no-commit flag to init command. If set, don't wire GitCommitter — handler skips commit when nil.

### File Ownership

- bootstrap/application/bootstrap_handler.go — Add optional GitCommitter + commit logic in Execute
- bootstrap/infrastructure/git_committer_adapter.go — NEW implements GitCommitter

4. Wire commit logic after file writing in Execute()
5. Add --no-commit flag to init.go

### REFACTOR Phase

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Enforcement |
|-----------|-------------|
| S | GitCommitter has one job: stage + commit files |
| O | Optional via functional option — no modification when absent |
| I | Narrow 3-method interface vs full 6-method GitOps (ISP) |

title: Fix .alty/knowledge and .alty/maintenance created as files instead of directories
description:
## Goal / Problem

`alty rescue` (via `ExecutePlan`) creates `.alty/knowledge` and `.alty/maintenance` as regular files with stub content instead of directories. This breaks the knowledge base and doc maintenance features which expect these paths to be directories.

## Background / Context

- Gap analysis correctly identifies directory gaps with trailing `/` paths: `.alty/knowledge/` and `.alty/maintenance/` (`rescue_handler.go:296,318`)
- However, `ExecutePlan` (`rescue_handler.go:159-173`) iterates ALL non-conflict gaps and calls `fileWriter.WriteFile()` indiscriminately
- `filepath.Join` strips the trailing `/`, so `filepath.Join("/proj", ".alty/knowledge/")` becomes `/proj/.alty/knowledge`
- `FilesystemFileWriter.WriteFile()` then creates a **file** at that path
- **Pattern reference:** The `FilesystemFileWriter` (`shared/infrastructure/persistence/filesystem_file_writer.go:29-38`) already calls `os.MkdirAll` for parent directories -- the missing piece is distinguishing "this gap IS a directory" from "this gap is a file"

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | **Rescue** (`internal/rescue/`) |
| Ubiquitous Language | `Gap` (VO), `GapType`, `MigrationPlan`, `GapAnalysis` (aggregate root), `ExecutePlan` (command) |
| Layer | Domain (add `IsDirectory()` to `Gap` VO) + Application (`ExecutePlan` branching logic) |

## Design

### Data Models

| Model | Type | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| `Gap` | Value Object | Represents a structural gap; gains `IsDirectory() bool` method |
| `FileWriter` | Port (interface) | Existing shared port -- unchanged |
| `DirCreator` | Port (interface) | New shared port: `EnsureDir(ctx, path) error` |
| `FilesystemDirCreator` | Adapter | New adapter implementing `DirCreator` via `os.MkdirAll` |

### Sequence / Flow

```
ExecutePlan          Gap              DirCreator       FileWriter
    |                 |                    |                |
    |-- IsDirectory()->|                    |                |
    |<-- true ---------|                    |                |
    |-- EnsureDir(path) ------------------>|                |
    |<-- ok --------------------------------|                |
    |                                                       |
    |-- IsDirectory()->|                    |                |
    |<-- false ---------|                    |                |
    |-- WriteFile(path, content) -------------------------->|
    |<-- ok -------------------------------------------------|
```

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| **S**ingle Responsibility | `Gap.IsDirectory()` -- the VO knows its own semantics; `RescueHandler` dispatches |
| **O**pen/Closed | New `DirCreator` port extends capability without modifying `FileWriter` |
| **L**iskov Substitution | Any `DirCreator` adapter (filesystem, in-memory) honors the contract |
| **I**nterface Segregation | `DirCreator` is separate from `FileWriter` |
| **D**ependency Inversion | `RescueHandler` depends on `DirCreator` port, not `os.MkdirAll` directly |

## TDD Workflow

### RED Phase

```go
// internal/rescue/domain/gap_analysis_test.go
TestGap_WhenPathHasTrailingSlash_ExpectIsDirectoryTrue
TestGap_WhenPathHasNoTrailingSlash_ExpectIsDirectoryFalse
TestGap_WhenPathIsRootSlash_ExpectIsDirectoryTrue

// internal/rescue/application/rescue_handler_test.go
TestRescueHandler_ExecutePlan_WhenGapIsDirectory_ExpectDirCreatedNotFile
TestRescueHandler_ExecutePlan_WhenGapIsFile_ExpectFileWritten
TestRescueHandler_ExecutePlan_WhenMixedGaps_ExpectBothDirsAndFiles

// internal/shared/infrastructure/persistence/filesystem_dir_creator_test.go
TestFilesystemDirCreator_EnsureDir_WhenPathNotExists_ExpectCreated
TestFilesystemDirCreator_EnsureDir_WhenPathAlreadyExists_ExpectIdempotent
TestFilesystemDirCreator_EnsureDir_WhenPathIsFile_ExpectError
```

### GREEN Phase

1. Add `IsDirectory() bool` to `Gap` VO (`internal/rescue/domain/gap_analysis.go`)
2. Add `DirCreator` port to `internal/shared/application/ports.go`
3. Create `FilesystemDirCreator` adapter in `internal/shared/infrastructure/persistence/`
4. Add `dirCreator` field to `RescueHandler`; update `NewRescueHandler` constructor
5. Branch on `gap.IsDirectory()` in `ExecutePlan` loop (`rescue_handler.go:159-173`)
6. Update composition root to wire `DirCreator`

### REFACTOR Phase

- Ensure `Gap.IsDirectory()` is a pure function
- Verify UL: `Gap`, `IsDirectory`, `DirCreator`, `EnsureDir`
- `golangci-lint run ./...` reports 0 issues
- No domain layer imports from application/infrastructure

## Steps

1. RED: Add domain VO tests for `IsDirectory()` -> verify FAIL
2. GREEN: Add `IsDirectory()` to `Gap` VO -> verify PASS
3. RED: Add `DirCreator` port + adapter tests -> verify FAIL
4. GREEN: Create `FilesystemDirCreator` adapter -> verify PASS
5. RED: Add handler tests for directory gap branching -> verify FAIL
6. GREEN: Update `RescueHandler` with `DirCreator` dep + branching -> verify PASS
7. Wire composition root
8. REFACTOR: naming, dead code, full quality gates

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.alty/knowledge` created as a directory
- [ ] `.alty/maintenance` created as a directory
- [ ] File-type gaps still written as files with stub content
- [ ] `Gap.IsDirectory()` returns true for paths ending with `/`
- [ ] `DirCreator` port exists in shared application
- [ ] No existing tests broken
- [ ] All quality gates pass

## Edge Cases

| Case | Input | Expected Output |
|------|-------|-----------------|
| Trailing slash | `.alty/knowledge/` | `IsDirectory()=true`, `EnsureDir` called |
| No trailing slash | `docs/PRD.md` | `IsDirectory()=false`, `WriteFile` called |
| Dir already exists | `.alty/knowledge/` exists | `EnsureDir` idempotent |
| Path is a file | `.alty/knowledge` exists as file | `EnsureDir` returns error |
| Conflict gap | `GapTypeConflict` with trailing `/` | Skipped (existing logic line 160) |
| Root slash | `/` | `IsDirectory()=true` |

## Pre-Implementation Validation

- [ ] `Gap` VO has no `IsDirectory()` method yet
- [ ] `DirCreator` port does not exist yet
- [ ] `NewRescueHandler` takes 5 params -- adding `DirCreator` makes 6
- [ ] Existing tests call `NewRescueHandler` with 5 args -- all must be updated
- [ ] `FilesystemFileWriter.WriteFile` creates parent dirs but writes a file -- NOT suitable for directory creation

## QA Before Close

- [ ] Happy path: mixed file and directory gaps create correct types
- [ ] All 6 edge cases have test coverage
- [ ] Error handling: `EnsureDir` failure reports clearly
- [ ] No regressions in existing rescue tests
- [ ] Domain layer has no external dependencies

## Risks / Dependencies

- **Constructor signature change**: `NewRescueHandler` gains 6th parameter. All call sites must be updated.
- **No formal blocking dependencies** -- standalone bug fix within Rescue context.
close_reason: Closed

title: Website review and polish
description:
## Goal / Problem

Final quality gate before launch. Layer 3 handled the polish pass (responsive, micro-interactions, edge cases). This ticket runs the remaining Impeccable skills (`/audit`, `/clarify`) and fixes the SEO gaps found in the build output review.

## What Layer 3 Already Did

- `/adapt`, `/delight`, `/harden`, `/polish`, `/critique` — all run on landing page
- Content fixes: `ApproveInvoice()`, `--force-branch` removed, `site` config added
- Responsive breakpoints (360px, 480px, 640px, 768px)
- `prefers-reduced-motion` on all animations
- Touch targets, keyboard :active states, overflow handling

## What This Ticket Covers

### 1. SEO Gaps (dev fix)

Landing page (`index.astro`) is missing OG tags that Starlight auto-generates for docs pages:
```html
<meta property="og:title" content="alty — Ship with structure, not chaos" />
<meta property="og:description" content="alty turns 4-5 sentences into..." />
<meta property="og:url" content="https://alty.ai/" />
<meta property="og:type" content="website" />
<meta property="og:site_name" content="alty" />
<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image" />
<link rel="canonical" href="https://alty.ai/" />
```

Also missing: `og:image` for social previews (needs a preview image asset).

### 2. Impeccable `/audit` (not yet run)

Run `/audit` on the full site — landing page + docs pages. This skill checks:
- Accessibility: contrast ratios, ARIA, keyboard nav, semantic HTML
- Performance: animation costs, lazy loading, bundle size
- Theming: dark/light mode consistency
- Responsive: viewport coverage

### 3. Impeccable `/clarify` (not yet run)

Run `/clarify` on UX copy — landing page text, nav labels, CTA buttons, footer links. Check:
- Is "Read the Docs" the right label? (links to concepts, not docs index)
- Are the feature descriptions clear to someone who doesn't know DDD?
- Is the terminal demo self-explanatory?

### 4. Hosting Decision

Decide and document hosting. Options:
- **Cloudflare Pages** — free, fast, auto-deploys, zero config for static
- **Netlify** — free tier, preview deploys, forms
- **Vercel** — free tier, edge functions (overkill for static)

Recommendation: Cloudflare Pages. Add deployment notes to `website/README.md`.

## Steps

1. Add OG meta tags to `index.astro` `<head>`
2. Add canonical URL to `index.astro`
3. Run `/audit` on full site — fix P0/P1 issues
4. Run `/clarify` on UX copy — improve where needed
5. Run `/quieter` only if audit/clarify surface aggressive elements
6. Add hosting deployment instructions to `website/README.md`
7. Final build: `cd website && npm run build`
8. Verify sitemap includes all pages
9. Verify OG tags render in build output

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Landing page has OG meta tags (og:title, og:description, og:url, og:type)
- [ ] Landing page has canonical URL
- [ ] `/audit` run — all P0/P1 issues fixed
- [ ] `/clarify` run — UX copy reviewed
- [ ] Hosting decision documented in `website/README.md`
- [ ] `npm run build` succeeds, sitemap includes all pages
- [ ] Build output < 1MB (currently 572K — should stay small)
close_reason: Final review complete — SEO meta tags added, /audit clean (2 rounds), /clarify clean (5 copy fixes), Cloudflare Pages hosting documented, build verified (9 pages, 572K)

## Research Question

- The alty.ai brand has a neon glow aesthetic (existing landing page — need to locate reference)

- Pencil.dev exports PNG/JPEG/WEBP/PDF — **no SVG export**
- **Logo refinement is descoped** from this ticket. Pencil.dev is a layout/mockup tool, not a vector illustration tool. Logo concepts can be generated via G() for later refinement in Figma/Inkscape.

5. **Generate logo concepts** — Use G() with AI image generation for neon glow logo concepts (reference material only, not final logo)

7. **Document workflow** — Write up the Pencil.dev → Astro translation approach

- [ ] Pencil.dev usage notes documented (workflow, key operations, gotchas)

- [ ] Documentation page mockup in .pen file (sidebar, content, code blocks)

- [ ] Mockups visually validated via get_screenshot
- [ ] Mockups exported as PNG files
- [ ] Pencil.dev workflow documented for team reuse
- [ ] Design specs (spacing, colors, layout) extracted and written down
- [ ] Timebox respected (or extended with justification)
- [ ] NO logo SVG deliverable (descoped — Pencil.dev doesn't export SVG)
notes:

description:

   - Footer

4. **`/extract`** — Extract reusable design tokens and component patterns into a systematic design system. Consolidate colors, spacing, typography into CSS custom properties and daisyUI theme config.

5. **`/normalize`** — Ensure consistency across all components. Match design system tokens, verify spacing/typography are uniform.

   - Navigation header
   - Footer

title: Spike: Website design research — Tailwind + daisyUI for high-quality product sites
description:
## Research Question

How to build a high-quality product website (not just docs) with Tailwind + daisyUI in Astro + Starlight? The site must look like Linear, Vercel, or Supabase — not a standard documentation template.

Specific questions:
1. What daisyUI components map to product website patterns (hero, feature grid, pricing, testimonials)?
2. Does daisyUI v5 conflict with Starlight's built-in CSS and theme switching? What overrides are needed?
3. How does daisyUI v5 + Tailwind v4 configure in Astro? (CSS-based, NOT tailwind.config.js)
4. What Tailwind plugins enhance typography and layout for marketing pages?
5. What color schemes, spacing scales, and typography pairings work for a developer-focused product with a neon glow aesthetic?
6. Are there Astro + Tailwind + daisyUI starter templates we can reference?
7. How do other Go CLI tools (Charm, Cobra, Buf) present their websites?

## Timebox

**Timebox:** 3 hours

## Background / Context

- Site uses Astro + Starlight (decided in spike alty-cli-dkc)
- Starlight has its own CSS variables, theme switcher, and component system
- daisyUI v5 is CSS-based configuration (NOT tailwind.config.js like v4) — this is a major change
- Known issue: Starlight's theme switcher and daisyUI `data-theme` attribute conflict. Reference: https://tricked.dev/blog/daisyui-starlight/
- The alty.ai brand has a neon glow aesthetic (existing landing page)

## Investigation Approach

title: Fix extractClassifications Q10 keyword matching ambiguity
description:
## Summary

When Q10 contains multiple contexts with different classifications (e.g., 'Sales is core competitive advantage, Inventory is supporting'), the `extractClassifications` function can misclassify contexts because it uses global keyword matching across the entire string.

## Problem

At `internal/discovery/application/artifact_generation_handler.go:296-317`, the matching logic:
```go
if strings.Contains(q10, keyword) && strings.Contains(q10, ctxLower) {
```
checks the ENTIRE Q10 string for both keyword and context name independently. With input `"Sales is core, Inventory is supporting"`:
- For "Sales": `Contains(q10, "supporting")=true` AND `Contains(q10, "sales")=true` → Sales gets Supporting (WRONG)
- Map iteration is random (`classificationKeywords` is a map), so results are nondeterministic

Existing tests work around this — L605-606: `// Use single-context events to avoid Q10 keyword matching ambiguity`

## Root Cause

Global substring matching on the full Q10 answer. Keywords like "supporting" and "core" apply to the entire string instead of being scoped to the segment mentioning a specific context.

## Fix

Split Q10 into segments (by comma, period, semicolon), then for each bounded context, find the segment that mentions it, and check only THAT segment for classification keywords.

```go
// Split Q10 into segments
segments := splitIntoSegments(q10) // split by , . ;

for _, ctx := range model.BoundedContexts() {
    ctxLower := strings.ToLower(ctx.Name())
    for _, seg := range segments {
        if !strings.Contains(seg, ctxLower) {
            continue
        }
        // Only check keywords in the segment mentioning this context
        for keyword, cls := range classificationKeywords {
            if strings.Contains(seg, keyword) {
                model.ClassifySubdomain(ctx.Name(), cls, ...)
                break
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Discovery |
| Ubiquitous Language | SubdomainClassification, BoundedContext, DomainModel |
| Layer | Application (artifact_generation_handler.go) |

## Design

### Data Models

No new types. Fix is internal to `extractClassifications` function.

### Sequence / Flow

```
Q10 string          splitIntoSegments       per-segment matching
    |                      |                        |
    |-- split by , . ; --->|                        |
    |                      |-- for each ctx -------->|
    |                      |   find segment with ctx |
    |                      |   check keywords in seg |
    |                      |<-- classification ------|
```

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| **S**ingle Responsibility | `extractClassifications` does one thing: parse Q10 → classify contexts |
| **O**pen/Closed | `classificationKeywords` map is extensible without modifying logic |

## TDD Workflow

### RED Phase

```
internal/discovery/application/artifact_generation_handler_test.go
test_multi_context_q10_core_and_supporting: "Sales is core, Inventory is supporting" → Sales=Core, Inventory=Supporting
test_multi_context_q10_three_contexts: "Sales core, Inventory supporting, Notifications generic" → all correct
test_single_context_q10_still_works: "Sales is core competitive advantage" → Sales=Core (no regression)
test_q10_with_periods: "Sales is core. Inventory is supporting." → both correct
test_q10_with_semicolons: "Sales is core; Inventory is supporting" → both correct
```

### GREEN Phase

1. Add `splitIntoSegments` helper (split by comma, period, semicolon)
2. Rewrite `extractClassifications` to scope keyword matching per segment
3. Remove workaround comments from existing tests (L605-606, L869)
4. Add multi-context Q10 test cases

### REFACTOR Phase

- Update existing single-context test workarounds to use multi-context Q10
- Verify `makeEvent()` default Q10 at L96 (`"Sales is core competitive advantage, Inventory is supporting necessary"`) now produces correct results

## Steps

1. Write failing test: multi-context Q10 with different classifications per context
2. Add `splitIntoSegments` helper function
3. Rewrite `extractClassifications` loop to match keywords per segment only
4. Verify existing tests pass (no regression)
5. Remove workaround comments and update tests to use multi-context Q10 where appropriate
6. Run quality gates

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `"Sales is core, Inventory is supporting"` → Sales=Core, Inventory=Supporting
- [ ] `"Sales is core. Inventory is supporting."` → both correct (period delimiter)
- [ ] `"Sales core; Inventory supporting; Notifications generic"` → all three correct
- [ ] Single-context Q10 still works (no regression)
- [ ] Empty Q10 still returns nil (no regression)
- [ ] Default `makeEvent()` Q10 at test L96 produces correct classifications
- [ ] Workaround comments removed from tests

## Edge Cases

| Case | Input | Expected Output |
|------|-------|-----------------|
| Single context | "Sales is core" | Sales=Core |
| Two contexts, same keyword | "Sales is core, Inventory is core" | Both=Core |
| Context name contains keyword | "Supporting Services is core" | Supporting Services=Core (context name match takes priority) |
| No matching keyword | "Sales is important" | Sales unclassified |
| Context not mentioned | "something generic" | Context unclassified |
| Mixed delimiters | "Sales core, Inventory supporting. Billing generic" | All correct |

## Quality Gates

```bash
go build ./...
go vet ./...
golangci-lint run ./...
go test ./... -race
```

- [ ] Lint passes
- [ ] All tests pass with >= 80% coverage
- [ ] Edge cases have test coverage

## Pre-Implementation Validation

- [x] `extractClassifications` at artifact_generation_handler.go:296-317 — confirmed, bug is at L308
- [x] `classificationKeywords` map at L20-31 — confirmed, 9 keywords across 3 classifications
- [x] `SplitAnswer` at L155 splits by comma — can reuse or adapt for segments
- [x] `model.ClassifySubdomain` at L309 — confirmed, takes (name, classification, rationale)
- [x] Default test event at L96 uses multi-context Q10 — confirms bug exists in test data
- [x] Existing tests avoid multi-context by using single-context Q10 (L605-606 comments)

## Risks / Dependencies

- `classificationKeywords` map iteration order is nondeterministic — segment-scoped matching eliminates this as a concern since only one keyword should match per segment
- Context names with spaces (e.g., "Order Processing") — existing code already lowercases both sides, segment matching preserves this
- No external dependencies

title: Create bounded_context_map.yaml schema and parser
description:
## Summary

Define YAML schema for bounded context map and implement parser. This includes creating the necessary domain types.

## DDD Alignment

- Bounded Context: Architecture Testing (fitness)
- New domain types: internal/fitness/domain/bounded_context_map.go
- Parser: internal/fitness/infrastructure/bounded_context_map_parser.go

## Design

### Domain Types (NEW)

```go
// RelationshipDirection indicates upstream/downstream flow
type RelationshipDirection string
const (
    RelationshipUpstream   RelationshipDirection = "upstream"
    RelationshipDownstream RelationshipDirection = "downstream"
)

// RelationshipPattern indicates integration pattern
type RelationshipPattern string
const (
    PatternDomainEvent   RelationshipPattern = "domain_event"
    PatternSharedKernel  RelationshipPattern = "shared_kernel"
    PatternACL           RelationshipPattern = "acl"
    PatternOpenHost      RelationshipPattern = "open_host"
)

// ContextRelationship describes a relationship to another context
type ContextRelationship struct {
    target    string
    direction RelationshipDirection
    pattern   RelationshipPattern
}

// BoundedContextEntry is one context in the map
type BoundedContextEntry struct {
    name           string
    modulePath     string
    classification vo.SubdomainClassification
    layers         []string
    relationships  []ContextRelationship
}

// BoundedContextMap is a collection of contexts with relationships (VALUE OBJECT)
type BoundedContextMap struct {
    projectName string
    rootPackage string
    contexts    []BoundedContextEntry
```

title: Implement TestRunnerAdapter for go/npm/pytest
description:
## Goal / Problem

Implement the TestRunner port using subprocess calls to detect and run tests for Go, npm, and pytest projects.

## Background / Context

- Depends on: TestRunner port definition
- Detection strategy: check for go.mod, package.json, pytest.ini/setup.py
- Run strategy: subprocess with timeout

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Rescue |
| Layer | Infrastructure (adapter) |

## Design

```go
type TestRunnerAdapter struct{}

func (t *TestRunnerAdapter) Detect(ctx context.Context, projectDir string) (string, error) {
    // Check go.mod -> "go"
    // Check package.json with "test" script -> "npm"
    // Check pytest.ini or conftest.py -> "pytest"
    // Return "" if none found
}

func (t *TestRunnerAdapter) Run(ctx context.Context, projectDir, framework string) error {
    var cmd *exec.Cmd
    switch framework {
    case "go":
        cmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "go", "test", "./...")
    case "npm":
        cmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "npm", "test")
    case "pytest":
        cmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "pytest")
    }
    cmd.Dir = projectDir
    output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
    if err \!= nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("tests failed: %s", output)
    }
    return nil
}
```

## Steps

1. Create `internal/rescue/infrastructure/test_runner_adapter.go`
2. Implement Detect with file-based detection
3. Implement Run with subprocess execution
4. Add unit tests with mocked file system
5. Add integration test with real go test

title: Implement GlobalSettingsScanner for tool conflicts
description:
## Goal / Problem

PRD 5.2.1 requires detecting global configs (~/.claude/, ~/.cursor/) that override local project settings. Users must be warned about conflicts before generating local configs.

## Background / Context

- PRD Section 5.2.1: Global Settings Detection - global configs "always win" over local
- `FilesystemToolScanner` already has `toolDirs` map at [internal/discovery/infrastructure/filesystem_tool_scanner.go:13](internal/discovery/infrastructure/filesystem_tool_scanner.go#L13)
- `ScanConflicts` at line 62 is a stub - only checks cursor existence
- **Pattern reference:** Extend existing scanner rather than create new one

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Discovery |
| Ubiquitous Language | GlobalConfig, SettingsConflict, ConflictSeverity |
| Layer | Domain (VOs) + Infrastructure (scanner enhancement) |

## Design

### Data Models

| Model | Type | Location | Purpose |
|-------|------|----------|---------|
| `GlobalConfig` | Value Object | `discovery/domain/` | toolName, path, content, exists |
| `SettingsConflict` | Value Object | `discovery/domain/` | globalPath, localPath, conflictType, severity |
| `ConflictSeverity` | Enum | `discovery/domain/` | Info, Warning, Error |

### Global Config Paths (from PRD 5.2.1)

| Tool | Global Path | Key Files |
|------|-------------|-----------|
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/` | `CLAUDE.md`, `settings.json` |
| Cursor | `~/.cursor/` | rules directory |
| Roo Code | `~/.roo/` | TBD (needs spike) |
| OpenCode | `~/.config/opencode/` | TBD (needs spike) |

### Enhanced ScanConflicts

```go
// Current stub (line 62-80):
func (s *FilesystemToolScanner) ScanConflicts(_ context.Context, _ string) ([]string, error) {
    // Only checks cursor existence
}

// Enhanced version:
func (s *FilesystemToolScanner) ScanConflicts(ctx context.Context, projectDir string) ([]SettingsConflict, error) {
    var conflicts []SettingsConflict
    
    for toolName, configRelPath := range toolDirs {
        globalPath := filepath.Join(s.homeDir, configRelPath)
        localPath := filepath.Join(projectDir, configRelPath)
        
        globalExists := fileExists(globalPath)
        localExists := fileExists(localPath)
        
        if globalExists && localExists {
            // Both exist - compare content
            conflict := compareConfigs(globalPath, localPath)
            if conflict != nil {
                conflicts = append(conflicts, *conflict)
            }
        } else if globalExists {
            // Global exists, local doesn't - info only
            conflicts = append(conflicts, SettingsConflict{
                Tool:     toolName,
                Global:   globalPath,
                Local:    localPath,
                Type:     "global_only",
                Severity: SeverityInfo,
                Message:  "Global config exists, will override any local config you create",
            })
        }
    }
    return conflicts, nil
}
```

### Sequence / Flow

```
DetectionHandler    FilesystemToolScanner    Filesystem
       |                    |                    |
       |-- Detect() ------->|                    |
       |                    |-- stat ~/.claude/->|
       |                    |<-- exists ---------|
       |<-- tools[] --------|                    |
       |                    |                    |
       |-- ScanConflicts(projectDir) ----------->|
       |                    |-- stat ~/.claude/->|
       |                    |<-- exists ---------|
       |                    |-- stat .claude/ -->|
       |                    |<-- exists ---------|
       |                    |-- read both ------>|
       |                    |<-- content --------|
       |                    |                    |
       |                    |-- compare -------->|
       |<-- []SettingsConflict ------------------|
```

### MCP Integration

Update `detect_tools` MCP handler to include conflicts in output:

```go
// internal/mcp/tools_bootstrap.go detectToolsHandler
conflicts, _ := app.DetectionHandler.ScanConflicts(projectDir)
if len(conflicts) > 0 {
    fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "\nGlobal Settings Conflicts:\n")
    for _, c := range conflicts {
        fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "- [%s] %s: %s\n", c.Severity, c.Tool, c.Message)
    }
}
```

## SOLID Mapping

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| **S**ingle Responsibility | Scanner detects, doesn't resolve conflicts |
| **O**pen/Closed | Enhance existing method, don't change signature drastically |
| **I**nterface Segregation | Keep Detect and ScanConflicts separate |

## TDD Workflow

### RED Phase

```go
// internal/discovery/infrastructure/filesystem_tool_scanner_test.go

func TestScanConflicts_GlobalOnly(t *testing.T) {
    // ~/.claude exists, .claude doesn't → Info severity
}

func TestScanConflicts_BothExist_SameContent(t *testing.T) {
    // Both exist, same content → no conflict
}

func TestScanConflicts_BothExist_DifferentContent(t *testing.T) {
    // Both exist, different → Warning with diff summary
}

func TestScanConflicts_NoGlobal(t *testing.T) {
    // No global config → empty conflicts
}

func TestScanConflicts_PermissionDenied(t *testing.T) {
    // Can't read global → skip with warning, not error
}
```

Run: `go test ./internal/discovery/infrastructure/... -run TestScanConflicts` → should FAIL

### GREEN Phase

1. Create `GlobalConfig` and `SettingsConflict` VOs in `discovery/domain/`
2. Update `FilesystemToolScanner.ScanConflicts` signature to return `[]SettingsConflict`
3. Implement content comparison logic
4. Update `DetectionHandler` to expose conflicts
5. Update MCP `detect_tools` handler

### REFACTOR Phase

- Factor out file reading/comparison to helpers
- Add content diffing for better conflict messages

## Steps

1. Create `internal/discovery/domain/global_config.go`:
   ```go
   type GlobalConfig struct { toolName, path, content string; exists bool }
   ```

2. Create `internal/discovery/domain/settings_conflict.go`:
   ```go
   type ConflictSeverity string
   const (SeverityInfo, SeverityWarning, SeverityError)
   type SettingsConflict struct { Tool, Global, Local, Type string; Severity; Message }
   ```

3. Update `FilesystemToolScanner.ScanConflicts`:
   - Change return type: `([]string, error)` → `([]SettingsConflict, error)`
   - Implement proper conflict detection

4. Update `DetectionHandler` to call and return conflicts

5. Update MCP `detect_tools` to display conflicts

6. Update composition adapter if return type changed

7. Run quality gates

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Detects ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md when present
- [ ] Detects ~/.cursor/ when present  
- [ ] Reports when global exists but local doesn't (Info)
- [ ] Reports when both exist with different content (Warning)
- [ ] `detect_tools` MCP output includes conflict warnings
- [ ] Works on Linux and macOS

## Edge Cases

| Case | Input | Expected Output |
|------|-------|-----------------|
| No global config | ~/.claude missing | No conflicts for claude-code |
| Global only | ~/.claude exists, no .claude | Info: "global will override" |
| Both same | Same CLAUDE.md content | No conflict |
| Both different | Different CLAUDE.md | Warning with summary |
| Permission denied | ~/.claude unreadable | Skip tool, log warning |
| Symlinked config | ~/.claude is symlink | Follow symlink, compare target |

## Quality Gates

```bash
golangci-lint run ./...
go test ./... -race
```

- [ ] Lint passes
- [ ] All tests pass with >= 80% coverage

## Pre-Implementation Validation

- [x] toolDirs map exists at line 13 with correct paths
- [x] os.UserHomeDir() used at line 33
- [x] ScanConflicts method exists (stub) at line 62
- [x] DetectionHandler exists at discovery/application/detection_handler.go
- [ ] Verify composition adapter handles return type change

## Risks / Dependencies

- Return type change may break existing callers (composition adapter at adapters.go:43)
- Content comparison may be slow for large files - consider size limits
- Cursor uses SQLite, not readable as text (existing conflict note)

description:
## Context

Running `alto doc-health --paths=alto-scaffold/` on the scaffold tree currently exits non-zero. The single violation is `NoInternalLeaksRule` firing on the literal token `alty-cli` (the beads ticket prefix used by this repo) inside `alto-scaffold/commands/launch-team.md`. The token is documentation, not a leak — it is the user-facing identifier of issues in the bundled issue tracker.

This is pre-existing on main and was surfaced during Wave 7b close-out of alty-cli-zc9 (TemplateRenderabilityRule). Independently verified twice by the wave's QA + WH reviewers via `git stash`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `alto doc-health --paths=alto-scaffold/` exits 0 on a clean working tree.
- The fix does NOT weaken `NoInternalLeaksRule` for actual internal-path tokens (home-dir paths, machine names, personal emails).
- A regression test asserts the rule still fires on a synthetic `<repo-root>` or home-dir-style token.

## Design options (decide during grooming)

1. Allowlist beads-prefix tokens in `NoInternalLeaksRule` (configurable via `ScaffoldParams`, defaulting to the project's `ticket_prefix`).
2. Move the prefix mention in `launch-team.md` to a `.project.md` overlay so the generic command body stays prefix-free.
3. Accept the gap; document the suppression mechanism in `launch-team.md` frontmatter.

Recommendation from the discovering wave: option 1 — `ticket_prefix` is already in `ScaffoldParams`, and the rule already accepts configuration via the composition root.

## Source citations

- `internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/no_internal_leaks_rule.go`
- `alto-scaffold/commands/launch-team.md` (offending token: the beads ticket prefix)
- `internal/dochealth/infrastructure/default_scaffold_rules.go:27` (rule wiring)

title: docs(scaffold): canonical Team-Mode Communication Protocol §P1-P7 + per-persona references
description:
## Goal

Land the canonical team-launch communication protocol as a single section in alto-scaffold/commands/launch-team.md, and have every persona under alto-scaffold/agents/ reference it instead of re-stating the rules in shorter or diverging form.

This is the FOUNDATION layer that alty-cli-561 sits on top of. 561 covers the Step-0 pre-launch hygiene + peer-canary replacement + orchestrator-as-router fallback. This ticket only covers the canonical §P1-P7 protocol body and the per-persona reference inserts.

## Background

During Wave 7b's launch attempt, the orchestrator detoured to detect transport behaviour (peer-canary). The detour surfaced that the protocol had no canonical home: each persona re-stated rough rules with subtle drift, and the orchestrator preamble had no shared spec to reference. The detour authored a canonical §Team-Mode Communication Protocol with §P1-P7 (Loading the transport, Addressing peers, One-shot semantics, Routing chart, Message format reference, What NOT to do, Failure handling) and inserted §Team-Mode Communication subsections into all six personas pointing back to the spec. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md gained a cosmetic ASCII-art alignment fix in the same pass.

## Files affected

- alto-scaffold/commands/launch-team.md (+270 lines: §Team-Mode Communication Protocol §P1-P7)
- alto-scaffold/agents/developer.md (+26 lines: §Team-Mode Communication subsection)
- alto-scaffold/agents/project-manager.md (+22 lines: §Team-Mode Communication subsection)
- alto-scaffold/agents/qa-engineer.md (+26 lines: §Team-Mode Communication subsection)
- alto-scaffold/agents/researcher.md (+26 lines: §Team-Mode Communication subsection)
- alto-scaffold/agents/tech-lead.md (+36 lines: §Team-Mode Communication subsection + tools frontmatter gains SendMessage, ToolSearch)
- alto-scaffold/agents/white-hacker.md (+27 lines: §Team-Mode Communication subsection)
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (4±4: ASCII-art alignment cosmetic)

## Acceptance Criteria

- launch-team.md has a single §Team-Mode Communication Protocol containing §P1 (Loading the transport), §P2 (Addressing peers), §P3 (One-shot exit semantics), §P4 (Routing chart), §P5 (Message format reference), §P6 (What NOT to do), §P7 (Failure handling).
- Each persona under alto-scaffold/agents/ contains a §Team-Mode Communication subsection that references the canonical spec by section, without re-stating the rules.
- tech-lead.md frontmatter `tools` list includes `SendMessage` and `ToolSearch`.
- Privacy: `grep -nE '/home/[a-z]+/|<your-username>' alto-scaffold/commands/launch-team.md` returns zero matches.
- arch-go and golangci-lint clean (this is doc-only — should be a no-op for both).

## Out of scope

- Step-0 pre-launch hygiene (TeamDelete + member shutdown_request) — owned by alty-cli-561.
- Peer-canary replacement of the single-agent canary — owned by alty-cli-561.
- Failure Mode 4 option (d) orchestrator-as-router fallback — owned by alty-cli-561.

## Status

Code is already on-disk in the working tree (uncommitted). This ticket exists for audit-trail; close on commit.
