All 6 personas reference the spec without re-stating. tech-lead.md frontmatter tools gained SendMessage + ToolSearch. arch-go + golangci-lint clean (doc-only no-op). Foundation in place for alty-cli-561 (Step 0 + peer-canary + orchestrator-as-router fallback).

title: docs(launch-team): TeamDelete pre-launch + peer-canary + orchestrator-as-router fallback
description:
`alto-scaffold/commands/launch-team.md` §Team-Mode Communication Protocol assumes peer-to-peer SendMessage is universally available and has no pre-launch team-state hygiene step. Three real-session observations show gaps:

1. **Background-spawned agents do not always expose SendMessage.** Some harnesses return `"SendMessage tool not found in deferred tool list"` from a background subagent's `ToolSearch({query: "select:SendMessage"})`, even though foreground spawns load it normally. Receivers can still be resumed by SendMessage regardless of their own ToolSearch result — only the send side is missing.

2. **The current single-agent canary cannot distinguish parent-addressing failure from real transport failure.** The orchestrator is not in the addressable peer set; the canary trying to deliver `canary-ok` to recipient `"orchestrator"` fails with `"no agent named orchestrator is currently addressable"` even when peer-to-peer transport works fine.

3. **Prior team-launch sessions can leave lingering team members.** The next session's orchestrator inherits the prior session's team and must clear it before spawning a new wave. NOTE — the harness exposes only `TeamCreate` and `TeamDelete`; there is NO `TeamList` tool. Per TeamCreate's "Discovering Team Members" docs, team membership lives on disk at `<user-config>/.claude/teams/{team-name}/config.json` (members array). Per TeamDelete's docs, the tool auto-detects the current session's team (no arg) and FAILS if members are still active — alive teammates must first receive `{type:"shutdown_request"}` via SendMessage. Verbatim user symptom: "the prior session is still active. Let me load TeamDelete, check for any lingering members, then clear it and create the new team."

Wave 7b (alty-cli-zc9 + alty-cli-l8r) shipped via a fifth Failure Mode 4 option not in the original preamble: orchestrator-as-router. See the Wave 7b handoff §Team-launch issue encountered for the full diagnostic chronology and a worked example of how 5 background-spawned agents completed a wave without any peer-to-peer SendMessage call.
design:
**Execution order at wave start (orchestrator preamble):**

1. **Step 0 — Pre-launch team-state hygiene.** Before any spawn:
   - Discover inherited team state via filesystem, NOT a list tool. List `<user-config>/.claude/teams/` (via Bash + Read); for each directory, read `config.json` and inspect the `members` array. There is no `TeamList` tool in this harness.
   - For every member discovered, SendMessage `{type:"shutdown_request"}` addressed to that members `name` (or `agentId` from `config.json` if name resolution fails). Each shutdown gracefully terminates the teammate.
   - Call `TeamDelete` (no arg — it auto-detects the inherited team). TeamDelete is destructive (removes the team + tasks directories) — NOT a no-op. If TeamDelete fails because members are still alive (race after shutdown), retry once after a short pause; if still failing, escalate to the user as a stuck-team-state condition (do NOT silently launch the wave on top of a stale team).
   - When no inherited team is present (empty `<user-config>/.claude/teams/`), Step 0 still emits a "no inherited team — clean state" log line so the absence is observable.

2. **Step 1 — Transport tool load.** `ToolSearch({query: "select:SendMessage,TaskList,TaskStop"})` in the orchestrator session. If `SendMessage` does not appear, abort per Failure mode 1.

3. **Step 2 — Peer-canary** (replaces the single-agent canary at current `launch-team.md:371-379`):
   - Spawn `peer-b` in BACKGROUND FIRST so it is addressable before any send. peer-b's prompt: `ToolSearch({query: "select:SendMessage"})`, record whether SendMessage loaded, then exit awaiting a peer message.
   - Spawn `peer-a` in FOREGROUND SECOND. peer-a's prompt: `ToolSearch({query: "select:SendMessage"})`, then `SendMessage({to: "peer-b", message: "<probe>"})`, then exit.
   - On peer-b's resume (triggered by peer-a's SendMessage), peer-b reports whether its own ToolSearch loaded SendMessage. If yes → peer-to-peer mode. If no → orchestrator-as-router mode.
   - Spawn ORDER matters: peer-b must be addressable before peer-a sends; reverse order makes peer-a's SendMessage fail with the same class of error this ticket is closing.

4. **Step 3 — Fan out the wave in the chosen mode.** Peer-to-peer mode follows the existing §P4 routing chart. Orchestrator-as-router mode follows the new subsection added by this work.

**Why peer-canary not single-agent canary:** the parent (orchestrator) is not addressable as a peer; a single-agent canary trying to send to `"orchestrator"` always fails to deliver even when transport is healthy. A 2-agent canary tests the only things that actually matter at wave start — peer-to-peer reachability AND whether background-spawned agents load SendMessage in this harness.

**Why orchestrator-as-router preserves §P3 unchanged:** in both modes, agents are one-shot and resume on incoming SendMessage. The difference is only who calls SendMessage — the peer (p2p mode) or the orchestrator (router mode). No agent-side prompt change is needed beyond "do not call SendMessage; emit final-output reports."

**Why `<user-config>` is a placeholder, not `~`:** the doc is OSS-distributed via the scaffold. Concrete home paths (e.g. `~/.claude/...` or `/home/<user>/.claude/...`) leak environment specifics into a committable artefact and trigger NoInternalLeaksRule. `<user-config>` is the documented placeholder convention for any per-user filesystem reference in the doc body.

**Citations:**
- `alto-scaffold/commands/launch-team.md` §Tool-loading preamble (lines 363-379, the single-agent canary to be replaced); §Team-Mode Communication Protocol §P3 (line 87, preserved unchanged); §Failure mode 4 (lines 905-927, gains option (d)).
- TeamCreate tool docs — "Discovering Team Members" section names `<user-config>/.claude/teams/{team-name}/config.json` with a `members` array as the team-state surface.
- TeamDelete tool docs — "fails if the team still has active members. Gracefully terminate teammates first"; "team name is automatically determined from the current session's team context" (no team_name arg).
- `.notes/handoff-wave-7b-dochealth.md` §Team-launch issue encountered (gitignored; informational reference only — do not cite from committable artefacts).
acceptance_criteria:
Doc-edit assertions (each verifiable by grep / reading the updated file):

- §Tool-loading preamble contains a **Step 0 BEFORE the canary** that:
  - Lists `<user-config>/.claude/teams/` and reads each `config.json` to enumerate inherited members (filesystem, NOT a `TeamList` tool — that tool does not exist).
  - For each member, emits a `SendMessage` invocation with `{type:"shutdown_request"}`.
  - Calls `TeamDelete` (no arg, auto-detected current-session team).
  - Documents the "TeamDelete fails on live members" branch with retry-once-then-escalate semantics, and the "no inherited team" empty-state branch with an observable log line.

- The single-agent canary block at the current `launch-team.md:371-379` is replaced by a 2-agent peer-canary block that:
  - Spawns `peer-b` in BACKGROUND FIRST (so it is addressable before any send).
  - Then spawns `peer-a` in FOREGROUND with a `SendMessage({to: "peer-b", ...})` call.
  - Decides transport mode by inspecting peer-bs ToolSearch outcome on resume.
  - Explicitly states the spawn order (peer-b first) in the doc body — reversing it re-triggers this tickets symptom class.

- An **orchestrator-as-router** subsection is added as a sibling to the current peer-to-peer protocol describing: agents emit canonical reports as final output; orchestrator quotes reports verbatim into the next agent's prompt (no paraphrase); resume via SendMessage from the main session embeds fix-requests / contracts.

- §P3 one-shot semantics text is **byte-identical** to its pre-update form (verify with `git diff` against the line range — preservation, not edit).

- §Failure mode 4 enumeration lists (a) defer, (b) single-agent, (c) re-groom, **and (d) orchestrator-as-router** with a pointer to the new subsection.

- Privacy: `grep -nE '/home/[a-z]+/|<your-username>|~/' alto-scaffold/commands/launch-team.md` produces **zero matches**. All per-user filesystem references use `<user-config>/...` placeholders.

Empirical validation:

- The next wave that triggers team-launch with the updated protocol either runs cleanly in peer-to-peer mode or drops cleanly into orchestrator-as-router without manual mid-flow intervention from the user. No "lingering team" / "TeamList not found" / "TeamDelete fails on live members" surprises.

- §Tool-loading preamble (canary to be replaced): old lines 363-379 → now lines 751-770 (in the team-mode-only Step 6.0 block). The body command file also gained a NEW Step -1 — Harness probe at lines 52-77 with the same single-agent canary pattern.

Suggest reviewing whether items 1-3 reduce the scope of this ticket before re-claiming. Citations otherwise still apply.

title: feat(ci): preflight check that hook-referenced scripts resolve
description:
## Goal / Problem

Structural follow-up from `alty-cli-6n4` root-cause Q5: the bd-close-hook
(and any future hook in `bin/` or `.claude/`) references the script it
execs by literal string path. No automated check verifies that path
resolves on `main`. When `.alto/` was renamed to `alto-scaffold/` in
commit `56fdd29`, the hook's `RIPPLE="$PROJECT_ROOT/bin/bd-ripple"`
silently broke; the same class of break can recur next time anything
moves.

`alty-cli-6n4` flipped the runtime behaviour from silent `exit 0` to
loud `exit 1` so the NEXT break will surface immediately. This ticket
adds the EARLIER check: catch the break at preflight time, before push.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `make preflight` (or `.githooks/pre-push`) runs a small script that:
  - Scans `bin/bd-close-hook` (and any `.git/hooks/*` if present locally)
    for `RIPPLE=` or similar assignments to a literal path
  - Greps `.claude/settings.local.json` allow patterns for hook-related
    `Bash(...)` entries
  - Asserts each referenced path resolves to an executable file
- [ ] Failing test added: a deliberately bad path in a fixture
  (e.g. `tests/fixtures/hooks/bad/bd-close-hook`) fails the check
- [ ] Passing test: current `bin/bd-close-hook` after `alty-cli-6n4`
  fix passes the check
- [ ] Documentation: README's "First-time setup" section mentions the
  new gate
- [ ] `make ci-local` 6/6 green

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Workflow / tooling (`make preflight` surface) |
| Layer | Outside the bounded contexts — pure tooling gate |

## Steps

1. Decide where the check lives. Three options:
   a. New `scripts/preflight/check-hook-paths.sh` — invoked by `Makefile`
      `preflight` target after `bd preflight --check`.
   b. New Go cmd `cmd/altohealth` or extend `alto doc-health` with a
      `--paths=hooks/` mode.
   c. Bash inside `.githooks/pre-push` (smallest scope, no install step).
2. Recommended: (a) — Makefile-driven, single-shot, no new Go surface,
   composable with `ci-local`.
3. Write the script: parse `RIPPLE=...` assignments, resolve each path
   relative to its hook's directory, fail with the offending path if not
   executable.
4. Wire into `Makefile preflight` after the `bd preflight --check` line.
5. Add fixture test case.

## Out of Scope

- Generalising to other shell scripts in the repo. This is hook-specific.
- A Go re-implementation. Bash is fine for a glue check.

## Risks / Dependencies

- Risk: false positives on hook scripts that derive paths dynamically.
  Mitigation: limit the regex to `RIPPLE=` and `BD_*=` assignments.
- Dependency: none.

## Labels

`task`, `dochealth`, `ci`, `dogfooding`

---

## DISCOVERED FROM

- `alty-cli-6n4` root-cause Q5: "the connection between 'hook references
  X' and 'X moved' is implicit (string path in bash), not explicit (a
  typed dependency)". Filed as the structural action item from the
  blameless Five Whys analysis.

title: fix(hook): bin/bd-close-hook hardcodes moved bin/bd-ripple path -> silent ripple-miss
description:
## Severity & Priority

- **Severity:** S2 — feature degraded (silent ripple-miss); workaround exists (run `alto-scaffold/scripts/bd-ripple <id>` manually). Dogfood-loop impact only; no end-user surface.
- **Priority:** P3
- **RCA artifact:** inline below (S2 — separate doc not required)

## Goal / Problem

`bin/bd-close-hook` fires on every `bd close` from a Claude Code session, but the ripple script it `exec`s lives at a path that no longer exists. The hook silently no-ops on the missing script, so the documented After-Close Protocol's auto-ripple step has not run for any `bd close` in this repo since commit 56fdd29.

## Environment

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| OS / runtime | Linux 6.8.0-111-generic / bash (any) |
| alto version | `0e9b4fc..05a4e51` (any commit after `56fdd29`) |
| Tool surface | `.claude/settings.local.json` PostToolUse hook → `bin/bd-close-hook` |
| First-seen commit | `56fdd29` (the `.alto/` → `alto-scaffold/` rename — when `bin/bd-ripple` moved out from under the hook) |
| Last-known-good commit | The commit immediately before `56fdd29` |

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Clean checkout of this repo on any commit after `56fdd29`. Confirm `bin/bd-close-hook` is registered as a Claude Code PostToolUse hook (see `.claude/settings.local.json:140-145`).
2. Create a pair of tickets where the second formally depends on the first:

   ```bash
   bd create --title="first"  --type=task --priority=3
   bd create --title="second" --type=task --priority=3
   bd dep add <second-id> <first-id>
   ```

3. Close the first ticket from inside a Claude Code session: `bd close <first-id> --reason "test ripple"`.

## Expected Result

After `bd close`, the PostToolUse hook execs `alto-scaffold/scripts/bd-ripple`, which flags `<second-id>` with the `review_needed` label and adds a context-diff comment.

## Actual Result

`bd close` returns success. The hook fires (visible in Claude Code's permission allowlist activity). But `bd label list <second-id>` shows no `review_needed`, and `bd comments <second-id>` shows no new comment. No error surfaces anywhere — neither in Claude Code nor in any log.

## Evidence

```bash
$ sed -n '48,55p' bin/bd-close-hook
# Find the project root (where bin/bd-ripple lives).
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PROJECT_ROOT="$(dirname "$SCRIPT_DIR")"
RIPPLE="$PROJECT_ROOT/bin/bd-ripple"

if [[ ! -x "$RIPPLE" ]]; then
    exit 0
fi

$ ls bin/bd-ripple 2>&1
ls: cannot access 'bin/bd-ripple': No such file or directory

$ ls alto-scaffold/scripts/bd-ripple
-rwxr-xr-x 1 kusanagi kusanagi 8881 Jun 1 16:52 alto-scaffold/scripts/bd-ripple

$ grep -n bd-ripple .claude/settings.local.json
65:      "Bash(bin/bd-ripple:*)",
89:      "Bash(./bin/bd-ripple:*)",
```

The two permission allowlist entries point at the moved file and are also stale.

## Reproducibility

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Rate | Always (deterministic — file is or is not on disk) |
| Across machines? | Yes |
| Concurrency-dependent? | No |
| Time-dependent? | No |

## Detection

- [x] Adjacent ticket grooming surfaced it — discovered while grooming `alty-cli-i80` (the productization ticket) on 2026-06-01.
- [x] Wave-4 close-out (the operator had to run ripple manually because the hook was silently no-op-ing).

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | N/A — this is a workflow / tooling defect, not a domain change |
| Layer | Tooling (`bin/`, `.claude/settings.local.json`) |
| Aggregate | N/A |

The productized cross-tool replacement (`alto ticket-ripple` Go subcommand + `alto init` beads hook scaffold) lives in the Ticket BC and is tracked separately as `alty-cli-2f9` + `alty-cli-bf7`. This ticket is the in-repo workaround patch only.

## Root Cause (Five Whys)

| # | Why? | Answer | Evidence |
|---|------|--------|----------|
| Q1 | Why does ripple not run when `bd close` fires? | `bin/bd-close-hook:51` references `$PROJECT_ROOT/bin/bd-ripple`, but `bin/bd-ripple` no longer exists. | `bin/bd-close-hook:51`, `ls bin/bd-ripple` fails |
| Q2 | Why doesn't the hook surface the missing-script case? | Lines 53–55 silently `exit 0` when `$RIPPLE` is not executable. No `>&2` write, no error code. | `bin/bd-close-hook:53-55` |
| Q3 (system) | Why was silent fall-through chosen for the missing-script branch? | Defensive design from when the hook was first added — the hook fires on every Bash tool call, and the original concern was "do not block the user's flow if the ripple script is unavailable". The cost flipped once the After-Close Protocol became load-bearing on the auto-ripple, but the hook did not get re-examined. | git history of `bin/bd-close-hook` |
| Q4 (system) | Why did the `.alto/` → `alto-scaffold/` rename in commit `56fdd29` not propagate to the hook? | The rename's scope was the scaffold tree itself. `bin/` is a per-project working-tree convention that lives outside `alto-scaffold/`, so the rename PR's file-list did not include it. The hook's reference is a literal string path in bash — no static analysis or test connects "hook references X" to "X moved". | `git show 56fdd29 --stat` shows no `bin/` touch |
| Q5 (system) | Why is there no check that hook scripts reference existing files? | The PostToolUse-hook pattern is *implicit*: the hook is registered by string path in `.claude/settings.local.json`, and the script it execs is a string path in the script body. There is no typed dependency, no integration test that exercises the hook end-to-end, and no preflight gate that verifies hook-referenced paths resolve. The same gap exists for the `.claude/settings.local.json:65,89` permission entries that ALSO reference the moved path. | `bd preflight --check` doesn't scan hook references; no `*_test.bats` or equivalent in the tree |

**Root cause (one sentence):** the hook references a script path with no static check, no integration test, and a silent missing-file fallback — so a scaffold-tree rename three levels up in the directory hierarchy broke it invisibly, and the After-Close Protocol has been load-bearing on manual execution ever since.

**Contributing factors:**

- `.claude/settings.local.json:65,89` permission entries also reference the moved `bin/bd-ripple` path — same root cause, separate surface
- The hook's silent fall-through makes the failure invisible even after it occurs — discoverability is the deeper issue

## TDD Workflow

This is a bash-script fix, so the RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle is light. The "regression test" is a manual smoke + a preflight rule.

### RED Phase — failing reproduction

Run the Steps to Reproduce above on `HEAD` before the fix. Confirm the second ticket does NOT receive the `review_needed` label (capture `bd label list <second-id>` output for the Verification section).

### GREEN Phase — minimal fix

1. `bin/bd-close-hook:51` — change `RIPPLE="$PROJECT_ROOT/bin/bd-ripple"` to `RIPPLE="$PROJECT_ROOT/alto-scaffold/scripts/bd-ripple"`.
2. `bin/bd-close-hook:53-55` — change the silent `exit 0` to:
   ```bash
   echo "bd-close-hook: ripple script not at $RIPPLE" >&2
   exit 1
   ```
   The silent branch is exactly how this bug went unnoticed.
3. `.claude/settings.local.json:65,89` — update both `Bash(bin/bd-ripple:*)` entries to `Bash(alto-scaffold/scripts/bd-ripple:*)` and `Bash(./alto-scaffold/scripts/bd-ripple:*)`.

### REFACTOR Phase

- Re-run the Steps to Reproduce — verify the second ticket now has the `review_needed` label.
- Run `make preflight` — should remain 6/6 green.
- Test the failure path: temporarily rename `alto-scaffold/scripts/bd-ripple` and run `bd close` again — verify the hook now writes `bd-close-hook: ripple script not at ...` to stderr and exits 1.

## Verification

### Before fix (REPRODUCE)

```
commit: <hash of HEAD before fix>
$ bd close <first-id> --reason "test ripple"
✓ Closed alty-cli-<first-id>
$ bd label list <second-id>
(no review_needed label)
```

### After fix (RESOLVED)

```
commit: <fix commit hash>
$ bd close <first-id> --reason "test ripple"
✓ Closed alty-cli-<first-id>
[ripple output to stdout, flagging dependents]
$ bd label list <second-id>
```

Follow-up suggestion (file as separate ticket if approved): add a `make preflight` check that `grep`s `bin/bd-close-hook` for the literal path and asserts the file resolves. Catches the next rename automatically.

title: fix(dochealth): FrontmatterSchemaRule rejects valid YAML-list "tools" as missing
description:
## Severity & Priority

- **Severity:** S2 — feature degraded (false ERROR on canonically valid input); workaround exists (use inline-CSV form documented in `write-a-workflow-asset.md`). Internal tooling only; no end-user surface.
- **Priority:** P3
- **RCA artifact:** inline below (S2 — separate doc not required)

## Goal / Problem

`FrontmatterSchemaRule` is the canonical schema gate for scaffold assets. It emits a false `missing required frontmatter field "tools"` ERROR when an asset author writes the field as a YAML block list — even though a YAML block list is the canonically allowed form (the downstream parser `toolsList` accepts both string and `[]any`). The schema gate and the parser are inconsistent: the gate is string-only, the parser is polymorphic. Any author who uses the natural YAML-list form hits a false error and is forced into the documented CSV workaround.

## Environment

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| OS / runtime | any / Go 1.26 |
| alto version | `3bfafd8` onward (post `tools_required → tools` rename); same shape pre-rename with the literal `tools_required` field name |
| Tool surface | `alto doc-health --paths=alto-scaffold/` → `FrontmatterSchemaRule` |
| First-seen commit | `5a860a4` (`feat(dochealth): .alto/ scaffold-health validator (alty-cli-766.7)`) — the commit that introduced `FrontmatterSchemaRule` and its `stringValue` presence-check |
| Last-known-good commit | None — bug was present from the rule's first commit |

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a scaffold asset at `alto-scaffold/lifecycle/in-progress/repro.md` with frontmatter that uses a YAML block list for `tools`:

   ```yaml
   ---
   name: repro
   description: demo
   kind: command
   phase: design
   when_to_use: demo
   tools:
     - Read
     - Write
   bash_substitution_policy: none
   license: Apache-2.0
   ---
   # /repro
   ```

2. Run `go run ./cmd/alto doc-health --paths=alto-scaffold/`.

## Expected Result

Zero violations on `repro.md`. The asset is canonically well-formed: `tools` is present with two valid entries, and the downstream parser `toolsList` at [internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/rules.go:107-134](internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/rules.go#L107-L134) accepts the `[]any` shape.

## Actual Result

`FrontmatterSchemaRule` emits ERROR:

```
ERROR FrontmatterSchemaRule alto-scaffold/lifecycle/in-progress/repro.md — missing required frontmatter field "tools"
```

Downstream rules (`UnknownToolsRule`, `BashArgumentsRule`) parse `tools` correctly and pass — confirming the field IS canonically present and the schema gate is wrong, not the asset.

## Evidence

```go
// internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/frontmatter_schema_rule.go:55-64
fm := asset.Frontmatter()
var out []dochealthdomain.ScaffoldViolation
for _, field := range canonicalSchemaFields {
    if _, ok := stringValue(fm, field); !ok {
        out = append(out, makeViolation(
            pathDisplay(asset.Path()),
            r.Name(),
            fmt.Sprintf("missing required frontmatter field %q", field),
        ))
    }
}
```

`stringValue` (defined elsewhere in `rules.go`) returns `ok=false` for any non-string value. `tools` is in `canonicalSchemaFields` and is the only field whose canonical type is `string OR []any`.

Compare with the polymorphic parser:

```go
// internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/rules.go:107-134
func toolsList(fm map[string]any) []string {
    raw, ok := fm["tools"]
    if !ok { return nil }
    switch v := raw.(type) {
    case string:    // CSV form
        ...
    case []any:     // YAML block-list form
        ...
    default:
        return nil
    }
}
```

The parser accepts both; the schema gate accepts only one. Inconsistency.

## Reproducibility

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Rate | Always — deterministic on input shape |
| Across machines? | Yes |
| Concurrency-dependent? | No |
| Time-dependent? | No |

## Detection

- [x] Adjacent ticket grooming surfaced it — discovered during `alty-cli-766.6` (write-a-workflow-asset meta-skill) review on 2026-05-31.
- [x] Documented workaround already in place: the meta-skill at [alto-scaffold/commands/write-a-workflow-asset.md:91-98](alto-scaffold/commands/write-a-workflow-asset.md#L91-L98) instructs authors to use CSV-only — a symptom-level patch, not a root-cause fix.

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | `dochealth` |
| Layer | Infrastructure (`internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/`) |
| Aggregate | `ScaffoldAsset` — the rule reads `asset.Frontmatter()` |

No domain change. The fix is a localized improvement to one rule's presence-check.

## Root Cause (Five Whys)

| # | Why? | Answer | Evidence |
|---|------|--------|----------|
| Q1 | Why does `FrontmatterSchemaRule` report `tools` as missing when it IS present (as a YAML list)? | The check at `frontmatter_schema_rule.go:59` uses `stringValue(fm, field)`, which returns `ok=false` for non-string values. A YAML block list parses to `[]any`. | `frontmatter_schema_rule.go:55-64` |
| Q2 | Why is `stringValue` used for *presence* checking when some canonical fields are polymorphic? | The original rule conflated "field present" with "field is a non-empty string" — that conflation was correct for 7 of the 8 canonical fields, but `tools` is semantically a list and got compressed into the string form for spec simplicity. | `canonicalSchemaFields` declared in `frontmatter_schema_rule.go:13-22`; 7 of 8 ARE string-typed |
| Q3 (system) | Why did the 8-field spec compress a list-typed field into a string? | The spike `docs/research/20260529_workflow-scaffold-generic.md:224-244` specified the canonical schema as 8 string-shaped key-value pairs for editor ergonomics — simple to write, simple to validate. YAML allows BOTH forms, and authors familiar with YAML reach for block-list first. The spec did not say which form was canonical for `tools`. | spike L224-244 |
| Q4 (system) | Why did the implementation not converge on a single canonical form? | The downstream parser `toolsList` at `rules.go:107-134` was written defensively to accept BOTH forms — likely because the author noticed real assets in both shapes during development. But the schema gate kept the original string-only check. Two layers, two different opinions. | `rules.go:107-134` vs `frontmatter_schema_rule.go:55-64` |
| Q5 (system) | Why didn't a test catch the inconsistency between the schema gate and the downstream parser? | No test combines "valid YAML block-list for `tools`" with "FrontmatterSchemaRule should pass". `frontmatter_schema_rule_test.go` exercises missing/regex/enum cases for string-typed fields. The integration between schema-gate's presence-check and `toolsList`'s parser, for the list form, is untested. | `internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/frontmatter_schema_rule_test.go` — grep for `[]any` or block-list returns no matches |

**Root cause (one sentence):** `FrontmatterSchemaRule` uses a string-only presence check for fields that are canonically polymorphic (`string` OR `[]any`), creating a false-missing error whenever an author chooses the YAML-list form — the schema gate and the downstream parser have inconsistent type assumptions and no test pins them to a shared truth.

**Contributing factors:**

- The `tools_required → tools` rename in commit `3bfafd8` updated the field name but did not address the type-narrowness — the bug persists at the new name. (Renaming is not fixing.)
- The write-a-workflow-asset meta-skill documents the CSV workaround as authoritative guidance, which makes the symptom invisible to new authors but encodes the bug into the docs.
- The schema gate is one of seven rules that share the `canonicalSchemaFields` list. Any future polymorphic field would hit the same trap.

## TDD Workflow

### RED Phase — failing regression tests

New tests in `internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/frontmatter_schema_rule_test.go`:

- `TestFrontmatterSchemaRule_ToolsAsYAMLList_PassesPresenceCheck` — frontmatter has `tools: [Read, Write]` → no `missing required frontmatter field "tools"` violation
- `TestFrontmatterSchemaRule_ToolsAsInlineCSV_PassesPresenceCheck` — frontmatter has `tools: "Read, Write"` → no violation (regression guard for the current passing case)
- `TestFrontmatterSchemaRule_ToolsAsEmptyList_FailsAsMissing` — frontmatter has `tools: []` → emits missing violation (empty list = no tools = missing)
- `TestFrontmatterSchemaRule_ToolsAsEmptyString_FailsAsMissing` — frontmatter has `tools: ""` → emits missing violation (regression guard)
- `TestFrontmatterSchemaRule_ToolsMissingKey_FailsAsMissing` — `tools` absent entirely → emits missing violation (regression guard)
- `TestFrontmatterSchemaRule_NonToolsFields_StillStringOnly` — `name: 42` (int), `kind: [command]` (list) → both emit missing violations (the polymorphic carve-out applies to `tools` only)

```bash
go test -run TestFrontmatterSchemaRule -count=1 ./internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/
# expected: FAIL on the new tests
```

### GREEN Phase — minimal fix

Two design options:

| Option | Approach | Trade-off |
|--------|----------|-----------|
| **A** | Generalise: introduce a `fieldPresent(fm, key) bool` helper that accepts string-non-empty OR `[]any`-non-empty. Use it in the for-loop. Keep `stringValue` for the typed regex/enum checks on `name`/`kind`. | Principled; covers any future polymorphic field |
| **B** | Special-case: in the for-loop, when `field == "tools"`, call `len(toolsList(fm)) > 0` instead of `stringValue`. Other fields stay on `stringValue`. | Minimal LOC; tight to one field |

**Recommendation: Option A.** Reasons: (1) the bug class is "presence check uses the wrong typer for polymorphic fields", and option A fixes the class. (2) `toolsList` would have to be imported into the schema rule, creating a dependency the schema gate previously didn't have.

```go
// Add to rules.go:
func fieldPresent(fm map[string]any, key string) bool {
    raw, ok := fm[key]
    if !ok || raw == nil {
        return false
    }
    switch v := raw.(type) {
    case string:
        return strings.TrimSpace(v) != ""
    case []any:
        return len(v) > 0
    default:
        return false
    }
}

// In frontmatter_schema_rule.go, change line 59:
if !fieldPresent(fm, field) {
    out = append(out, makeViolation(...))
}
```

```bash
go test -run TestFrontmatterSchemaRule -count=1 ./internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/
# expected: PASS on all (new + existing)
```

### REFACTOR Phase

- Run the full `internal/dochealth/...` suite to verify no other rule broke.
- Run `make ci-local` to verify the full preflight green.
- Verify `go run ./cmd/alto doc-health --paths=alto-scaffold/` is still 0 violations on the canonical scaffold (the existing assets all use CSV; the fix should not regress them).
- Update the write-a-workflow-asset meta-skill at `alto-scaffold/commands/write-a-workflow-asset.md:91-98` to note that both forms are now canonical — CSV is no longer mandatory, just the recommended terse form. (This is a documentation cleanup that removes the symptom-level workaround.)

## Verification

### Before fix (REPRODUCE)

```
commit: <hash of HEAD before fix>
$ go test -run TestFrontmatterSchemaRule_ToolsAsYAMLList_PassesPresenceCheck -count=1 ./internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/
--- FAIL: TestFrontmatterSchemaRule_ToolsAsYAMLList_PassesPresenceCheck
    frontmatter_schema_rule_test.go:NN: ... expected no violation; got: missing required frontmatter field "tools"
FAIL
```

### After fix (RESOLVED)

```
commit: <fix commit hash>
$ go test -run TestFrontmatterSchemaRule -count=1 ./internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/
PASS  (NN tests)
```

### Regression guard

The 6 new tests stay in the suite. Specifically:

- `TestFrontmatterSchemaRule_ToolsAsYAMLList_PassesPresenceCheck` — fails if the schema gate ever regresses to string-only
- `TestFrontmatterSchemaRule_NonToolsFields_StillStringOnly` — fails if someone over-relaxes the polymorphic carve-out and starts accepting lists for `name` / `kind` / etc.

Removing either of these tests in a future PR requires written justification.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Failing regression tests added** in RED phase, all six listed above
- [ ] **Fix passes** all six tests AND the full `internal/dochealth/...` suite
- [ ] **Verification block** above filled with verbatim before-FAIL + after-PASS output and the fix commit hash
- [ ] **Design path A selected** (`fieldPresent` helper) — Option B requires explicit justification
- [ ] **Inline Root Cause section** complete with all five whys and `file:line` evidence (already in this template)
- [ ] **Meta-skill workaround text cleaned up** at `alto-scaffold/commands/write-a-workflow-asset.md:91-98` to remove the "CSV only" guidance now that both forms validate
- [ ] **Doc-health stays clean** on the full scaffold (`alto doc-health --paths=alto-scaffold/` → 0 violations)
- [ ] `make ci-local` 6/6 green
- [ ] Coverage on `fieldPresent` ≥ 80% (it's a small helper; trivial to hit)

## Out of Scope

- Renaming the field again. The `tools` name is fine; only the type-handling is broken.
- Adding a JSON-schema-style declarative spec for the 8 canonical fields. Worth a separate refactor ticket if the polymorphism appears in another field — out of scope here.
- The other 7 canonical fields. They are string-typed by design; the polymorphic carve-out applies to `tools` only.

## Risks / Dependencies

- Risk: A poorly-written `fieldPresent` could silently accept other shapes (`map[string]any`, `bool`). Mitigation: the `switch` explicitly covers `string` and `[]any` and returns `false` in the default arm — same pattern `toolsList` already uses.
- Dependency: none. Self-contained fix inside `internal/dochealth/infrastructure/rules/`.

## Labels

`bug`, `severity:S2`, `dochealth`, `scaffold`

---

## DISCOVERED FROM

- `alty-cli-766.6` (write-a-workflow-asset meta-skill) review on 2026-05-31
- The CSV-only workaround documented in `alto-scaffold/commands/write-a-workflow-asset.md` — the bug, encoded as guidance

title: feat(dochealth): bash-rule regex catches ${VAR:-default} parameter-expansion forms
description:
> Source: ihk Round 1 SUB-FINDING-1 (see .notes/wave-3-relay/wh-reverify-ihk-round1.md §SUB-FINDING-1). TL decision Option B per .notes/wave-3-relay/tl-decision-ihk-sub-finding-1.md.

## Goal

WH SUB-FINDING-1 identified that "${ARGUMENTS:-default}" parameter-expansion form is not caught by the current brace regex in bash_substitution_policy_rule.go:32. Bare "${X}" and indexed "${X[N]}" forms ARE caught; only the parameter-expansion suffix gap (:-, :=, :?, :+, ##, %%, /, etc.) remains.

Defence-in-depth gap. Bare brace form catches common case; this extends coverage to advanced bash idioms.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Extend the brace inner pattern in unquotedSubstitutionRegex to allow optional [^}]* suffix after the identifier.
- Suggested regex (per WH):
  \{(?:ARGUMENTS(?:\[[0-9]+\])?|[0-9]+|[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)(?:[^}]*)?\}
- 2 new test cases:
  - "${ARGUMENTS:-d}" fires (BashArgumentsRule)
  - "\"${ARGUMENTS:-d}\"" passes (quoted form)
- All existing rule tests still pass.
- arch-go 100% unchanged.

## Suggested fix scope

~5 LOC regex + 2 test cases.

title: test(bootstrap): expand TestEmbedScaffoldWriter_NoSecretsInEmbed to 13 high-precision token regexes
description:
## Goal

Current TestEmbedScaffoldWriter_NoSecretsInEmbed at internal/bootstrap/infrastructure/embed_scaffold_writer_test.go:212 asserts 3 high-precision patterns:
- AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16} (AWS access key)
- gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,} (GitHub PAT family)
- -----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY----- (PEM private key)

WH's 20-pattern superset sweep (alty-cli-766.4 wave-3 re-verify) confirmed zero hits across 34 embed files. Dev-Deviation 5 reduced scope to those 3 patterns. This ticket EXPANDS proactively, codifying ~13 of WH's curated patterns into the test as ongoing regression guards.

Source: WH re-verify recommendation on alty-cli-766.4 wave-3 review.

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Bootstrap (infrastructure test) |

- **Each pattern carries an explanatory inline comment** naming the secret family and citing WH's pattern source.
- **Table-driven structure.** Use a regex-per-row table with name + pattern + provenance comment; iterate the embed.FS walk once per pattern, assert zero matches.

## Pattern list (WH-curated)

| # | Family | Regex |
|---|--------|-------|
| 1 | AWS access key | AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16} |
| 2 | GitHub PAT/OAuth | gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,} |
| 3 | PEM private key | -----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY----- |
| 4 | OpenSSH private key | -----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY----- |
| 5 | PGP/GPG private key | -----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK----- |
| 6 | Slack token | xox[abps]-[0-9]+-[0-9a-zA-Z-]+ |
| 7 | Stripe live key | (sk|pk)_live_[A-Za-z0-9]{24,} |
| 8 | OpenAI API key | sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{48} |
| 9 | Anthropic API key | sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{90,} |
| 10 | JWT | eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\\.eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+ |
| 11 | Google API key | AIza[A-Za-z0-9_-]{35} |
| 12 | npm token | npm_[A-Za-z0-9]{36} |
| 13 | SendGrid key | SG\\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{22}\\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43} |
| 14 | Twilio SID | AC[a-f0-9]{32} |
| 15 | Database URI w/ creds | (mongodb|postgres|mysql|redis)://[^@\\s]+:[^@\\s]+@ |
| 16 | Basic-auth URL | https?://[^/@\\s]+:[^/@\\s]+@ |

(Picking the strongest 13 from this 16-pattern superset is fine — the table is a starting bank; AC is ≥ 13 patterns asserted, each with provenance comment.)

## TDD Workflow

- **GREEN phase:** No production change required. The test passing on the current embed corpus IS the green signal.
- **Future regression:** If a new embed file introduces any of the 13 secret families, this test fails before merge.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: feat(bootstrap): WithPreviewWriter(io.Writer) option on EmbedScaffoldWriter for CI/logger pipe
description:
## Goal

[OVERWRITE] preview lines currently go directly to os.Stderr (Dev-Deviation 4 from wave-3). Functional behavior is correct. But a future feature wanting to pipe [OVERWRITE] to a logger or transform it (e.g., JSON output for CI) has no seam.

Add a WithPreviewWriter(io.Writer) option to EmbedScaffoldWriter. Default behavior unchanged (os.Stderr); option enables custom destination for CI/logger consumers.

Source: QA-MIN-1 finding on alty-cli-766.4 wave-3 QA review.

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Bootstrap (infrastructure adapter) |
| Ubiquitous Language | EmbedScaffoldWriter, PreviewWriter (io.Writer seam) |
| Layer | Infrastructure — port (ScaffoldWriter) signature unchanged; adapter constructor gains options |

## Design — settled decisions

The 'BootstrapOption-style functional option' phrasing in the original brief is aspirational — that pattern does NOT yet exist in this codebase. This ticket DEFINES the pattern for EmbedScaffoldWriter.

**Concrete shape:**

```go
// internal/bootstrap/infrastructure/embed_scaffold_writer.go

type EmbedScaffoldWriter struct {
    // ... existing fields ...
    previewWriter io.Writer  // NEW field; defaults to os.Stderr
}

type EmbedScaffoldWriterOption func(*EmbedScaffoldWriter)

func WithPreviewWriter(w io.Writer) EmbedScaffoldWriterOption {
    return func(e *EmbedScaffoldWriter) { e.previewWriter = w }
}

func NewEmbedScaffoldWriter(opts ...EmbedScaffoldWriterOption) *EmbedScaffoldWriter {
    w := &EmbedScaffoldWriter{
        // ... existing field defaults ...
        previewWriter: os.Stderr,
    }
    for _, opt := range opts {
        opt(w)
    }
    return w
}
```

- **Line 109 rewrite.** Current internal/bootstrap/infrastructure/embed_scaffold_writer.go:109 reads:
  _, _ = fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[OVERWRITE] alto-scaffold/%s\\n", filepath.ToSlash(rel))
  Replace os.Stderr with w.previewWriter.
- **Variadic options preserve backward compatibility.** All 9 existing call sites of NewEmbedScaffoldWriter() compile unchanged:
  - internal/bootstrap/infrastructure/embed_scaffold_writer_export_test.go:25,37,60,73
  - internal/bootstrap/infrastructure/embed_scaffold_writer_test.go:37,44,59,106,115
  Plus the composition-root call site in internal/composition/app.go.

## TDD Workflow — RED tests by name

internal/bootstrap/infrastructure/embed_scaffold_writer_test.go:
- TestEmbedScaffoldWriter_WithoutOption_DefaultsToStderr — sanity test: construct via the no-arg form, verify the [OVERWRITE] line still appears on os.Stderr (use a captured-stderr helper or skip the assertion if too brittle; the option-not-set case is the more important behaviour to preserve).
- TestEmbedScaffoldWriter_WithPreviewWriter_OverridesDestination — pass a bytes.Buffer via WithPreviewWriter, trigger an overwrite scenario, assert the [OVERWRITE] line appears in the buffer and NOT on os.Stderr.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New exported types: EmbedScaffoldWriterOption (function type), WithPreviewWriter (option constructor).
- NewEmbedScaffoldWriter signature changes to variadic options: NewEmbedScaffoldWriter(opts ...EmbedScaffoldWriterOption) *EmbedScaffoldWriter.
- New EmbedScaffoldWriter.previewWriter field defaults to os.Stderr when no option supplied.
- Line 109 of embed_scaffold_writer.go writes to w.previewWriter (NOT os.Stderr directly).
- ALL 9 existing call sites of NewEmbedScaffoldWriter() compile unchanged (no code edits at call sites, just at the constructor + struct).
- 2 RED tests above pass.
- arch-go 100% unchanged (no new package boundaries).
- go build / vet / golangci-lint / go test ./... -race all clean.

## Files

| Path | Action |
|------|--------|
| internal/bootstrap/infrastructure/embed_scaffold_writer.go | MODIFY (new field, new types, constructor variadic, line 109 rewrite) |
| internal/bootstrap/infrastructure/embed_scaffold_writer_test.go | MODIFY (2 new RED tests) |

## Existing code (REUSE, do NOT recreate)

- The 9 call sites of NewEmbedScaffoldWriter() — DO NOT EDIT; they must compile unchanged.
- The existing struct fields + writer methods — UNCHANGED except for line 109.

## Scope

~25 LOC (option types + field + constructor refactor + line 109 swap) + 2 test cases.

title: refactor(shared): hoist frontmatter parser to internal/shared/infrastructure/markdown/
description:

title: chore(dochealth): clear 81 pre-existing docs/ violations surfaced by alty-cli-766.2 close-out
description:
> **Before Starting:** Confirm `alty-cli-766.2` closed and the `alto-scaffold/` migration is in place. This ticket addresses PRE-EXISTING `docs/` violations surfaced by `alto doc-health` during the 766.2 close-out (concern C); it does NOT validate `alto-scaffold/` (that work landed in 766.7 + ihk).
>
> **Freshness:** Run `bd label list <this-id>` and check for `review_needed` before starting. This ticket was groomed against the post-Wave-3 codebase: paths are `alto-scaffold/` (not `.alto/`); 81-violation count re-verified on 2026-06-01.

## Goal / Problem

`go run ./cmd/alto doc-health` currently reports **81 violations** across `docs/` — all pre-existing tech debt, none introduced by the 766.2 scaffold migration. The migration's Phase 7 verification documented this as concern C and explicitly deferred remediation so the migration commit set could close clean against the gates it owned. This ticket inventories the 81 violations, classifies them by `DocHealthStatus`, and clears them in order of effort-to-payoff. Closure removes the only remaining background noise in `alto doc-health` output and re-establishes the gate as a "zero or fail" signal for future work.

## Background / Context

- **Origin:** 766.2 Phase 7 close report classified concern C as "ACCEPTED as pre-existing tech debt", with 81 violations all in `docs/*` and zero in `alto-scaffold/*`. Re-verified post-Wave-3.
- **Current distribution (re-counted 2026-06-01):**
  - 3 `stale`: `docs/PRD.md`, `docs/DDD.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (freshness thresholds exceeded)
  - ~28 `stale`: `docs/research/20260222_*` files (date-prefixed research reports exceeding the freshness window)
  - ~50 `no_frontmatter`: docs missing the required frontmatter that `FrontmatterSchemaRule` expects
- **Pattern references (read at ticket-claim time, NOT now to keep description fresh):**
  - `internal/dochealth/application/doc_health_handler.go` — `Handle(ctx, projectDir) (domain.DocHealthReport, error)` — the call surface that emits the violations
  - `internal/dochealth/domain/doc_health.go:13-22` — `DocHealthStatus` enum (`ok`, `stale`, `missing`, `no_frontmatter`) determines violation type
  - Audit start point: `go run ./cmd/alto doc-health 2>&1 | grep -cE "^\s+!"` confirms the running count
- **No new Go code shipped here.** This is a docs hygiene ticket — the deliverable is updates to `docs/*` files plus, if any class of violation is fundamentally invalid (e.g. spike reports legitimately predate a freshness window and re-stamping is wrong), a one-line config or rule change with justification recorded in the PR.

## DDD Alignment

N/A. This ticket touches `docs/` content + (possibly) `internal/dochealth/` config / rule constants. No bounded-context boundaries crossed. No new ubiquitous-language terms.

## Steps

1. Run `go run ./cmd/alto doc-health 2>&1` and capture full output to a scratch file (NOT committed).
2. Bucket the 81 violations by `DocHealthStatus`: `stale`, `missing`, `no_frontmatter`, `broken_link`.
3. For each bucket:
   - **stale**: refresh `last_updated` (or equivalent) on docs that genuinely have been reviewed and remain accurate. For PRD / DDD / ARCHITECTURE specifically, confirm with the operator before re-stamping that the content is still current.
   - **no_frontmatter** on `docs/research/*`: spike research reports historically shipped without frontmatter. Either (a) backfill minimal frontmatter (`title`, `date`, `status: archive`) per a single template; OR (b) extend `internal/dochealth/` to exempt the `docs/research/**` glob with a justified comment. Pick one before grinding — both touch every file once.
   - **broken_link**: fix or remove dead links.
4. Re-run `go run ./cmd/alto doc-health 2>&1` — must report 0 violations.

title: fix: mark discovery.completed = true in config.toml after guide completes
description:
## Problem

After successful `alto guide`, `.alto/config.toml` still shows `discovery.completed = false`. The field is hardcoded to `false` at `content.go:61` and nothing ever updates it. No current code path reads this flag from disk, but it is misleading and will break as soon as any command checks it.

**Found in:** E2E round 4 simulation (alty-cli-3k3).

**Root cause:** `internal/bootstrap/infrastructure/content.go:61` writes `completed = false` at init time. No code path updates it after `DiscoveryCompletedEvent` fires.

## Solution

Add a simple `markDiscoveryCompleted(altoDir string)` helper function in `cmd/alto/commands/guide.go`. Uses `bytes.Replace` on the raw file content to flip `completed = false` → `completed = true`, preserving comments and field ordering (no TOML encode/decode round-trip).

### Why this approach (not port/adapter)

The architect originally proposed a `ConfigUpdater` port interface + `TOMLConfigUpdater` adapter. TL review rejected:
- `arch-go.yml:204-208` forbids bootstrap importing discovery — port placement violates DDD boundary
- Full TOML decode/encode strips comments from the config file (BurntSushi/toml encoder does not preserve comments)
- A port/adapter for a single boolean flip is over-engineered for a Low-severity fix
- All 4 call sites are in `cmd/alto/commands/guide.go` — no cross-context dependency needed

### Implementation

**New helper in `cmd/alto/commands/guide.go`:**
```go
func markDiscoveryCompleted(altoDir string) {
    path := filepath.Join(altoDir, "config.toml")
    data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
    if err != nil {
        return // best-effort
    }
    updated := bytes.Replace(data, []byte("completed = false"), []byte("completed = true"), 1)
    _ = os.WriteFile(path, updated, 0o644)
}
```

**Call sites (4):**
1. `guide.go` after `adapter.Run(ctx)` returns nil (~line 148) — standard guide flow
2. `guide.go` after `adapter.Resume(ctx)` returns nil (~line 256) — `--continue` flow
3. `guide.go` after `handler.Complete()` succeeds in `runGuideAgentIngestFromReader` (~line 406) — `--ingest` flow
4. `guide.go` after `handler.Complete()` succeeds in `runLegacyFlowWithDeps` (~line 513) — `--legacy` flow

### Files to modify

- `cmd/alto/commands/guide.go` — add helper + 4 call sites, add `"bytes"` import

### No changes to

- No new port interfaces
- No new adapter files
- No cross-context imports
- No TOML encoding dependency

## TDD Plan

### RED phase
1. `TestMarkDiscoveryCompleted_FlipsFalseToTrue` — write config with `completed = false`, call helper, assert file contains `completed = true`
2. `TestMarkDiscoveryCompleted_PreservesOtherContent` — config with `[project]` and `[llm]` sections, assert they survive
3. `TestMarkDiscoveryCompleted_IdempotentWhenAlreadyTrue` — already `true`, stays `true`, no duplication
4. `TestMarkDiscoveryCompleted_MissingFile_NoPanic` — non-existent path, returns silently
5. `TestMarkDiscoveryCompleted_NoDiscoverySection_Noop` — config without `completed = false` string, file unchanged

### GREEN phase
- Implement the `bytes.Replace` helper

### REFACTOR phase
- Confirm `gofumpt` formatting and `gci` import ordering
- Verify no lint issues with `_ = os.WriteFile` (errcheck exemption for best-effort)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After `alto guide` completes, `.alto/config.toml` contains `completed = true`
- [ ] After `alto guide --continue` completes, `.alto/config.toml` contains `completed = true`
- [ ] After `alto guide --ingest` completes, `.alto/config.toml` contains `completed = true`
- [ ] After `alto guide --legacy` completes, `.alto/config.toml` contains `completed = true`
- [ ] Comments in config.toml are preserved (no TOML round-trip)
- [ ] Missing or malformed config.toml does not cause panic or non-zero exit
- [ ] `golangci-lint run ./...` clean
- [ ] All existing tests pass
notes: TL review note: `_ = os.WriteFile` in guide.go will fail errcheck (only excluded in test files per .golangci.yml:46-50). Use `//nolint:errcheck // best-effort config update` or log the error as a warning. Do NOT use bare `_ =` in production code.
close_reason: All 5 fixes implemented, code reviewed, quality gates pass (build/vet/lint/test-race). Unstaged, awaiting commit.

title: fix: artifact templates hardcode Python — use detected language from TechStack
description:
## Problem

The `MarkdownArtifactRenderer` has 4 hardcoded Python-specific strings that are emitted regardless of the detected tech stack:

| File | Line | Hardcoded value |
|------|------|-----------------|
| `markdown_artifact_renderer.go` | 86 | `Python 3.12+` |
| `markdown_artifact_renderer.go` | 87 | `uv` |
| `markdown_artifact_renderer.go` | 272 | `Nothing (pure Python)` |
| `markdown_artifact_renderer.go` | 276-289 | `src/domain/`, `src/application/`, `src/infrastructure/` (Python layout) |

**Found in:** E2E round 4 simulation (alty-cli-3k3). kura README specifies Go, detection confirmed Go, but `ARCHITECTURE_alto.md` reads "pure Python" and `PRD_alto.md` reads "Python 3.12+" and "uv".

**Root cause:** The renderer never receives the detected `TechStack`. The data exists — `DiscoveryCompletedEvent.TechStack()` (discovery_events.go:72) returns `*vo.TechStack` and `StackProfile` (stack_profile.go) has `GoModProfile`/`PythonUvProfile` with correct `SourceLayout()` — but there is no thread from detection to rendering.

**Secondary bug:** `ResolveProfile` (stack_resolver.go:7-12) only handles "python" → `PythonUvProfile`. Go projects get `GenericProfile` (nil layout). Must fix to return `GoModProfile` for Go.

## Solution

**Constructor injection** on `MarkdownArtifactRenderer` — inject `StackProfile` at construction time. No port interface changes, no type assertions, no new methods on the port.

### Files to modify

1. **`internal/discovery/infrastructure/markdown_artifact_renderer.go`**
   - Add `profile vo.StackProfile` field to struct
   - Update `NewMarkdownArtifactRenderer` constructor to accept `vo.StackProfile`
   - Add unexported `renderContext` struct with language/packageManager/pureLayerNote/sourceLayout
   - Add `renderContextFromProfile(profile vo.StackProfile) renderContext` helper
   - Replace lines 86-87 with `rc.language` and `rc.packageManager`
   - Replace line 272 with `rc.pureLayerNote`
   - Replace lines 276-289 with `rc.sourceLayout`
   - When profile is nil, fall back to current Python defaults (backward compat)

2. **`internal/discovery/domain/stack_resolver.go`**
   - Add case for "go" → `GoModProfile{}` (currently only handles "python")
   - Use case-insensitive matching

3. **Composition root** (wherever `NewMarkdownArtifactRenderer()` is called)
   - Pass resolved `StackProfile` from TechStack/config

### No changes to

- `internal/discovery/application/ports.go` — `ArtifactRenderer` interface unchanged
- `internal/shared/domain/valueobjects/stack_profile.go` — already correct
- `internal/shared/domain/valueobjects/tech_stack.go` — already correct

### Why constructor injection (not WithStack methods)

The architect originally proposed 3 new `RenderPRDWithStack` methods + type-assertion in the handler. TL review rejected this:
- Type-assertion couples application layer to infrastructure capability (violates DIP)
- 3 new methods is over-engineered for template interpolation
- Constructor injection: renderer owns the interpolation logic (SRP), port interface stays clean (ISP)
- Both `BuildPreview` and `GenerateFromStories` paths are covered automatically (GenerateFromStories has TechStack via `session.TechStack()` at cli_discovery_adapter.go:246)

## TDD Plan

### RED phase
1. `TestRenderPRD_GoProfile_ContainsGoLanguage` — PRD constraints table has "Go" and "go mod", not "Python"/"uv"
2. `TestRenderArchitecture_GoProfile_ContainsPureGo` — layer table reads "pure Go"
3. `TestRenderArchitecture_GoProfile_ContainsGoSourceLayout` — source layout has "internal/" paths, not "src/"
4. `TestRenderPRD_NilProfile_FallsBackToDefaults` — nil profile produces non-empty, non-panic output
5. `TestResolveProfile_Go_ReturnsGoModProfile` — "go" and "Go" both resolve to GoModProfile
6. Negative: assert no output contains "Python" when Go profile is used

### GREEN phase
- Add `profile` field to renderer struct
- Implement `renderContextFromProfile`
- Replace 4 hardcoded string sites with renderContext values
- Fix `ResolveProfile` to handle Go

### REFACTOR phase
- Extract shared `renderContext` helper used by all 3 render methods
- Ensure nil-profile fallback uses PythonUvProfile (preserves current behavior exactly)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No generated markdown contains "Python" when project TechStack is Go
- [ ] PRD constraints table shows detected language and package manager
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE layer table shows "pure Go" and internal/ layout for Go projects
- [ ] `ResolveProfile` returns `GoModProfile` for Go language
- [ ] Nil profile fallback produces current Python defaults (no regression)
- [ ] `ArtifactRenderer` port interface is unchanged
- [ ] All existing tests pass without modification
- [ ] `golangci-lint run ./...` clean

title: fix: clarify --continue flag requires agent-mode session in help text
description:
## Goal / Problem

The --continue flag help text says "Resume a previously interrupted discovery session" without clarifying that only agent-mode sessions are persisted. Users interrupted during interactive sessions try --continue and get "no session to continue. Run \`alto guide\` first" with no explanation. The actual requirement is a session started with --agent.

Discovered during E2E simulation alty-cli-3k3 (round 3, phase 7).

## Background / Context

- Flag description at `guide.go:67`: `"Resume a previously interrupted discovery session"`
- Long help at `guide.go:41`: `"--continue   Resume a previously interrupted storytelling session"`
- Error message at `guide.go:180`: `"no session to continue. Run \`alto guide\` first"`
- `--continue` and `--agent` are mutually exclusive (`guide.go:75-76`) because you cannot start a new agent session and continue an old one simultaneously. But `--continue` IS for resuming sessions created by `--agent`.
- Interactive storytelling flow does NOT persist sessions. Only `runGuideAgent` creates `.alto/discovery_session.json`.
- Pattern reference: `--ingest` flag at `guide.go:69` correctly states its constraint inline: "requires --agent".

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Discovery |
| Layer | CLI Adapter (flag metadata only) |

## Design

Three string changes in `cmd/alto/commands/guide.go`:

1. **Flag description (line 67):**
   - Before: `"Resume a previously interrupted discovery session"`
   - After: `"Resume a previously interrupted agent-mode session (requires prior \`alto guide --agent\` run)"`

2. **Long help block (line 41):**
   - Before: `--continue   Resume a previously interrupted storytelling session`
   - After: `--continue   Resume a previously interrupted agent-mode session (session must have been started with --agent)`

3. **Error message (line 180):**
   - Before: `"no session to continue. Run \`alto guide\` first"`
   - After: `"no session to continue: --continue requires a session started with \`alto guide --agent\`; interactive sessions are not persisted"`

## TDD Workflow

### RED
Add `TestGuideCmd_ContinueFlagUsage_MentionsAgentMode` to `cmd/alto/commands/`:
- Build command via NewGuideCmd(nil)
- Lookup "continue" flag
- Assert flag.Usage contains "agent"

### GREEN
Apply the three string changes.

### REFACTOR
Run quality gates.

## Steps

1. Update flag description at line 67
2. Update Long help at line 41
3. Update error message at line 180
4. Add flag description test
5. Run quality gates

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `alto guide --help` output for --continue mentions agent-mode requirement
- [ ] `alto guide --continue` with no session prints updated error naming --agent
- [ ] New test asserts flag description contains "agent"
- [ ] All quality gates pass

## Edge Cases

| Case | Expected |
|------|----------|
| No session file | Updated error names --agent as prerequisite |
| Help flag | --continue line names agent-mode requirement |

## Quality Gates

- [ ] `go build ./...` zero errors
- [ ] `go vet ./...` zero errors
- [ ] `golangci-lint run ./...` zero issues
- [ ] `go test ./... -race` all pass

- [x] Line 180: error message confirmed

- No functional risk — string-only change
- If interactive session persistence is added later, these strings need updating again

title: Document --force-branch flag in help output
description:
## Goal / Problem

\`alty init --existing\` fails with \"branch alty/init already exists, delete it first or use --force-branch to override\" on second run. The \`--force-branch\` flag is mentioned in the error but does not exist as a Cobra flag and has no implementation.

## Background / Context

- Issue 8 from .notes/issues.md
- Error at \`internal/rescue/application/rescue_handler.go:77\`

1. \`ValidatePreconditions\` detects branch exists

3. Continue with \`CreateBranch\` as normal

\`\`\`go
TestValidatePreconditions_WhenBranchExistsAndForceTrue_ExpectDeleteAndContinue
TestValidatePreconditions_WhenBranchExistsAndForceFalse_ExpectError
TestValidatePreconditions_WhenBranchNotExistsAndForceTrue_ExpectNoDelete
TestRescue_WhenForceBranch_ExpectDeleteBeforeCreate

### GREEN Phase

4. Add \`--force-branch\` flag to Cobra command in \`cmd/alty/commands/init.go:37-39\`

## Edge Cases

title: Spike: Static site generator for project docs
description:
## Research Question

What is the best static site generator for alty's user-facing documentation, given that:
1. Source content is existing Markdown files in `docs/` (PRD.md, DDD.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, etc.)
2. The project is a Go repo — we don't want `package.json`, `node_modules`, etc. in the repo root
3. We want beautiful output with layouts, CSS, and templates (not just rendered markdown)
4. If JS-based (Astro, etc.), all tooling must live in a `website/` subdirectory — isolated from the Go project
5. If Go-based (Hugo, etc.), it should support modern themes and custom layouts without heavy templating

Specific questions:
- Can Astro live entirely in `website/` and reference `../docs/*.md` as content sources?
- Does Hugo offer comparable visual quality to Astro for documentation sites?
- Are there Go-native options (Hugo, Docusaurus alternatives) that avoid JS entirely?
- What's the maintenance burden of each option (updates, theme management, build pipeline)?
- Can we automate doc freshness metadata (`last_reviewed`, owners) from `.alty/maintenance/doc-registry.toml` into the site?

## Timebox

**Timebox:** 4 hours

## Background / Context

- alty generates project docs (PRD.md, DDD.md, ARCHITECTURE.md) during `alty init`
- These docs live in `docs/` and are maintained via `alty doc-health` and `alty doc-review`
- Doc metadata (owners, review cadence) is tracked in `.alty/maintenance/doc-registry.toml`
- We need user-facing documentation for alty itself (usage guide, getting started, architecture overview)
- The site should be deployable as static HTML (no server required)
- The Go project root must stay clean — no JS config files at root level

## Investigation Approach

1. **Astro** — Can it live in `website/` and pull content from `../docs/`? Evaluate content collections, MDX support, Starlight theme (purpose-built for docs). Check if Astro's content layer can reference files outside its own directory.

2. **Hugo** — Go-native SSG. Evaluate modern themes (Doks, Docsy, Book). Check if it can use `docs/` as content source without duplicating files. Assess template customization effort vs Astro components.

3. **MkDocs (Material)** — Python-based, popular for project docs. Beautiful out of the box with Material theme. Check if it can live in `website/` with `docs_dir: ../docs`. Lightweight, no JS build step.

4. **mdBook** — Rust-based, used by Rust ecosystem. Minimal config, clean output. May be too simple for our needs.

5. **Docusaurus** — React-based, similar to Astro but heavier. Evaluate only if Astro has showstopper limitations.

## Research Guidelines for AI Agents

```markdown
Please investigate and provide a clear research report with:

1. **Use Context7** for library/package documentation lookup
2. **Web search** for recent information (use current year in queries, filter out 2025)
3. **Structured findings** with pros/cons table for each option
4. **Clear recommendation** with justification
5. **Follow-up tasks** if implementation is needed
6. **PoC verification** — for the top 2 candidates, verify the `website/` isolation claim by checking official docs for content directory configuration
```

## Expected Deliverables

- [ ] Research report created at `docs/research/20260314_static_site_generator.md`
- [ ] Comparison table of options (Astro, Hugo, MkDocs, mdBook)
- [ ] Verification that top candidate can reference `../docs/` from `website/` subdirectory
- [ ] Recommendation with justification
- [ ] Follow-up tickets created for implementation (if applicable)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Research question(s) answered
- [ ] Findings documented at `docs/research/20260314_static_site_generator.md`
- [ ] Recommendation provided with clear justification
- [ ] Top candidate verified for `website/` isolation (not just claimed)
- [ ] Follow-up tickets created (if implementation needed)
- [ ] Timebox respected (or extended with justification)
notes:
## Additional Context (2026-03-14)

This site will be the public-facing **alty.ai** website — not just internal docs. Design quality must be high:
- Landing page with product positioning
- Beautiful documentation pages with navigation, search, code blocks
- Professional visual design (not just a docs theme)
- Must represent the product to potential users

This shifts the evaluation criteria: pure docs tools (MkDocs, mdBook) may be too limited. Need a tool that supports both marketing pages AND documentation from the same codebase.
close_reason: research complete: Astro + Starlight recommended, report at docs/research/20260314_static_site_generator.md

title: Add --no-tui flag to alty guide command
description:
## Goal / Problem

Allow users to disable TUI prompts via `--no-tui` flag, falling back to plain stdin/stdout. Required for accessibility (screen readers) and CI/scripting.

## Background / Context

- Default: `HuhPrompter` with TUI (arrow keys, styled output)
- Fallback: `StdinPrompter` with plain text I/O
- Flag enables: accessibility mode, CI pipelines, piped input
- **Spike finding:** huh has `WithAccessible(true)` but separate adapter is cleaner (see `docs/research/20260311_cli_prompt_library.md`)
- **Pattern reference:** `cmd/alty/guide.go`

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | Discovery (CLI command) |
| Layer | Composition (DI wiring) |

## Design

### CLI Flag

```go
// cmd/alty/guide.go
var guideCmd = &cobra.Command{
    Use:   "guide",
    Short: "Guided DDD discovery",
    RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
        noTUI, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("no-tui")
        
        var prompter application.Prompter
        if noTUI {
            prompter = infrastructure.NewStdinPrompter(os.Stdin, os.Stdout)
        } else {
            prompter = infrastructure.NewHuhPrompter()
        }
        
        adapter := infrastructure.NewCLIDiscoveryAdapter(handler, prompter)
        return adapter.Run(cmd.Context())
    },
}

func init() {
    guideCmd.Flags().Bool("no-tui", false, "Disable TUI, use plain stdin/stdout")
}
```

### Environment Variable (optional)

```go
// Also respect ALTY_NO_TUI=1 for CI environments
if os.Getenv("ALTY_NO_TUI") == "1" {
    noTUI = true
}
```

## Steps

1. Add `--no-tui` flag to `guide.go`
2. Wire flag to adapter selection in composition
3. Add `ALTY_NO_TUI` environment variable support
4. Update help text to document accessibility use case
5. Add integration test for `--no-tui` mode

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `alty guide --no-tui` uses `StdinPrompter`
- [ ] `ALTY_NO_TUI=1 alty guide` uses `StdinPrompter`
- [ ] Default (no flag) uses `HuhPrompter` with TUI
- [ ] Help text documents accessibility use case
- [ ] Integration test verifies flag wiring

## Dependencies

- Depends on: stdin fallback adapter ticket

## Quality Gates

```bash
golangci-lint run ./...
go test ./cmd/alty/... -race
```
close_reason: Added --no-tui flag and ALTY_NO_TUI env var support to alty guide command, selects StdinPrompter for accessibility/CI mode

design:
### Exact Implementation

**File:** `internal/integration/config_generation_test.go` (new file)

**Test Structure:**

```go
package integration_test

import (
	"context"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/alty-cli/alty/internal/composition"
	"github.com/alty-cli/alty/internal/shared/domain/ddd"
	vo "github.com/alty-cli/alty/internal/shared/domain/valueobjects"
	"github.com/alty-cli/alty/internal/tooltranslation/domain"
)

func TestFullConfigGenerationFlow_ClaudeCode(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	
	// Setup temp directory
	tmpDir := t.TempDir()
	
	// Create domain model (simulates completed discovery)
	model := createTestModel(t)
	profile := vo.PythonUvProfile{}
	
	// Generate configs via ClaudeCodeAdapter
	adapter := domain.NewClaudeCodeAdapter()
	sections := adapter.Translate(model, profile)
	
	// Write files using real FileWriter
	writer := composition.NewFilesystemFileWriter()
	for _, section := range sections {
		fullPath := filepath.Join(tmpDir, section.FilePath())
		require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(fullPath), 0755))
		require.NoError(t, writer.WriteFile(context.Background(), fullPath, section.Content()))
	}
	
	// Verify expected files exist
	expectedFiles := []string{
		".claude/CLAUDE.md",
		".claude/memory/MEMORY.md",
		".claude/agents/developer.md",
		".claude/agents/tech-lead.md",
		".claude/agents/qa-engineer.md",
		".claude/agents/researcher.md",
	}
	for _, f := range expectedFiles {
		path := filepath.Join(tmpDir, f)
		assert.FileExists(t, path, "missing %s", f)
	}
	
	// Verify content correctness
	devContent, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(tmpDir, ".claude/agents/developer.md"))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Contains(t, string(devContent), "name: developer")
	assert.Contains(t, string(devContent), "Bounded Contexts")
}
```

### Test Scenarios

| Test | What it validates |
|------|-------------------|
| `TestFullConfigGenerationFlow_ClaudeCode` | 6 files created with correct content |
| `TestFullConfigGenerationFlow_Cursor` | AGENTS.md + 2 .mdc files (3 total with domain-expert) |
| `TestFullConfigGenerationFlow_RooCode` | AGENTS.md + .roomodes + rules (3 files) |
| `TestFullConfigGenerationFlow_AllTools` | All 4 adapters produce expected file counts |
| `TestConfigGeneration_ConflictRename` | Pre-existing file → _alty suffix |
| `TestConfigGeneration_GlobalConflict` | Reports conflict when global config exists |

### File Count Expectations

| Tool | Files |
|------|-------|
| Claude Code | 6 (CLAUDE.md, MEMORY.md, 4 personas) |
| Cursor | 3 (AGENTS.md, project-conventions.mdc, domain-expert.mdc) |
| Roo Code | 3 (AGENTS.md, .roomodes, project-conventions.md) |
| OpenCode | 3 (AGENTS.md, opencode.json, project-conventions.md) |

### Helper Functions

```go
func createTestModel(t *testing.T) *ddd.DomainModel {
	t.Helper()
	m := ddd.NewDomainModel("test-integration")
	// Add domain story, bounded context, ubiquitous language term
	require.NoError(t, m.AddDomainStory(vo.NewDomainStory(
		"Test flow", []string{"User"}, "User starts", []string{"User manages Orders"}, nil,
	)))
	require.NoError(t, m.AddTerm("Orders", "Order domain", "Orders", nil))
	require.NoError(t, m.AddBoundedContext(vo.NewDomainBoundedContext(
		"Orders", "Manages orders", nil, nil, "",
	)))
	require.NoError(t, m.ClassifySubdomain("Orders", vo.SubdomainCore, ""))
	return m
}
```

title: test: fix time-boundary flake in TestCreateDocStatus
description:
## Goal / Problem

Three subtests in TestCreateDocStatus flake intermittently because "today" is derived from time.Now() at test execution time. The test anchors today with time.Now().Truncate(24*time.Hour) at doc_health_test.go:114, then computes reviewed dates by subtracting days. At UTC midnight boundaries, this produces off-by-one results. The fix is test-only: replace the wall-clock anchor with a fixed time.Date(2025, 1, 15, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC).

Discovered during E2E simulation alty-cli-3k3 round 3, quality gates.

## Background / Context

- `doc_health_test.go:114`: `today := time.Now().Truncate(24 * time.Hour)` — wall clock anchor
- `CreateDocStatus` at `doc_health.go:148` accepts `today *time.Time`; when non-nil, uses caller's value (line 181)
- All six subtests pass `&today` — the production fallback is never exercised
- The flake is solely in the test setup, not in production code
- `TestDocReviewResult` at line 245 also uses `time.Now()` but only asserts identity, not day arithmetic — out of scope

## DDD Alignment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Bounded Context | dochealth |
| Layer | Domain (test file only) |

## Design

Single-line change in `internal/dochealth/domain/doc_health_test.go` at line 114:

Before:
```go
today := time.Now().Truncate(24 * time.Hour)
```

After:
```go
// Fixed anchor: noon UTC on a non-DST, non-boundary date.
// Avoids off-by-one flakes when the test runs near UTC midnight.
today := time.Date(2025, 1, 15, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
```

No production code changes. No other test changes needed.

## TDD Workflow

### RED
The flake already exists. Reproduce with: `for i in $(seq 1 100); do go test ./internal/dochealth/domain/... -run TestCreateDocStatus -count=1 -race; done`

### GREEN
Apply the fixed anchor. All subtests become deterministic.

### REFACTOR
Verify `TestDocReviewResult` is unaffected. Run quality gates.

## Steps

1. Replace time.Now() with fixed date at doc_health_test.go:114
2. Run `go test ./internal/dochealth/domain/... -run TestCreateDocStatus -count=50 -race`
3. Run full quality gates

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `today` uses `time.Date(2025, 1, 15, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)` — no time.Now() in TestCreateDocStatus
- [ ] `-count=50 -race` produces zero failures
- [ ] No production code modified
- [ ] TestDocReviewResult unchanged and passing
- [ ] All quality gates pass

## Edge Cases

All existing subtests cover boundary cases (0, 10, 30, 31, 45 days). Fixed anchor makes them deterministic.

## Quality Gates

- [ ] `go build ./...` zero errors
- [ ] `go vet ./...` zero errors
- [ ] `golangci-lint run ./...` zero issues
- [ ] `go test ./... -race` all pass
- [ ] `go test ./internal/dochealth/domain/... -run TestCreateDocStatus -count=50 -race` zero failures

## Pre-Implementation Validation

- [x] Line 114 confirmed: `time.Now().Truncate(24 * time.Hour)`
- [x] All subtests pass `&today` to CreateDocStatus
- [x] CreateDocStatus uses caller's today when non-nil (line 180-181)
- [x] Fixed anchor produces exact integer arithmetic for all N used in subtests

## Risks / Dependencies

- No runtime risk — test-only change
- No dependencies on other tickets
